◆ addDefaultConstructorIfRequired()

bool SageInterface::addDefaultConstructorIfRequired ( SgClassType * classType,
int physical_file_id )

Adds a default constructor to a class if one is required but not present.

This function examines a class type to determine whether it needs an explicit default constructor. A default constructor is required when a class has at least one user-defined constructor (which prevents the compiler from generating a default constructor automatically) but does not have a default constructor (a constructor with no parameters).

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Retrieves the class definition from the provided class type.
  2. Iterates through all member declarations to find constructors.
  3. For each constructor found, checks if it is a default constructor (zero parameters).
  4. If at least one constructor exists but no default constructor is found, a new default constructor is built using SageBuilder::buildDefaultConstructor and prepended to the class definition.
  5. The newly created constructor is marked for unparsing using the specified physical file ID.

If no constructors are found in the class, the function assumes the compiler will generate a default constructor automatically and takes no action.

Parameters
classTypePointer to the SgClassType representing the class to be examined and potentially modified. Must not be NULL.
physical_file_idThe physical file identifier used to mark the generated constructor for unparsing. This is particularly relevant when header file unparsing is active. Defaults to Sg_File_Info::TRANSFORMATION_FILE_ID.
Returns
True if a default constructor was added to the class, false otherwise. Returns false if the class already has a default constructor, has no constructors at all, or if no modification was necessary.
Precondition
classType must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgClassType.
The class type must have an associated defining class declaration with a valid definition.
Postcondition
If a default constructor was added, it will be the first member in the class definition.
The added constructor will have public access modifier.
The added constructor and its subtree will be marked for unparsing with the specified physical_file_id.
Note
This function is useful for source-to-source transformations where explicit default constructors may be needed for code that will be compiled separately from its original context.
The generated default constructor is created with an empty body using SageBuilder::buildDefaultConstructor.
Debug output can be enabled by setting DEBUG_ADD_DEFAULT_CONSTRUCTOR to a non-zero value.
Warning
This function modifies the AST by adding a new member function declaration to the class definition. Ensure that subsequent processing accounts for this modification.

◆ addMangledNameToCache()

std::string SageInterface::addMangledNameToCache ( SgNode * astNode,
const std::string & oldMangledName )

Adds a mangled name to the global mangled name cache, optionally shortening long names.

This function stores a mangled name associated with an AST node in a global cache for later retrieval. When the mangled name exceeds 40 characters and short name generation is enabled, the function computes a shortened version using SHA-256 hashing. The hash is converted to a 64-bit value and then encoded in base-62 format, surrounded by 'L' and 'R' delimiters.

The shortening mechanism helps reduce memory usage and improves performance when dealing with complex C++ mangled names that can become extremely long, particularly for template-heavy code. A separate cache maps original long mangled names to their computed hash values to ensure consistency when the same long name is encountered multiple times.

When short name generation is disabled via SgProject::get_mangled_noshortname(), the original mangled name is used directly. A periodic warning is emitted in this mode to alert users that special characters in operator names may cause issues with certain test cases.

Debug modes are available via preprocessor macros to check for hash collisions and trace the caching process.

Parameters
astNodePointer to the AST node for which the mangled name is being cached. Must not be NULL. The node serves as the key in the mangled name cache.
oldMangledNameThe original mangled name string to be cached. If longer than 40 characters and short names are enabled, this will be hashed and shortened before storage.
Returns
The mangled name that was actually stored in the cache. This may be the original name or a shortened base-62 encoded version depending on the name length and configuration settings.
Warning
When using longer forms of mangled names (short names disabled), function names containing embedded special characters such as ampersand may cause failures. For example, conversion operators like "operator T&() const;" may fail because the special character remains in the mangled name.
Adding IR nodes to the cache before their scope is properly set may be premature and could lead to issues. Debug builds will emit warnings in such cases.
Precondition
astNode must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgNode.
The global mangled name map must be properly initialized.
Postcondition
The astNode and its associated mangled name are inserted into the global mangled name cache.
If a new shortened name was generated, the mapping from oldMangledName to its hash value is stored in the short mangled name cache.
Note
The shortened name format is 'L' followed by base-62 encoded 64-bit hash followed by 'R', for example "L1a2B3c4D5eR".
The hashing algorithm uses SHA-256 via Combinatorics::HasherSha256Builtin, then extracts a 64-bit value from the digest.
Debug output can be enabled by defining DEBUG_SAGE_INTERFACE_ADD_MANGLED_TO_CACHE.
Hash collision detection can be enabled by defining DEBUG_MANGLED_SHORTNAME.

◆ addStepToLoopBody()

void SageInterface::addStepToLoopBody ( SgScopeStatement * loopStmt,
SgStatement * step )

Adds a step statement to the end of a loop body while preserving continue statement semantics.

This function modifies a loop by inserting a step statement at the end of its body. To ensure that continue statements within the original loop body still execute the step statement before the next iteration, all continue statements are transformed into goto statements that jump to a newly created label placed just before the step.

The transformation creates a new basic block containing:

  1. The original loop body
  2. A generated label statement (with a unique name of the form "rose_label__N")
  3. The provided step statement

This approach ensures that both normal execution flow and continue statements will execute the step statement before proceeding to the next loop iteration. The algorithm uses a global counter (gensym_counter) to generate unique label names.

Parameters
loopStmtPointer to the loop statement (such as while, for, or do-while) whose body will be modified. Must be a valid loop statement.
stepPointer to the statement to be appended as the step operation at the end of the loop body. This statement will be executed at the end of each iteration.
Warning
This function modifies the AST in place. The original loop body structure is altered and continue statements are replaced with goto statements.
The function relies on a global counter (gensym_counter) for generating unique label names, which may cause issues in multi-threaded contexts.
Precondition
loopStmt must be a valid pointer to a loop statement (SgWhileStmt, SgForStatement, or SgDoWhileStmt).
step must be a valid pointer to a statement that can be legally placed in the loop body.
The loop must be contained within a procedure or function scope.
Postcondition
The loop body is replaced with a new basic block containing the original body, a label statement, and the step statement.
All continue statements in the original body are converted to goto statements targeting the newly created label.
Note
The generated label name follows the pattern "rose_label__N" where N is an incrementing counter value.
The label statement is created with an empty basic block as its scope.

◆ addTextForUnparser()

void SageInterface::addTextForUnparser ( SgNode * astNode,
string s,
AstUnparseAttribute::RelativePositionType inputlocation )

Adds custom text to an AST node for inclusion during unparsing.

This function attaches a string of text to a specified AST node that will be included when the AST is unparsed back to source code. The text can be positioned relative to the node based on the specified location parameter. The function uses the AstUnparseAttribute mechanism to store the text strings associated with nodes.

If the node already has an AstUnparseAttribute attached, the new string is added to the existing attribute with the specified relative position. If no attribute exists, a new AstUnparseAttribute is created with the given string and position, then attached to the node.

This mechanism is not intended for use with SgType nodes because type nodes are shared across the AST, and adding unparse text to them would affect all locations where the type is referenced.

Parameters
astNodeThe AST node to which the text should be attached. Must not be an SgType node, as type nodes are shared and cannot have node-specific unparse text.
sThe string of text to be added for unparsing. This text will appear in the output when the AST is unparsed.
inputlocationSpecifies the relative position where the text should appear with respect to the AST node during unparsing. This determines whether the text appears before, after, or in place of the node's normal output.
Warning
This function will abort the program if called with an SgType node, as the text attachment mechanism is not designed for shared type nodes.
Precondition
astNode must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgNode.
astNode must not be an SgType node or any of its derived types.
Postcondition
The specified string is attached to astNode via an AstUnparseAttribute and will be included when the node is unparsed.
If an AstUnparseAttribute already existed on the node, the string is appended to it; otherwise, a new attribute is created and attached.
Note
The inputlocation parameter is significant even when creating a new attribute, as it specifies the position relative to the statement rather than relative to other AstUnparseAttribute objects.

◆ addVarRefExpFromArrayDimInfo()

void SageInterface::addVarRefExpFromArrayDimInfo ( SgNode * astNode,
Rose_STL_Container< SgNode * > & NodeList_t )

Collects variable references from array dimension information within a subtree.

This function traverses the AST subtree rooted at the given node to find all SgPntrArrRefExp (pointer array reference expression) nodes. For each array reference expression found, it examines the left-hand side operand to identify variable references. If any of these variables have an array type with associated dimension information, the function extracts all SgVarRefExp nodes from that dimension information and adds them to the output container.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Query the subtree for all SgPntrArrRefExp nodes
  2. For each array reference, query its left-hand side for SgVarRefExp nodes
  3. For each variable reference, check if it refers to an array with dimension info
  4. If dimension info exists, extract all variable references from it and add to the result

This is useful for identifying variables that are used in array dimension specifications, which may be needed for dependency analysis or variable liveness analysis in the context of array operations.

Parameters
astNodeThe root node of the AST subtree to search. Must not be null.
NodeList_tA reference to a container that will be populated with SgVarRefExp nodes found in array dimension information. The container is not cleared before adding new elements; results are appended.
Precondition
astNode must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgNode.
NodeList_t should be a valid container, possibly empty or containing existing elements.
Postcondition
NodeList_t contains all SgVarRefExp nodes from array dimension information found within the subtree, appended to any existing contents.
Note
This function uses NodeQuery::querySubTree to perform AST traversal.
Only arrays with explicit dimension information (get_dim_info() returns non-null) contribute variable references to the output.
The function performs multiple levels of nested queries, which may have performance implications for large AST subtrees.
Warning
The function assumes all intermediate pointers (symbols, declarations, types) are valid and will trigger assertions if any are null.

◆ annotateExpressionsWithUniqueNames()

void SageInterface::annotateExpressionsWithUniqueNames ( SgProject * project)

Generate unique names for expressions and attach the names as persistent attributes.

This function traverses all nodes in the given ROSE project's abstract syntax tree (AST) and annotates each expression node with a unique name attribute. The traversal is performed using a simple AST processing visitor pattern. For each SgExpression node encountered, a unique name is generated by combining the result of generateUniqueName() with the expression's class name, separated by a hyphen. This unique name is then stored as a UniqueNameAttribute and attached to the expression node with the key "UniqueNameAttribute".

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Define an inner visitor class that inherits from AstSimpleProcessing
  2. In the visit method, check if the current node is an SgExpression
  3. If so, generate a unique name string and create a UniqueNameAttribute object
  4. Attach the attribute to the expression node using addNewAttribute
  5. Traverse the entire project AST in preorder using the visitor
Parameters
projectPointer to the SgProject representing the ROSE project to be annotated. This project contains the AST that will be traversed.
Precondition
The project parameter must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SgProject.
The AST within the project should be fully constructed before calling this function.
Postcondition
All SgExpression nodes in the project's AST will have a "UniqueNameAttribute" attached containing a unique identifier string.
The unique name format for each expression is: unique_name_base + "-" + class_name.
Note
The function uses a local visitor class (visitorTraversal) that inherits from AstSimpleProcessing to perform the AST traversal.
The traversal uses the traverse() method rather than traverseInputFiles() to process the entire project.
Each unique name attribute is dynamically allocated and ownership is transferred to the expression node.
Warning
The function does not check if a "UniqueNameAttribute" already exists on expression nodes before adding a new one, which could lead to attribute conflicts if called multiple times on the same project.

◆ appendArg()

SgVariableSymbol * SageInterface::appendArg ( SgFunctionParameterList * paraList,
SgInitializedName * initName )

Appends a new argument to the end of a function parameter list.

This function adds a new parameter to a function's parameter list by appending it at the end of the existing parameters. It serves as a convenience wrapper around the more general addArg function, specifically configured for append operations. The function delegates to addArg with the prepend flag set to false, ensuring the new parameter is placed after all existing parameters.

Parameters
paraListPointer to the SgFunctionParameterList to which the new argument will be appended. Must not be null.
initNamePointer to the SgInitializedName representing the new parameter to be added to the parameter list. Must not be null.
Returns
Pointer to the SgVariableSymbol associated with the newly appended parameter, or null if the operation fails.
Precondition
paraList must be a valid, non-null pointer to an existing SgFunctionParameterList.
initName must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgInitializedName object.
Postcondition
The parameter represented by initName is appended to the end of paraList.
A corresponding variable symbol is created and registered in the appropriate symbol table.
Note
This function is equivalent to calling addArg(paraList, initName, false).
See also
SageInterface::addArg
SageInterface::prependArg

◆ appendExpression()

void SageInterface::appendExpression ( SgExprListExp * expList,
SgExpression * exp )

Appends an expression to an expression list and updates the AST parent relationship.

This function adds a given expression node to the end of an expression list within the ROSE AST (Abstract Syntax Tree). It performs two operations: first, it appends the expression to the expression list using the internal append_expression method, and second, it establishes the proper parent-child relationship by setting the expression list as the parent of the appended expression. This ensures the AST maintains consistent structural integrity.

Parameters
expListPointer to the expression list (SgExprListExp) to which the expression will be appended. Must not be NULL.
expPointer to the expression (SgExpression) to be appended to the list. Must not be NULL.
Precondition
expList is a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgExprListExp node.
exp is a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgExpression node.
Postcondition
The expression exp is appended to the end of expList.
The parent of exp is set to expList, maintaining proper AST structure.
Note
This function modifies both the expression list and the expression node by updating their internal relationships.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate input parameters, which will terminate the program if assertions fail in debug builds.
Warning
Passing NULL pointers for either parameter will trigger an assertion failure and program termination.
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the expression is not already attached to another parent node, as this could lead to inconsistent AST state.

◆ appendExpressionList()

void SageInterface::appendExpressionList ( SgExprListExp * expList,
const std::vector< SgExpression * > & exp )

Appends a vector of expressions to an existing expression list.

This function iterates through a vector of SgExpression pointers and appends each expression to the specified SgExprListExp node. It serves as a convenience wrapper that allows batch appending of multiple expressions in a single call by internally invoking appendExpression for each element in the vector.

Parameters
expListPointer to the SgExprListExp node to which expressions will be appended. This must be a valid, non-null expression list node.
expA constant reference to a vector of SgExpression pointers that will be appended to the expression list. The expressions are appended in the order they appear in the vector.
Precondition
expList must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExprListExp node.
All SgExpression pointers in the exp vector should be valid expressions suitable for inclusion in the expression list.
Postcondition
All expressions from the input vector have been appended to expList in order, with their parent pointers set appropriately.
The size of expList is increased by the number of elements in exp.
Note
This function does not perform null checks on individual expression pointers within the vector. Callers should ensure all pointers are valid.
The function modifies the AST by adding new child nodes to expList.
Warning
If expList is null, the behavior depends on the implementation of the underlying appendExpression function.

◆ appendStatement() [1/2]

void SageInterface::appendStatement ( SgStatement * stmt,
SgForInitStatement * for_init_stmt )

Appends a statement to the end of an SgForInitStatement.

This function appends a given statement to the initialization statement list of a for-loop's initialization clause (SgForInitStatement). Before appending, the function updates internal data structures to handle cases where the statement is being moved from another location. This ensures that any macro expansions associated with the statement or the target for-init statement are properly marked as transformations.

The function performs the following steps:

  1. Validates that both the statement and for-init statement are non-null.
  2. Calls resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement on the statement being appended to update internal tracking for moved statements and macro expansions.
  3. Calls resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement on the for-init statement to ensure statements adjacent to the insertion point are checked for macro expansion associations.
  4. Appends the statement to the for-init statement's initialization list.
Parameters
stmtPointer to the SgStatement to be appended to the for-loop initialization statement. Must not be NULL.
for_init_stmtPointer to the SgForInitStatement where the statement will be appended. Must not be NULL.
Warning
This function modifies the AST structure. Ensure that the statement being appended is not already attached to another parent node, or detach it first to avoid inconsistent AST state.
Precondition
stmt is not NULL.
for_init_stmt is not NULL.
stmt is a valid statement that can be placed in a for-loop initialization.
Postcondition
stmt is appended to the end of for_init_stmt's initialization statement list.
Internal maps tracking macro expansions are updated appropriately for both the statement and the for-init statement.
Note
This function is part of the SageInterface namespace which provides utility functions for manipulating the ROSE AST.
The function handles macro expansion tracking to ensure that moved statements associated with macros are properly marked as transformations.

◆ appendStatement() [2/2]

void SageInterface::appendStatement ( SgStatement * stmt,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Appends a statement to the end of a specified scope.

This function appends a given statement to the end of a scope statement in the ROSE AST (Abstract Syntax Tree). If no scope is provided, the function uses the top of the scope stack maintained by SageBuilder as the target scope.

The function performs several important operations before and after appending:

  • Validates that both the statement and scope are non-null
  • Handles special cases for class declarations and enum declarations that are non-autonomous (embedded within other declarations like typedefs)
  • Checks for duplicate statements already existing in the scope to prevent redundant insertions, particularly relevant for template instantiations
  • Calls fixStatement() to perform necessary statement fixup before insertion
  • Updates the parent pointer of the statement to point to the scope
  • Updates defining and non-defining declaration links for function declarations when not in frontend construction mode

The function includes logic to skip adding statements in certain cases:

  • Non-autonomous class declarations (those embedded in other constructs)
  • Non-autonomous enum declarations
  • Statements that already exist in the target scope (to avoid duplicates)
Parameters
stmtPointer to the SgStatement to be appended to the scope. Must not be NULL. The statement will have its parent pointer set to the scope after insertion.
scopePointer to the SgScopeStatement where the statement should be appended. If NULL, the function will use SageBuilder::topScopeStack() as the default scope.
Precondition
The stmt parameter must point to a valid SgStatement object.
If scope is NULL, there must be a valid scope on the SageBuilder scope stack.
Postcondition
The statement is appended to the scope (unless it is a non-autonomous declaration or already exists in the scope).
The statement's parent pointer is set to the scope.
For function declarations, the defining and non-defining declaration links are updated (except during frontend construction mode).
Note
It is legal to append the first and only statement in a scope.
For non-autonomous declarations (such as class or enum declarations embedded within typedefs), the statement will not be added to the scope to avoid duplicate entries.
Template instantiation declarations that have already been added to a scope will be silently skipped to prevent duplicates.
The function performs statement fixup via fixStatement() before the actual insertion into the scope.
Warning
If moving a statement from one scope to another, the caller should explicitly call removeStatement() before calling appendStatement(), as this function does not automatically remove the statement from its original scope.

◆ appendStatementList()

void SageInterface::appendStatementList ( const std::vector< SgStatement * > & stmts,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Appends a list of statements to a specified scope.

This function iterates through a vector of SgStatement pointers and appends each statement to the given scope. The actual insertion logic, including validation of parent pointers and proper placement within the scope, is delegated to the appendStatement function for each individual statement.

The function processes statements in order from the beginning to the end of the vector, maintaining their relative ordering when added to the scope.

Parameters
stmtsA constant reference to a vector of SgStatement pointers to be appended to the scope. Each statement in the vector will be processed and added to the target scope sequentially.
scopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement where the statements should be appended. This defines the target scope that will contain the statements after the operation completes.
Precondition
The scope parameter should point to a valid SgScopeStatement object.
Each element in the stmts vector should be a valid SgStatement pointer.
Postcondition
All statements from the stmts vector have been appended to the specified scope in their original order.
The parent pointers of the appended statements are set appropriately by the underlying appendStatement function.
Note
This function delegates parent pointer validation and other insertion logic to the appendStatement function, which handles individual statement insertion details.
Debug output code exists in the implementation but is conditionally compiled out. When enabled via ROSE_DEBUG_NEW_EDG_ROSE_CONNECTION, it provides diagnostic information about each statement being processed.
See also
appendStatement

◆ appendStatementWithDependentDeclaration()

void SageInterface::appendStatementWithDependentDeclaration ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl,
SgGlobal * scope,
SgStatement * original_statement,
bool excludeHeaderFiles )

Appends a declaration statement along with its dependent declarations to a global scope.

This function supports outlining of functions into separate files by ensuring that all required dependent declarations are also copied and inserted into the target scope. The function performs the following major operations:

  1. Validates that the input declaration is consistent in its representation across files, ensuring the first non-defining declaration exists and is in the same source file.
  2. Collects all declarations that the input declaration depends upon from the original file.
  3. Generates copies of all dependent declarations and inserts them into the target scope ahead of the input declaration.
  4. Builds a replacement map to track mappings between original AST nodes and their copies, particularly for symbols that need to be updated.
  5. Collects required C preprocessor directives from the original source file and attaches them to the first statement in the outlined file, avoiding redundant directives.
  6. Performs edge pointer replacement across the outlined file to update references from old AST nodes to their new copies using the replacement map.
  7. Adds comment markers to identify the outlined function and its dependent declarations in the generated code.

This function is primarily used by the AST outlining infrastructure when extracting functions into separate compilation units.

Parameters
declThe declaration statement to be appended to the target scope. Must be a valid declaration with a non-null first non-defining declaration. Typically this is an SgFunctionDeclaration representing the outlined function.
scopeThe global scope (SgGlobal) where the declaration and its dependencies will be inserted. This is typically the global scope of the separate outlined file.
original_statementThe original statement from which to collect preprocessing directives and determine the source file context.
excludeHeaderFilesIf true, include directives for header files will not be copied to the outlined file. This can simplify the output for external tools but may leave unsatisfied dependent declarations.
Warning
The function assumes that the input declaration has already been properly set up with its scope pointing to the target global scope before this function is called.
Support for dependent member function declarations and SgTemplateInstantiationDecl as dependent declarations is not implemented and will cause an abort.
When excludeHeaderFiles is true, there may be remaining unsatisfied dependent declarations that were defined in header files.
A warning message is printed indicating that the symbol lookup function being used may not be the correct one for this context.
Precondition
decl must not be NULL.
decl->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() must not be NULL.
The source file of decl must match the source file of its first non-defining declaration.
decl->get_scope() must equal the provided scope parameter.
decl must already be present in scope's declaration list.
scope must be a valid SgGlobal node.
original_statement must not be NULL and must be associated with a valid source file.
Postcondition
The declaration decl and all its dependent declarations are inserted into scope.
All dependent declarations have their parent set to scope.
Preprocessing directives from the original file are attached to the first statement.
AST edge pointers in the outlined file are updated to reference copied nodes.
Comment markers are added to identify outlined function and dependent declarations.

◆ astIntersection()

std::vector< SgNode * > SageInterface::astIntersection ( SgNode * original,
SgNode * copy,
SgCopyHelp * help )

Computes the intersection of nodes between an original AST and its copy.

This function analyzes two abstract syntax trees (ASTs) to find nodes that are shared between an original AST and a copied version of it. The intersection identifies references in the copy that still point to nodes in the original AST, which may indicate incomplete or improper deep copying.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Queries all nodes from both the original and copied AST subtrees.
  2. Converts both node collections to sets for efficient intersection computation.
  3. Computes the set intersection using std::set_intersection.
  4. Filters out type nodes (SgType) from the intersection since types are allowed to be shared between the original and copy.
  5. If a SgCopyHelp object is provided, it uses the copied node map to match original nodes with their corresponding copies and identifies unmatched nodes.
  6. Reports size differences and unmatched IR nodes, potentially aborting if strict testing conditions are violated.

The function outputs diagnostic information to stdout when verbose mode is enabled via SgProject::get_verbose().

Parameters
originalPointer to the root node of the original AST to be analyzed.
copyPointer to the root node of the copied AST to be compared against the original.
helpOptional pointer to a SgCopyHelp object containing the mapping between original nodes and their copies. If provided, enables detailed matching analysis. May be nullptr if detailed analysis is not needed.
Returns
A vector of SgNode pointers representing the intersection set. Note that the current implementation returns an empty vector as the actual intersection results are stored in meaningIntersectionList which is not returned.
Warning
If the original and copied AST sizes differ and there are unmatched IR nodes, the function will call ROSE_ABORT() to terminate execution under strict testing.
This function produces console output even in non-error conditions when verbose mode is enabled or when size differences are detected.
Precondition
The original parameter must point to a valid SgNode representing the root of an AST.
The copy parameter must point to a valid SgNode representing the root of a copied AST.
Postcondition
The returned vector contains nodes that appear in both ASTs, excluding type nodes.
Diagnostic messages may have been printed to stdout.
Note
Type nodes (SgType and its subclasses) are intentionally excluded from the intersection result as they are designed to be shared across AST copies.
The function uses NodeQuery::querySubTree with V_SgNode to collect all nodes in each AST subtree.
There appears to be a bug in the implementation where the function returns intersectionSet which is never populated, rather than meaningIntersectionList which contains the actual computed intersection.

◆ attachArbitraryText()

PreprocessingInfo * SageInterface::attachArbitraryText ( SgLocatedNode * target,
const std::string & text,
PreprocessingInfo::RelativePositionType position )

Attaches arbitrary text to a located node in the AST as preprocessing information.

This function attaches user-specified arbitrary text to a target AST node as preprocessing information. The text is internally represented as a if preprocessor declaration rather than a define declaration. This design choice was made because ROSE evaluates all define CPP declarations as self-referential macros, whereas if declarations are not evaluated internally. The attached preprocessing information is marked as a transformation so that it can be properly output, which is necessary for correct handling of comments and CPP directives for shared IR nodes when multiple files are used on the command line.

Parameters
targetPointer to the SgLocatedNode in the AST where the text should be attached. Must not be NULL as dangling preprocessor directives are not allowed in the ROSE AST.
textThe arbitrary text string to be attached to the target node.
positionThe relative position where the text should be attached with respect to the target node. Defaults to PreprocessingInfo::before if not specified.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created PreprocessingInfo object containing the attached text. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL upon successful execution.
Warning
This function outputs a warning message to stdout indicating that arbitrary text is being attached as a if declaration. This mechanism is considered suboptimal and may need improvement in future versions.
The attached text is represented as a CpreprocessorIfDeclaration internally, which may not be semantically correct for all use cases.
Precondition
The target parameter must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The target node will have the new PreprocessingInfo attached to its preprocessing information list.
The returned PreprocessingInfo object will have its file info marked as a transformation.
Note
The function was modified in January 2014 to use CpreprocessorIfDeclaration instead of CpreprocessorDefineDeclaration to avoid issues with macro evaluation.
The transformation marking was added in March 2019 to support correct handling of comments and CPP directives for shared IR nodes in multi-file scenarios.

◆ attachComment() [1/2]

PreprocessingInfo * SageInterface::attachComment ( SgLocatedNode * target,
const string & content,
PreprocessingInfo::RelativePositionType position,
PreprocessingInfo::DirectiveType dtype )

Attaches a comment or preprocessor directive to a target AST node.

This function creates and attaches a PreprocessingInfo object representing a comment or preprocessor directive to a specified located node in the ROSE AST. The function automatically infers the appropriate comment style based on the source language of the target node if the directive type is not explicitly specified.

The function supports multiple programming languages including C, C++, Java, Fortran, Ada, and Jovial, each with their respective comment syntax. For C-style comments, the content is wrapped with slash-asterisk delimiters. For C++ and Java, double-slash prefix is used. Fortran uses exclamation mark prefix, Ada uses double-dash prefix, and Jovial comments are expected to already contain their delimiters.

The function also handles various C preprocessor directives such as ifndef, define, endif, and line directives, formatting them appropriately with their respective preprocessor syntax.

Parameters
targetPointer to the SgLocatedNode in the AST where the comment or directive will be attached. Must not be null as dangling comments are not allowed.
contentThe text content of the comment or directive to be attached. For most comment types, this is the raw comment text without delimiters. For Jovial comments, the content should already include the comment delimiters.
positionThe relative position of the comment with respect to the target node. Defaults to PreprocessingInfo::before, meaning the comment appears before the target node in the output.
dtypeThe directive type specifying the kind of comment or preprocessor directive. Defaults to PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration, which triggers automatic language-based inference of the comment style.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created PreprocessingInfo object that has been attached to the target node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Warning
If the programming language cannot be determined and dtype is set to CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration, the function will print a warning message and abort execution.
For CpreprocessorLineDeclaration, the directive type is internally changed to CplusplusStyleComment and the position information is reset to match the target statement.
Precondition
The target parameter must not be null.
If dtype is CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration, the target node must be associated with a source file that has a determinable programming language.
Postcondition
A new PreprocessingInfo object is created and attached to the target node.
The returned PreprocessingInfo object is marked as transformation-generated unless it is a CpreprocessorLineDeclaration, in which case its file info matches the target node.
Note
The function uses expensive language detection by chasing pointers back to the SgFile object when automatic language inference is needed.
Comments and directives are marked as transformations to ensure correct handling when multiple files share IR nodes.
For Jovial comments, the content parameter should already contain the appropriate comment delimiters (percent or quote characters).

const std::string & content,

Attaches a comment or preprocessing directive to a source file's global scope.

This function creates a new PreprocessingInfo object containing the specified content and attaches it to the global scope of the given source file. The preprocessing information is marked as a transformation to ensure proper output handling, which is particularly important when dealing with shared IR nodes that occur when multiple files are specified on the command line. The function supports attaching comments or directives either before or after the global scope.

contentThe string content of the comment or preprocessing directive to attach.
directive_typeThe type of preprocessing directive being attached, specified as a PreprocessingInfo::DirectiveType enumeration value.

Returns

source_file must not be NULL.
position must be either PreprocessingInfo::before or PreprocessingInfo::after.

A new PreprocessingInfo object is created and attached to the global scope of the source file.

◆ buildForwardFunctionDeclaration()

SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl * SageInterface::buildForwardFunctionDeclaration ( SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl * memberFunctionInstantiation)

Builds a forward declaration copy of a template instantiation member function.

This function creates a copy of the input template instantiation member function declaration suitable for use as a forward declaration. This is required when the instantiated function definition needs to be output as a specialization by ROSE.

The implementation uses a custom copy helper class (NondefiningFunctionDeclarationCopyType) derived from SgCopyHelp to control the AST copying process. This custom copier implements the following behavior:

  • Skips copying function definitions (the body of functions)
  • For function declarations, performs a shallow copy if it is a defining declaration, and a deep copy if it is a non-defining declaration
  • All other node types are copied normally using the standard copy mechanism

The function also performs necessary fixups after copying, including:

  • Resetting the firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer to maintain correct symbol table associations
  • Verifying that the copied declaration has the same number of arguments as the original
  • Ensuring source position information consistency between original and copy
Parameters
memberFunctionInstantiationPointer to the template instantiation member function declaration from which to build the forward declaration. Must not be NULL. If this declaration has an associated definition, an error will be triggered as the current implementation requires the definition pointer to be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl that serves as a forward declaration copy of the input function.
Precondition
memberFunctionInstantiation must not be NULL.
memberFunctionInstantiation should not have an associated definition (get_definition() should return NULL), otherwise the function will abort.
Postcondition
The returned declaration has the same number of arguments as the original.
The returned declaration has its firstNondefiningDeclaration set to match the original's firstNondefiningDeclaration.
Source position output and compiler-generated flags are preserved from the original.
Warning
This function will call ROSE_ABORT() if the input declaration has a non-NULL definition, as the code to handle removal of pointers to SgClassDefinition objects is not yet implemented.
Note
The shallow copy mechanism can cause IR nodes to be shared, which is why this function uses a specialized copy helper to ensure proper deep copies of the parameter list and constructor initializer list where needed.
Originally designed and implemented by Qing Yi, with modifications by Dan Quinlan.

◆ buildFunctionPrototype()

SgFunctionDeclaration * SageInterface::buildFunctionPrototype ( SgFunctionDeclaration * functionDeclaration)

Builds a non-defining function declaration (prototype) from a given function declaration.

This function constructs a function prototype (non-defining declaration) from an existing function declaration, which may be a defining declaration. The function handles various types of function declarations including regular functions, member functions, template functions, template member functions, and template instantiations.

The implementation uses a switch statement to dispatch to the appropriate builder function based on the variant type of the input declaration. For each case, it extracts the necessary information such as name, return type, parameter list, scope, and template parameters or arguments, then calls the corresponding buildNondefining* function to create the prototype.

Special handling is provided for:

  • Template member function declarations (V_SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration)
  • Template function declarations (V_SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration)
  • Template instantiation member function declarations (V_SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl)
  • Regular member function declarations (V_SgMemberFunctionDeclaration)
  • Regular function declarations (V_SgFunctionDeclaration)
  • Template instantiation function declarations (V_SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl)

Member functions defined outside of their class scope cannot be output as prototypes (not allowed in C++), so NULL is returned in such cases.

Parameters
functionDeclarationPointer to the source function declaration from which to build the prototype. This can be a defining or non-defining declaration of various types including regular functions, member functions, templates, and template instantiations.
Returns
Pointer to the newly created non-defining function declaration (prototype), or NULL if the prototype cannot be built (e.g., for member functions defined outside their class scope, or for unsupported declaration types).
Warning
Default arguments from the original function declaration may not be reproduced in the generated prototype.
Member functions defined outside of their class cannot have prototypes generated for them, as this is not allowed in C++. NULL is returned in such cases.
Precondition
The functionDeclaration parameter must not be NULL.
The functionDeclaration must have a valid type with a return type accessible via get_type()->get_return_type().
Postcondition
If a non-NULL value is returned, the returned declaration will have its firstNondefiningDeclaration and definingDeclaration pointers set appropriately.
If a non-NULL value is returned, any attached preprocessing info on the returned declaration will be distinct from that of the input declaration.
The returned declaration's parameter list (if created) will have a valid parent pointer.
Note
Constructor functions are detected and marked appropriately using the specialFunctionModifier in the generated prototype.
For template instantiations, the template name is used rather than the instantiated name.
The function builds a new parameter list from the function type's argument list rather than reusing the existing parameter list to avoid parent pointer issues.

◆ call_liveness_analysis()

LivenessAnalysis * SageInterface::call_liveness_analysis ( SgProject * project,
bool debug = false )

Performs liveness analysis on an entire ROSE project.

This function conducts variable liveness analysis across all functions within a given ROSE project. It implements a singleton pattern where the analysis is performed only once, and subsequent calls return the cached result from the first execution.

The implementation follows a two-phase approach:

  1. First, it performs def-use analysis on the project using the DefUseAnalysis class. This establishes the definition and use chains for variables throughout the code.
  2. Second, it creates a LivenessAnalysis object that uses the def-use results to compute variable liveness information.

The function iterates over all function definitions in the project, running liveness analysis on each function body individually. After analyzing each function, it calls fixupStatementsINOUT to propagate the liveness results to the statement level.

When debug mode is enabled, the function outputs DOT format files for visualization of the data flow analysis results, including a var.dot file containing the liveness analysis results.

Parameters
projectPointer to the SgProject representing the entire source code project to be analyzed. Must not be NULL.
debugBoolean flag to enable debug output. When true, the function prints progress information and generates DOT files for visualization. Defaults to false.
Returns
Pointer to the LivenessAnalysis object containing the analysis results. The same pointer is returned on subsequent calls. Returns NULL implicitly if the analysis aborts due to errors (though the function calls ROSE_ABORT in this case).
Warning
If the liveness analysis encounters an error and sets the abort flag, the function will call ROSE_ABORT() which terminates program execution.
This function uses static variables internally, making it not thread-safe. Concurrent calls from multiple threads may result in undefined behavior.
Precondition
The project parameter must point to a valid, fully parsed SgProject object.
The AST within the project should be well-formed and complete.
Postcondition
On successful completion, liveness information is available for all function definitions in the project.
The returned LivenessAnalysis object remains valid for the lifetime of the program and should not be deleted by the caller.
If debug is true, a file named var.dot will be created in the current working directory.
Note
This function implements a singleton pattern for both DefUseAnalysis and LivenessAnalysis objects. The analysis is only performed on the first call.
The caller should not delete the returned LivenessAnalysis pointer as it is managed internally by this function.
The function queries the AST for all SgFunctionDefinition nodes and processes them sequentially.

◆ changeAllBodiesToBlocks()

void SageInterface::changeAllBodiesToBlocks ( SgNode * top,
bool createEmptyBody = true )

Transforms all control flow statement bodies into basic blocks throughout an AST subtree.

This function traverses the AST rooted at the specified node and ensures that all control flow statements have basic blocks (SgBasicBlock) as their body statements. The transformation is performed using a post-order traversal, which processes children before parents. This normalization is useful for subsequent analyses and transformations that expect a consistent AST structure where all statement bodies are wrapped in basic blocks.

The function handles the following statement types:

  • SgForStatement: Ensures the loop body is a basic block
  • SgWhileStmt: Ensures the loop body is a basic block
  • SgDoWhileStmt: Ensures the loop body is a basic block
  • SgSwitchStatement: Ensures the switch body is a basic block
  • SgIfStmt: Ensures both true and false branches are basic blocks
  • SgCatchOptionStmt: Ensures the catch body is a basic block
  • SgUpcForAllStatement: Ensures the UPC forall body is a basic block
  • SgOmpBodyStatement: Ensures OpenMP body statements have basic blocks

The function preserves the isModified flag state for nodes that were not previously modified, resetting the flag if it was only changed by this transformation. This behavior is important for token-based unparsing scenarios.

Parameters
topPointer to the root node of the AST subtree to be transformed. All descendant nodes will be visited and processed.
createEmptyBodyFlag indicating whether to create empty basic blocks for missing bodies (e.g., missing else clauses in if statements). Defaults to true.
Warning
This function modifies the AST structure in place. Ensure that any iterators or pointers to AST nodes within the subtree remain valid after the transformation.
Precondition
The parameter top must point to a valid SgNode within a properly constructed AST.
Postcondition
All control flow statement bodies within the subtree rooted at top will be wrapped in SgBasicBlock nodes.
The isModified flag of nodes that were not previously modified will be preserved (reset to false if changed only by this function).
Note
This function uses an internal visitor class derived from AstSimpleProcessing to perform the post-order traversal.
The transformation calls various ensureBasicBlockAsBody helper functions specific to each statement type.

◆ changeBreakStatementsToGotos()

void SageInterface::changeBreakStatementsToGotos ( SgStatement * loopOrSwitch)

Transforms break statements within a loop or switch into goto statements.

This function locates all break statements within the body of a given loop (while, do-while, or for) or switch statement and replaces them with goto statements that jump to a newly created label placed immediately after the original loop or switch construct. This transformation is useful for code restructuring, loop transformations, or when preparing code for certain optimization passes that cannot handle break statements directly.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Extracts the body of the loop or switch statement
  2. Finds all break statements within that body using SageInterface::findBreakStmts
  3. If break statements exist, creates a unique label statement named breakLabelN (where N is an incrementing counter) and inserts it after the loop or switch
  4. Replaces each break statement with a goto statement targeting the new label

A static counter ensures that each generated label has a unique name across multiple invocations of this function within the same compilation.

Parameters
loopOrSwitchA pointer to a statement that must be either a while loop (SgWhileStmt), do-while loop (SgDoWhileStmt), for loop (SgForStatement), or switch statement (SgSwitchStatement). The function will assert if the body cannot be extracted.
Warning
This function modifies the AST in place. The original break statements are replaced and their parent relationships are updated. Ensure that any iterators or references to the original break statements are invalidated after calling this function.
The function uses a static counter for label naming, which means label names are not reset between different translation units or separate transformation passes.
Precondition
The loopOrSwitch parameter must point to a valid SgWhileStmt, SgDoWhileStmt, SgForStatement, or SgSwitchStatement node.
The parent of loopOrSwitch must be a valid scope statement to allow insertion of the new label.
The loop or switch must have a non-null body.
Postcondition
All break statements that were direct children of the loop or switch body are replaced with goto statements.
If any break statements were found, a new label statement is inserted immediately after the loop or switch statement.
The AST remains well-formed with correct parent-child relationships.
Note
This function only affects break statements found by findBreakStmts, which typically finds breaks at the immediate level without descending into nested loops or switches.
The generated label contains an empty basic block as its statement body.

◆ changeContinuesToGotos()

void SageInterface::changeContinuesToGotos ( SgStatement * stmt,
SgLabelStatement * label )

Transforms all continue statements within a code block into goto statements targeting a specified label.

This function searches for all continue statements (SgContinueStmt) within the given statement block and replaces each one with a goto statement that jumps to the provided label. This transformation is useful for loop restructuring, code normalization, or preparing code for certain optimization passes where continue semantics need to be expressed as explicit control flow jumps.

The implementation first collects all continue statements using SageInterface::findContinueStmts, then iterates through them, creating a new goto statement for each continue and replacing the original continue statement using LowLevelRewrite::replace.

This function is conditionally compiled and is not available when ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is defined, as the LowLevelRewrite::replace functionality is unavailable in that mode. Additionally, on Microsoft Visual C++ compilers (when _MSC_VER is defined), the function will abort as the replacement operation is not supported.

Parameters
stmtThe statement block in which to search for continue statements. This can be any SgStatement that may contain nested continue statements, such as a loop body or compound statement.
labelThe label statement that all generated goto statements will target. This label should be positioned appropriately in the code to achieve the desired control flow behavior.
Warning
This function calls ROSE_ABORT() when compiled with ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT defined or when compiled with Microsoft Visual C++ (_MSC_VER defined).
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the label is valid and properly placed in the control flow graph to maintain correct program semantics.
Precondition
stmt must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgStatement.
label must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgLabelStatement that exists in the same scope or an enclosing scope accessible from the continue statements.
Postcondition
All continue statements originally contained within stmt are replaced with goto statements targeting label.
The original continue statements are removed from the AST.
Note
This function modifies the AST in place by replacing nodes.
The function relies on SageBuilder::buildGotoStatement to create the replacement goto statements and LowLevelRewrite::replace to perform the AST modification.

void SageInterface::checkAccessPermissions ( SgNode * astNode)

Checks and displays access permissions of all declarations in an AST subtree.

This function performs a traversal of the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) starting from the given node and examines the access permissions (access modifiers) of all declaration statements found within the subtree. For each declaration encountered, it identifies and displays the access modifier information for the defining declaration, the first non-defining declaration, and any other declaration variants.

The function uses an internal traversal class derived from AstSimpleProcessing to visit each node in preorder. When a declaration statement is found, it retrieves the associated defining and non-defining declarations and outputs their access modifier details using the display method. This is primarily intended as a debugging utility for analyzing access permission consistency across different declaration forms.

◆ checkSymbolTables()

void SageInterface::checkSymbolTables ( SgNode * astNode)

Checks and prints symbol tables for specific scopes in the AST for debugging purposes.

This function traverses the AST subtree rooted at the given node and examines symbol tables of specific scopes for debugging purposes. It uses a custom traversal class derived from AstSimpleProcessing to visit each node in preorder.

The function specifically targets two types of scopes:

  1. Function definitions: If a function named "main" is found, the symbol table of its function body (basic block) is printed.
  2. Namespace definitions: If a namespace named "B" is found, its symbol table is printed.

For each matching scope, the function prints the name of the function or namespace to standard output, followed by the contents of the associated symbol table.

The function only checks symbol tables for functions named "main" and namespaces named "B". Other scopes are visited but their symbol tables are not printed.
Precondition
astNode must be a valid pointer to an SgNode within a properly constructed AST.
Postcondition
The symbol tables of the main function body and namespace B (if present in the subtree) will have been printed to standard output.
Note
This function was added for debugging support as indicated by the implementation date of August 14, 2020.
The traversal is performed in preorder, meaning parent nodes are visited before their children.

◆ cleanupNontransformedBasicBlockNode()

void SageInterface::cleanupNontransformedBasicBlockNode ( )

Removes unused basic block IR nodes that were added during normalization.

This function performs denormalization of the ROSE AST by removing unnecessary SgBasicBlock nodes that were previously added as part of the normalization process. It iterates through a collection of tracked basic block nodes (addedBasicBlockNodes) and for each block containing exactly one statement, it replaces the block with its single contained statement in the parent construct.

The function handles denormalization for various control flow constructs including:

  • SgIfStmt (both true and false bodies)
  • SgWhileStmt
  • SgSwitchStatement
  • SgForStatement
  • SgCaseOptionStmt
  • SgDefaultOptionStmt
  • SgDoWhileStmt

The algorithm preserves the isModified flag state of parent nodes. If a parent node was not previously marked as modified, the function resets the flag after making structural changes, ensuring that this cleanup operation does not incorrectly mark nodes as transformed.

This function is designed to support better quality token-based unparsing by removing artificial basic blocks that would otherwise affect the output format.

Warning
This function should be called before the unparse step to ensure proper output formatting.
The function will call ROSE_ABORT() if it encounters an unhandled parent statement type.
Precondition
The addedBasicBlockNodes vector must contain valid pointers to SgBasicBlock nodes that were added during normalization.
Each SgBasicBlock in addedBasicBlockNodes must have a valid non-null parent that is an SgStatement.
Postcondition
Basic blocks containing exactly one statement are replaced by their contained statement in the parent construct.
Processed basic block pointers in addedBasicBlockNodes are set to NULL or nullptr.
The isModified flag of parent nodes is preserved if they were not previously modified.
Note
This function modifies the global addedBasicBlockNodes vector by setting processed entries to NULL or nullptr.
Basic blocks with zero statements or more than one statement are left unchanged.

◆ clearUnusedVariableSymbols()

void SageInterface::clearUnusedVariableSymbols ( SgNode * root)

Removes unused variable symbols with unknown type declarations from the memory pool.

This function identifies and deletes variable symbols that have declarations with SgTypeUnknown type. It queries the memory pool for all SgVariableSymbol nodes and examines each one to determine if it should be removed. The deletion criteria depends on whether a root node is specified:

When root is NULL, all variable symbols with SgTypeUnknown type declarations are deleted unconditionally. When root is specified, the function additionally checks whether the symbol is referenced by any SgVarRefExp nodes within the subtree rooted at the given node. Only symbols that are not referenced within that subtree are deleted.

The function performs cleanup by deleting both the symbol and its associated declaration to prevent memory leaks and maintain consistency in the AST symbol tables.

Parameters
rootOptional pointer to an SgNode that serves as the root of a subtree to check for variable references. If NULL, all symbols with unknown type declarations are deleted without checking for references. If non-NULL, only symbols not referenced within the specified subtree are deleted.
Warning
This function permanently deletes symbols and their declarations from memory. Ensure that the symbols being deleted are truly unused to avoid dangling references elsewhere in the AST.
When root is NULL, the function does not check for references before deletion, which may lead to invalid symbol pointers if the symbols are still in use elsewhere in the program.
Precondition
The memory pool must be properly initialized and contain valid SgVariableSymbol nodes.
If root is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SgNode within the AST.
Postcondition
All variable symbols with SgTypeUnknown type declarations that meet the deletion criteria are removed from memory along with their associated declarations.
Note
Symbols with declarations that have types other than SgTypeUnknown are preserved regardless of whether they are referenced.
The function uses NodeQuery::queryMemoryPool to find all variable symbols and NodeQuery::querySubTree to find variable references within the specified subtree.

◆ collectReadOnlyVariables()

void SageInterface::collectReadOnlyVariables ( SgStatement * stmt,
std::set< SgInitializedName * > & readOnlyVars,
bool coarseGrain = true )

Collects read-only variables within a given statement.

This function identifies and collects all variables that are read but not written within the specified statement. The statement can be a function body, a scope block, or a single line statement. The function employs two strategies for collecting read-only variables:

Primary strategy: Uses the collectReadWriteVariables() function to obtain sets of read and write variables, then computes the set difference (read - write) to determine read-only variables.

Fallback strategy: If the primary analysis fails (which can happen with Qing's side effect analysis), the function falls back to a simpler type-based approach. This fallback traverses the AST and collects all referenced variables that have a const type, adding their declarations to the read-only set.

Parameters
stmtPointer to the SgStatement to analyze. This can be a function body, a scope statement, or a single line statement. Must not be NULL.
readOnlyVarsReference to a set that will be populated with pointers to SgInitializedName objects representing the read-only variables found within the statement. Results are inserted into this set.
coarseGrainBoolean flag controlling the granularity of the analysis. When true (default), uses coarse-grained analysis. When false, uses fine-grained analysis. This parameter is passed to the underlying collectReadWriteVariables() function.
Precondition
stmt must not be NULL.
readOnlyVars should be a valid set, typically empty before the call.
Postcondition
readOnlyVars contains all identified read-only variables from the statement. If the primary analysis succeeds, these are variables that are read but never written. If the fallback is used, these are variables with const types.
Note
The fallback mechanism using const type detection may produce different results than the primary read/write analysis, as it only considers type information rather than actual data flow.
The function uses RoseAst iterator for AST traversal in the fallback case.
Warning
If collectReadWriteVariables() fails, the fallback analysis may not capture all semantically read-only variables, only those with explicit const type qualifiers.

◆ collectReadWriteRefs()

bool SageInterface::collectReadWriteRefs ( SgStatement * stmt,
std::vector< SgNode * > & readRefs,
std::vector< SgNode * > & writeRefs,
bool useCachedDefUse )

Collects read and write references from a given statement using side effect analysis.

This function performs side effect analysis on a given statement to identify all memory read and write references. It utilizes the ROSE compiler infrastructure's loop transformation interface and array annotation system to analyze statement references. The function handles both regular statements and function declarations by extracting the function body when a function declaration is provided.

The analysis uses the AnalyzeStmtRefs function from the loop transformation framework, which relies on array annotations for tracking side effects. When useCachedDefUse is true, the function uses a cached array interface instance; otherwise, it creates a new instance and observes the AST without performing alias analysis or value propagation.

The function accumulates results into the provided vectors, allowing multiple statements to have their effects collected into the same containers.

Parameters
stmtThe statement to analyze for read and write references. Can be a regular statement or a function declaration. If a function declaration is provided, the function will extract and analyze its body. Must not be NULL.
readRefsOutput vector that will be populated with SgNode pointers representing all read references found in the statement. Results are appended to any existing contents.
writeRefsOutput vector that will be populated with SgNode pointers representing all write references found in the statement. Results are appended to any existing contents.
useCachedDefUseWhen true, uses a cached ArrayInterface instance for def-use analysis. When false, creates a new ArrayInterface instance with observation only (no alias analysis or value propagation).
Returns
True if the analysis completed successfully with all called functions properly annotated. False if the statement calls at least one function that has not been annotated with the RWset annotation method.
Precondition
stmt must not be NULL.
If stmt is a function declaration, it must have a defining declaration with a function body available.
The enclosing function definition must be determinable for the given statement.
Postcondition
readRefs contains all read reference nodes found in the analyzed statement, appended to any previous contents.
writeRefs contains all write reference nodes found in the analyzed statement, appended to any previous contents.
Warning
This function is disabled when ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is defined.
The reference types stored in the vectors may include SgInitializedName nodes (for variable declarations) rather than SgVarRefExp nodes.
A return value of false does not necessarily indicate a failure; it may simply mean that some called functions lack annotations, which may be acceptable depending on the use case.
Note
The function modifies global state through LoopTransformInterface::set_arrayInfo, LoopTransformInterface::set_astInterface, and LoopTransformInterface::set_sideEffectInfo.
When useCachedDefUse is false, alias analysis and value propagation are intentionally disabled during array interface initialization.

◆ collectReadWriteVariables()

set< SgInitializedName * > & readVars,
set< SgInitializedName * > & writeVars,

Collects unique variables that are read or written within a statement.

This function analyzes a given statement and identifies all variables that are read from or written to within that statement. The analysis collects unique variable references and stores them in separate sets for read and write operations. Note that a variable can appear in both sets if it is both read and written within the same statement. The statement can be a function body, a scope block, or a single line statement.

The implementation first delegates to collectReadWriteRefs to obtain raw read and write references, then converts each reference to its corresponding SgInitializedName using convertRefToInitializedName. The use of std::set containers ensures that only unique variables are stored in the output collections.

A variable may appear in both readVars and writeVars if it is both read from and written to within the statement.

Collects variable references that are used by address within a given statement.

This function traverses a given statement and identifies all variable references that are used by address. A variable is considered to be used by address in two primary cases:

  1. The variable reference is the operand of an address-of operator (SgAddressOfOp), such as in the expression &a.
  2. In C++ code, the variable reference is passed as an argument to a function call where the corresponding parameter has a reference type (Type&), such as foo(a) when foo is declared as foo(Type& parameter).

The function uses NodeQuery to traverse the subtree rooted at the given statement and collect all SgVarRefExp nodes. Each variable reference is then checked using the isUseByAddressVariableRef helper function to determine if it qualifies as a use-by-address reference. Qualifying references are inserted into the output set.

sPointer to the SgStatement to be analyzed. The function will traverse all descendants of this statement to find variable references. Must not be NULL.
varSetBOutput parameter. A reference to a set that will be populated with pointers to SgVarRefExp nodes that represent variables used by address. The set ensures uniqueness of collected references.
Precondition
The parameter s must point to a valid SgStatement node.
The AST containing s must be properly constructed with valid parent pointers.
Postcondition
The set varSetB contains all variable references within s that are used by address, in addition to any elements it contained prior to the call.
Note
This function relies on the isUseByAddressVariableRef helper function to determine whether a given variable reference qualifies as use-by-address.
The commented-out code block shows the original implementation logic that has been refactored into the isUseByAddressVariableRef function.
Warning
This function casts away the const qualifier from the input statement when calling NodeQuery::querySubTree. The statement itself is not modified.

Empty function or ill-formed function detected.

Collects variable references found within array type expressions in constructor initializers.

This function traverses the subtree rooted at the given node and searches for constructor initializers (SgConstructorInitializer). For each constructor initializer that has an array type expression, the function extracts all variable reference expressions (SgVarRefExp) from the array index expressions and appends them to the provided collection list.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Query the subtree for all SgConstructorInitializer nodes
  2. For each constructor initializer, check if its expression type is an array type
  3. If so, query the array index expression for all variable references
  4. Append each found variable reference to the output list

This is useful for identifying variables that are used in array dimension specifications within constructor contexts, which may require special handling during code transformations or analysis.

Precondition
root must not be NULL.
currentVarRefList should be a valid container, though it may contain existing elements.
Postcondition
currentVarRefList contains all previously existing elements plus any newly discovered variable references from array type index expressions.
The return value equals the number of new elements added to currentVarRefList.
Note
The variable references collected have special scopes associated with their constructor initializer context. Currently, this scope information is not communicated to users, which may be addressed in future implementations.

This transformation can be useful for code normalization, simplification of analysis passes, or when targeting backends that prefer while-loop constructs over for-loops.

The AST remains in a valid and consistent state.

◆ convertForToWhile()

void SageInterface::convertForToWhile ( SgForStatement * f)

Converts a for loop statement into an equivalent while loop statement.

This function transforms a SgForStatement into a semantically equivalent SgWhileStmt wrapped in a basic block. The transformation follows these steps:

  1. The increment expression of the for loop is moved into the loop body by calling moveForStatementIncrementIntoBody.
  2. A new basic block is created to contain the initialization statements and the resulting while loop.
  3. The initialization statements from the for loop are transferred to the new basic block with their parent pointers updated accordingly.
  4. If the for loop has an empty test condition, a constant true expression is used as the while loop condition (creating an infinite loop that must be exited via break or return). Otherwise, the original test condition is preserved.
  5. The while statement is constructed with the test condition and the original loop body.
  6. The original for statement is replaced in the AST with the new basic block containing the initialization and while loop.
Parameters
fPointer to the SgForStatement node to be converted. This for statement will be replaced in the AST by the equivalent while loop construct.
Warning
The original SgForStatement node is replaced in the AST and may become detached. Callers should not use the original for statement pointer after this function returns.
This function assumes the for statement has a valid parent that is a statement capable of having child statements replaced.
Precondition
The parameter f must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgForStatement.
The for statement must have a valid parent that is an SgStatement.
The for statement must be properly formed with valid for_init_stmt and loop_body components.
Postcondition
The original for statement is replaced in the AST by a basic block containing the initialization statements followed by a while loop.
The while loop condition is either the original test expression or a constant true value if the original condition was empty.
All transferred statements have their parent pointers correctly updated.
Note
The increment expression handling is delegated to moveForStatementIncrementIntoBody, which must be called before the loop body is transferred to the while statement.
This transformation preserves the semantics of the original for loop while changing its syntactic representation in the AST.
