◆ loopCollapsing()

SgExprListExp * SageInterface::loopCollapsing ( SgForStatement * loop,
size_t collapsing_factor )

Collapses multiple nested for-loops into a single loop for parallelization optimization.

This function performs loop collapsing transformation on a nest of perfectly nested for-loops. Loop collapsing is a common optimization technique used to increase parallelism by combining multiple nested loops into a single loop with a larger iteration space. This is particularly useful for OpenMP parallelization where collapsing loops can improve load balancing and reduce synchronization overhead.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Extracts loop header information (induction variable, lower bound, upper bound, step) for each level of the nested loops up to the collapsing factor.
  2. Normalizes each target loop to ensure canonical form with iteration starting from 0.
  3. Computes the total iteration count for each loop level and the combined iteration space.
  4. Creates new variables to store iteration counts and interval values needed for index calculation.
  5. Generates a new collapsed loop with a single index variable that iterates over the combined iteration space.
  6. Inserts assignment statements at the beginning of the loop body to reconstruct the original induction variables from the collapsed index using division and modulo operations.
  7. Applies constant folding optimization to simplify the transformed AST.

The transformation handles both incremental and decremental loops. For a loop with induction variable i at level k, the original value is computed as: i = (collapsed_index / interval[k]) * step[k] + lb[k] for incremental loops, or i = -(collapsed_index / interval[k]) * step[k] + lb[k] for decremental loops.

Parameters
loopPointer to the outermost SgForStatement of the loop nest to be collapsed. The loop nest must contain at least collapsing_factor levels of perfectly nested canonical for-loops.
collapsing_factorThe number of nested loop levels to collapse into a single loop. Must be greater than 1 for any transformation to occur.
Returns
A pointer to an SgExprListExp containing SgVarRefExp pointers to all newly created variables that may need to be added to OpenMP map-in clauses. Returns NULL if collapsing_factor is less than or equal to 1, or if any of the target loops is not in canonical form.
Precondition
The loop parameter must point to a valid SgForStatement node.
The loop nest must contain at least collapsing_factor levels of nested for-loops.
Each loop in the nest up to collapsing_factor must be in canonical form or be normalizable to canonical form.
This function requires ROSE to be built without USE_ROSE and without ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT defined.
Postcondition
The original loop nest is replaced with a single collapsed loop in the AST.
New variable declarations are inserted before the loop for storing iteration counts and interval values.
The loop parameter is updated to point to the newly created collapsed loop.
Constant folding optimization is applied to the transformed scope.
Warning
This function modifies the AST in place, replacing the original loop structure.
The function assumes perfectly nested loops; imperfectly nested loops may produce incorrect results.
Memory for internal arrays is dynamically allocated and freed; if the function returns early due to non-canonical loops, memory is properly deallocated.
The function uses global scope for generating unique variable names to avoid conflicts when declarations are moved during OpenMP target data promotion.

◆ loopInterchange()

bool SageInterface::loopInterchange ( SgForStatement * loop,
size_t depth,
size_t lexicoOrder )

Performs loop interchange on a perfectly-nested loop using a lexicographical permutation order.

This function permutes the loop headers (initialization, test condition, and increment expressions) of a perfectly-nested loop nest according to a specified lexicographical order number. The lexicographical order represents one of the possible permutations of the loop levels, where the total number of permutations is depth factorial (depth!). The function extracts the loop headers from each level of the nest, computes the permutation array corresponding to the given lexicographical order, and then reassigns the headers to implement the interchange.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Collects all for-statements in the loop nest using a subtree query
  2. Saves the initialization statement, test expression, and increment expression for each loop level
  3. Converts the lexicographical order number to a permutation array using getPermutationOrder
  4. Rewrites each loop's header components according to the computed permutation
  5. Updates parent pointers and source position information for transformed nodes
Parameters
loopPointer to the outermost SgForStatement of the perfectly-nested loop to be interchanged. Must not be NULL and must be the root of a perfectly-nested loop structure.
depthThe number of loop levels to consider for interchange. Must be greater than 1.
lexicoOrderThe lexicographical order number specifying the desired permutation. Must be in the range [0, depth!). A value of 0 indicates no interchange.
Returns
True if the loop interchange was performed successfully. Always returns true if parameters are valid, including when lexicoOrder is 0 (no interchange needed).
Precondition
loop must not be NULL.
depth must be greater than 1.
lexicoOrder must be less than depth factorial.
The loop nest rooted at loop must contain at least depth levels of perfectly-nested for-loops.
Postcondition
The loop headers at each level have been permuted according to the specified lexicographical order.
Parent pointers for all modified AST nodes are correctly updated.
Source position information is set for all transformed nodes.
Note
A lexicoOrder value of 0 is treated as a special case that performs no interchange and returns immediately.
The function currently does not verify that the input loop has exactly depth levels of perfectly-nested children loops (marked as TODO in implementation).
This function modifies the AST in place by reassigning loop header components between different loop levels.
Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the loop interchange is semantically valid (i.e., that it preserves program correctness with respect to data dependencies).
The function assumes the loop nest is perfectly nested; behavior is undefined for imperfectly nested loops.

◆ loopTiling()

bool SageInterface::loopTiling ( SgForStatement * loopNest,
size_t targetLevel,
size_t tileSize )

Applies loop tiling transformation to a specified loop within a loop nest.

This function performs loop tiling (also known as loop blocking) on a target loop within a given loop nest structure. Loop tiling is a loop optimization technique that partitions a loop's iteration space into smaller blocks or tiles to improve cache locality and enable better data reuse.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Locates the target loop at the specified nesting level within the loop nest.
  2. Normalizes the target loop to ensure it is in canonical form.
  3. Creates a new outer controlling loop that iterates over tiles.
  4. Modifies the original target loop to iterate within each tile.
  5. Adjusts the loop bounds to handle boundary conditions using a conditional expression (min/max logic) to ensure correctness when the iteration space is not evenly divisible by the tile size.
  6. Applies constant folding to the control loop's test and increment expressions.

The controlling loop variable is named with a prefix "_lt_var_" followed by the original loop index variable name. The upper bound of the inner loop uses a conditional expression to handle the case where the remaining iterations are fewer than the tile size.

Parameters
loopNestPointer to the outermost for statement of the loop nest to be tiled. Must not be NULL.
targetLevelThe nesting level of the loop to be tiled, starting from 1. Level 1 corresponds to the outermost loop. Must be greater than 0 and must not exceed the actual depth of the loop nest.
tileSizeThe size of each tile (number of iterations per tile). If tileSize is 0 or 1, no tiling is performed and the function returns true immediately. This allows obtaining reference values for untiled code.
Returns
True if the tiling transformation was successful or if tileSize is less than or equal to 1 (no tiling needed). False if the target loop cannot be converted to canonical form.
Warning
The function will abort (ROSE_ABORT) if the target loop has an illegal condition operator or increment expression that is not recognized as part of a canonical loop form.
The normalization step's return value is noted as unreliable in the implementation, so normalization failures may not be properly reported.
Precondition
loopNest must not be NULL.
targetLevel must be greater than 0.
The loop nest must contain at least targetLevel nested for loops.
The target loop should be normalizable and in or convertible to canonical form.
Postcondition
If successful, a new controlling loop is inserted before the original loop nest.
The original loop nest is moved inside the new controlling loop's body.
The target loop's bounds are modified to iterate within tile boundaries.
A new loop index variable declaration is inserted before the controlling loop.
Constant folding is applied to the controlling loop's test and increment expressions.
Note
A canonical loop is expected to have a binary comparison operator (<=, >=) in its condition and a compound assignment operator (+=, -=) for its increment.
The function handles both incrementing (+=) and decrementing (-=) loops.
If the parent of loopNest is a single statement body, it is converted to a basic block to accommodate the additional statements.

◆ loopUnrolling()

bool SageInterface::loopUnrolling ( SgForStatement * target_loop,
size_t unrolling_factor )

Performs loop unrolling transformation on a given for loop.

This function applies loop unrolling optimization to a canonical for loop by replicating the loop body a specified number of times. The transformation reduces loop overhead by decreasing the number of iterations while increasing the amount of work done per iteration.

The algorithm proceeds as follows:

  1. Normalizes the target loop to ensure it is in canonical form.
  2. Validates that the loop is canonical with identifiable loop variable, bounds, and step.
  3. Creates a fringe loop to handle remaining iterations when the iteration count is not evenly divisible by the unrolling factor.
  4. Computes the iteration count using the formula: iter_count = (ub-lb+1)/step with adjustment for non-zero remainder.
  5. Calculates the fringe value to determine how many iterations the fringe loop must handle.
  6. Applies constant folding to determine at compile time if a fringe loop is necessary.
  7. Modifies the original loop's upper bound to account for the fringe iterations.
  8. Multiplies the step by the unrolling factor.
  9. Replicates the loop body (unrolling_factor - 1) times, adjusting index variable references to use offset expressions (ivar +/- step*i).
  10. Removes the fringe loop if constant folding determines it is unnecessary.
  11. Performs constant folding optimization on the transformed AST.
Parameters
target_loopPointer to the SgForStatement representing the for loop to be unrolled. The loop must be normalizable and in canonical form with identifiable loop variable, lower bound, upper bound, and step expression.
unrolling_factorThe number of times to replicate the loop body. A value of 0 or 1 results in no transformation being applied.
Returns
True if the loop unrolling transformation was successful or if unrolling_factor is less than or equal to 1 (no transformation needed). Returns false if the target loop is not in canonical form.
Warning
This function modifies the AST in place. The original loop structure will be altered after successful transformation.
If the loop cannot be normalized or is not canonical, an error message is printed to stderr and the function returns false.
Large unrolling factors may significantly increase code size and may not improve performance due to instruction cache effects.
Precondition
target_loop must be a valid pointer to an SgForStatement node in the AST.
The loop should be normalizable to canonical form for successful transformation.
The function is only operational when ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is not defined.
Postcondition
If successful, the target loop will have its body replicated unrolling_factor times with appropriate index variable adjustments.
The loop step will be multiplied by the unrolling factor.
A fringe loop may be inserted after the main loop to handle remaining iterations.
If the iteration count is evenly divisible by the unrolling factor, no fringe loop will be present in the final AST.
Constant folding optimization will have been applied to the enclosing scope.
Note
The function uses a global counter (gensym_counter) to generate unique variable names for the fringe calculation variable.
The fringe loop is initially created as a deep copy of the original loop and is used as a buffer for the original loop body during transformation.
Variables defined within the loop body are protected from redefinition issues through the introduction of new scopes via SgBasicBlock.

◆ makeSingleStatementBodyToBlock()

SgBasicBlock * SageInterface::makeSingleStatementBodyToBlock ( SgStatement * singleStmt)

Converts a single statement body into a basic block.

This function takes a single statement that serves as the body of a control structure (such as a loop, conditional, or switch statement) and wraps it in an SgBasicBlock. The function identifies the parent control structure of the given statement and delegates to the appropriate helper function to ensure the body is converted to a basic block.

The function handles the following parent statement types:

  • SgForStatement (loop body)
  • SgUpcForAllStatement (UPC forall loop body)
  • SgWhileStmt (while loop body)
  • SgDoWhileStmt (do-while loop body)
  • SgSwitchStatement (switch body)
  • SgCaseOptionStmt (case option body)
  • SgDefaultOptionStmt (default option body)
  • SgCatchOptionStmt (catch block body)
  • SgIfStmt (true body or false body)
  • SgOmpBodyStatement (OpenMP body statement)

For each case, the function verifies that the input statement matches the expected body position before performing the conversion.

Parameters
singleStmtPointer to the single statement that should be wrapped in a basic block. This statement must not be NULL, must not already be an SgBasicBlock, and must be a body statement of a recognized control structure.
Returns
Pointer to the newly created SgBasicBlock that now contains the original single statement.
Precondition
singleStmt is not NULL.
singleStmt is not already an SgBasicBlock.
singleStmt is a body statement (isBodyStatement returns true).
The parent of singleStmt is a valid SgLocatedNode representing a supported control structure.
Postcondition
The returned SgBasicBlock is not NULL.
The original single statement is now contained within the returned basic block.
The parent control structure's body pointer is updated to reference the new basic block.
Warning
The function will trigger an assertion failure if the input statement is NULL, is already a basic block, or is not a body statement.
The function will trigger an assertion failure if the conversion fails to produce a valid basic block.
Note
This function is useful for transformations that require a basic block as the body of control structures, ensuring consistent AST structure for subsequent analysis or transformation passes.

◆ mangleModifierType()

string SageInterface::mangleModifierType ( SgModifierType * type)

Mangles a modifier type into its encoded string representation for name mangling.

This function generates a mangled string representation for C++ type modifiers including const, volatile, and restrict qualifiers, as well as UPC (Unified Parallel C) shared type modifiers. The mangling follows a specific encoding scheme where each modifier is represented by a single character prefix:

  • K for const
  • V for volatile
  • r for restrict
  • S for UPC strict shared
  • R for UPC relaxed shared

For UPC shared types, the block size is also encoded as a numeric prefix followed by an underscore. The function recursively mangles the base type by calling mangleType on the underlying type after processing all modifiers.

The order of modifier encoding places volatile before const, and restrict before both. UPC shared modifiers are placed at the outermost position with their associated block size.

Parameters
typePointer to an SgModifierType object representing the modified type to be mangled. This parameter should not be null and must contain valid modifier information and a valid base type.
Returns
A string containing the mangled representation of the modifier type, including all qualifier prefixes concatenated with the mangled base type.
Precondition
The type parameter must be a valid non-null pointer to an SgModifierType.
The base type accessible via type->get_base_type() must be valid.
Postcondition
The returned string contains the complete mangled representation of the modifier type including its base type.
Note
This function supports UPC shared type modifiers in addition to standard C++ type qualifiers (const, volatile, restrict).
The mangling scheme appears to follow or be inspired by the Itanium C++ ABI name mangling conventions for type qualifiers.
For UPC shared types, the function distinguishes between strict and relaxed shared memory consistency models.
Warning
If the type pointer is null, the behavior is undefined as the function does not perform null pointer validation.
The function assumes that helper functions such as isConstType, isVolatileType, isRestrictType, isUpcSharedModifierType, getUpcSharedBlockSize, isUpcStrictSharedModifierType, and mangleType are available and correctly implemented.

◆ mangleScalarType()

string SageInterface::mangleScalarType ( SgType * type)

Generates a mangled name encoding for a scalar type according to the Itanium C++ ABI.

This function converts a ROSE compiler scalar type (SgType) into its corresponding mangled string representation following the Itanium C++ ABI name mangling specification. The function handles fundamental scalar types including void, boolean, character types, integer types of various sizes and signedness, floating-point types, and complex/imaginary types. Each type is mapped to a specific character or short string code as defined by the ABI specification.

The mangling codes used include:

  • v: void
  • w: wchar_t
  • c16: char16_t (C99/C++11)
  • c32: char32_t (C99/C++11)
  • b: bool
  • c: char
  • a: signed char
  • h: unsigned char
  • s: short/signed short
  • t: unsigned short
  • i: int/signed int
  • j: unsigned int
  • l: long/signed long
  • m: unsigned long
  • x: long long
  • y: unsigned long long
  • f: float
  • d: double
  • e: long double
  • C: complex
  • G: imaginary

Some types defined in the ABI specification are not supported by ROSE, including __int128, unsigned __int128, float128, ellipsis, and IEEE 754r decimal floating point types.

Parameters
typePointer to an SgType object representing the scalar type to be mangled. Must be a valid scalar type as determined by isScalarType().
Returns
A string containing the mangled representation of the scalar type. Returns "Invalid.mtype" if the type variant is not recognized, or ".unhandledSgTypeString." for SgTypeString which is not properly handled.
Precondition
The parameter type must not be null.
The parameter type must satisfy isScalarType(type) == true.
Postcondition
The returned string is non-empty and contains the mangled type encoding.
Warning
The isScalarType() check may not exactly match the ABI specification for what constitutes a scalar type.
SgTypeString is not properly handled and returns a placeholder string.
Several ABI-specified types are missing from ROSE and cannot be mangled, including __int128, unsigned __int128, float128, ellipsis, and IEEE 754r decimal floating point types.
Note
The char16_t and char32_t types use non-standard mangling codes (c16 and c32) which may differ from the official Itanium ABI encoding.
Signed and unsigned variants of short, int, and long are handled together with their explicitly signed counterparts.

◆ mangleType()

string SageInterface::mangleType ( SgType * type)

Generates a mangled string representation for a given SAGE type.

This function produces a mangled name string for C++ types following a naming convention similar to the Itanium C++ ABI name mangling scheme. The function handles various type categories including scalar types, modifier types, pointer types, reference types, typedef types, and array types. The implementation uses memoization through a type-to-string map to avoid redundant computation for previously processed types. For composite types such as pointers, references, and arrays, the function recursively mangles the base types.

The mangling conventions used include:

  • Scalar types are delegated to mangleScalarType
  • Modifier types are delegated to mangleModifierType
  • Pointer types are prefixed with 'P' followed by the mangled base type
  • Reference types are prefixed with 'R' followed by the mangled base type
  • Typedef types are resolved to their underlying base type
  • Array types use format "A<count>_<base_type>" with optional "H" suffix for UPC arrays with threads
Parameters
typePointer to the SgType object representing the type to be mangled. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A string containing the mangled representation of the input type. Returns "*Unhandled*" if the type category is not supported.
Warning
Rvalue reference types are not yet supported in EDG/ROSE/GCC and are not handled by this function.
Function types, class-enum types, pointer-to-member types, and template parameters are not currently implemented and will result in an error message being printed to stderr and "*Unhandled*" being returned.
There appears to be a bug in the reference type handling where isSgPointerType is used instead of isSgReferenceType to retrieve the base type.
Precondition
The parameter type must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgType object.
Global maps type_string_map and string_type_map must be properly initialized.
Postcondition
The mangled string result is cached in type_string_map for future lookups.
If the mangled string is new, the type is registered in string_type_map.
Note
This function is intended to be moved into sageInterface when ready.
The function uses memoization to improve performance for repeated type lookups.
For UPC array types with threads, the element count is suffixed with "H".

◆ markNodeToBeUnparsed()

void SageInterface::markNodeToBeUnparsed ( SgNode * node,
int physical_file_id )

Marks an AST node and its subtree to be unparsed during code generation.

This function marks a given ROSE AST node for unparsing, which means the node will be included in the generated output code. The function specifically handles SgLocatedNode types by setting transformation flags and configuring the output settings for code generation. Additionally, it associates the node with a specific physical file identifier, which is required for proper header file unparsing support.

The function performs the following operations on SgLocatedNode instances:

  1. Calls setTransformation() to mark the node as transformed
  2. Calls setOutputInCodeGeneration() to enable output during code generation
  3. Sets the physical file ID on the node's file info if available

Note that there is commented-out code for a subtree traversal via markTransformationsForOutput() which was previously used but found to cause issues with certain transformations such as Reverse Type Dependence, where too much of the AST would be marked for unparsing.

Parameters
nodePointer to the SgNode that should be marked for unparsing. If this node is not an SgLocatedNode, no action is taken. May be NULL, in which case the function has no effect.
physical_file_idThe physical file identifier to associate with this node. This ID is used during header file unparsing to determine which file the node belongs to.
Warning
The commented-out markTransformationsForOutput() call was removed because it caused excessive unparsing in certain transformation scenarios. This may affect the completeness of subtree marking in some cases.
Note
This function contains legacy code paths guarded by if 0 preprocessor directives that are pending cleanup.
If the node has no associated Sg_File_Info, a diagnostic message is printed but the transformation and output flags are still set on the located node.
Precondition
The node parameter should point to a valid SgNode in the AST, or be NULL.
Postcondition
If node is a valid SgLocatedNode, it will have its transformation flag set and will be marked for output in code generation. The physical file ID will be set if file info is available.

◆ markSubtreeToBeUnparsed()

void SageInterface::markSubtreeToBeUnparsed ( SgNode * root,
int physical_file_id )

Marks an entire subtree of AST nodes to be unparsed.

This function traverses the entire subtree rooted at the specified node and marks each node within the subtree to be unparsed. It uses the RoseAst iterator to perform a traversal of all nodes in the subtree, applying the markNodeToBeUnparsed function to each visited node. This is useful when modifications have been made to a portion of the AST and the corresponding source code needs to be regenerated during the unparsing phase.

The function iterates through all descendants of the root node using the RoseAst traversal mechanism, which provides a convenient way to visit all nodes in the abstract syntax tree rooted at the given node.

Parameters
rootPointer to the root node of the subtree that should be marked for unparsing. All nodes in this subtree, including the root itself, will be marked.
physical_file_idThe identifier of the physical file associated with the unparsing operation. This ID is passed to each call of markNodeToBeUnparsed to associate the nodes with the correct output file.
Precondition
root must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgNode in a well-formed AST.
physical_file_id should be a valid file identifier recognized by the unparsing infrastructure.
Postcondition
All nodes in the subtree rooted at root are marked to be unparsed with the specified physical_file_id.
Note
This function relies on the RoseAst iterator for tree traversal, which visits nodes in a depth-first manner.
The marking affects how the unparser generates output code for the affected nodes.
Warning
If root is null, the behavior depends on the RoseAst iterator implementation and may result in undefined behavior.
See also
markNodeToBeUnparsed
RoseAst

◆ markSubtreeToBeUnparsedTreeTraversal()

void SageInterface::markSubtreeToBeUnparsedTreeTraversal ( SgNode * root,
int physical_file_id )

Marks nodes in a subtree to be unparsed while avoiding marking subtrees of SgCastExp nodes.

This function traverses an AST subtree rooted at the given node and marks each node to be unparsed, with special handling for cast expressions. The function uses a top-down tree traversal pattern with an inherited attribute to track whether the current node is within a cast expression subtree.

The key behavior is that nodes within SgCastExp subtrees are intentionally not marked as transformations. This is important because marking an implicit cast as a transformation would cause it to be unparsed even though it is marked as implicit. The precedence of implicit flags over transformation flags is a known issue that this function works around.

The implementation defines a local InheritedAttribute class to carry the physical file ID and a boolean flag indicating whether the traversal is currently within a cast subtree. A local SubtreeTraversal class inherits from SgTopDownProcessing and implements the evaluateInheritedAttribute method to perform the actual marking logic.

Parameters
rootPointer to the root node of the AST subtree to be traversed and marked. This node and all its descendants (except those within SgCastExp subtrees) will be marked for unparsing.
physical_file_idThe file identifier used when marking nodes for unparsing. This ID is passed to markNodeToBeUnparsed for each eligible node.
Warning
This function only compiles with GNU GCC version 5.0 or newer. When compiled with GNU 4.9 or older compilers, the function prints a warning message and performs no operation. This limitation is due to local class usage with template inheritance not being fully supported in older compiler versions.
SgCastExp nodes themselves are not marked as transformations, not just their children. This is intentional behavior to prevent implicit casts from being unparsed.
Precondition
The root parameter should point to a valid SgNode within a properly constructed AST.
The physical_file_id should be a valid file identifier recognized by the unparsing system.
Postcondition
All nodes in the subtree rooted at root, except those within SgCastExp subtrees, are marked to be unparsed with the specified physical_file_id.
Nodes within SgCastExp subtrees remain unchanged.
Note
This function was implemented as part of debugging issues related to the precedence of implicit flags over transformation flags in the unparsing system.
The function uses preprocessor conditionals based on GNUC and GNUC_MINOR to handle compiler version compatibility.
Debug printf statements are present but disabled via if 0 preprocessor directives.

◆ mergeAssignmentWithDeclaration()

bool SageInterface::mergeAssignmentWithDeclaration ( SgExprStatement * assign_stmt,
SgVariableDeclaration * decl,
bool removeAssignStmt = true )

Merges an assignment statement with a variable declaration by converting the assignment into an initializer.

This function combines a separate assignment statement of the form "var = expr;" with its corresponding variable declaration, transforming the declaration to include an initializer. For example, it converts: int x; x = 5; into: int x = 5;

The function performs several sanity checks before attempting the merge:

  1. The assignment statement must be a simple assignment operation (var = expr)
  2. The left-hand side of the assignment must be a variable reference
  3. The variable declaration must not already have an initializer
  4. The variable in the assignment must match the declared variable (by symbol or name)

When merging, the function copies the right-hand side expression from the assignment, preserves preprocessing information (comments, directives) from the assignment statement by moving them to the declaration, optionally removes the original assignment statement, and creates an assign initializer for the declaration.

Parameters
assign_stmtPointer to the assignment expression statement to be merged. Must be a valid SgExprStatement containing an SgAssignOp with a variable reference on the left-hand side.
declPointer to the variable declaration that will receive the initializer. Must be a valid SgVariableDeclaration without an existing initializer.
removeAssignStmtFlag indicating whether to remove the assignment statement after merging. Defaults to true. Set to false if the caller needs to handle removal manually, such as when the statement is not yet in a container.
Returns
True if the merge was successful, false if any of the sanity checks failed (invalid assignment form, mismatched variables, or existing initializer).
Precondition
assign_stmt must not be NULL.
decl must not be NULL.
The assignment statement must contain an SgAssignOp expression.
The left-hand side of the assignment must be an SgVarRefExp.
The declaration must not already have an initializer.
Postcondition
If successful, the declaration will have an SgAssignInitializer containing a copy of the right-hand side expression from the assignment.
If successful and removeAssignStmt is true, the original assignment statement will be removed from its enclosing scope.
Preprocessing information from the assignment statement is moved to the declaration.
Note
The function handles the case where the declaration has not yet been inserted into its scope by falling back to name comparison when the symbol cannot be found.
The right-hand side expression is copied rather than moved, so the original expression in the assignment statement remains intact until the statement is removed.
Preprocessing information is appended (not prepended) to preserve the ordering of comments between the declaration and assignment statement.
Warning
The removeStatement function does not support removing statements that are not inside a container. Use removeAssignStmt=false and handle removal manually in such cases.

◆ mergeDeclarationAndAssignment()

bool SageInterface::mergeDeclarationAndAssignment ( SgVariableDeclaration * decl,
SgExprStatement * assign_stmt,
bool removeAssignStmt )

Merges a variable declaration with a subsequent assignment statement.

This function combines a variable declaration and an assignment statement into a single initialized declaration. It serves as a convenience wrapper that delegates to mergeAssignmentWithDeclaration with the parameters in a different order. This transformation is useful for code simplification and optimization passes where separate declaration and initialization can be combined into a single statement.

For example, this can transform: int x; x = 5; into: int x = 5;

Parameters
declPointer to the variable declaration statement that will receive the initializer from the assignment statement.
assign_stmtPointer to the expression statement containing the assignment whose right-hand side will become the initializer for the declaration.
removeAssignStmtFlag indicating whether the assignment statement should be removed from the AST after the merge operation. Defaults to true.
Returns
True if the merge operation was successful, false otherwise.
Precondition
decl must be a valid pointer to an SgVariableDeclaration node.
assign_stmt must be a valid pointer to an SgExprStatement containing an assignment expression.
The variable being assigned in assign_stmt should correspond to the variable declared in decl.
Postcondition
If successful and removeAssignStmt is true, the assignment statement is removed from the AST.
If successful, the declaration contains the initializer from the assignment.
Note
This function is a wrapper around mergeAssignmentWithDeclaration with swapped parameter order for convenience.
Warning
Passing null pointers for decl or assign_stmt may result in undefined behavior.

◆ mergeDeclarationWithAssignment()

bool SageInterface::mergeDeclarationWithAssignment ( SgVariableDeclaration * decl,
SgExprStatement * assign_stmt )

Merges a variable declaration with a subsequent assignment statement into a single initialized declaration.

This function combines a variable declaration that has no initializer with an assignment statement that assigns a value to the same variable. The result is a single variable declaration with an initializer, effectively transforming code patterns like: 

int x;
x = 5;

into: 

int x = 5;

The implementation performs the following steps:

  1. Validates that the assignment statement is of the form var = expression
  2. Validates that the declaration has no existing initializer
  3. Verifies that both statements refer to the same variable (by symbol or name)
  4. Copies the right-hand side of the assignment to create an initializer for the declaration
  5. Moves preprocessing information from the declaration to the next statement
  6. Relocates the declaration to the position of the assignment statement
  7. Preserves preprocessing information from the assignment statement
  8. Removes the original assignment statement
Parameters
declPointer to the variable declaration statement to be merged. Must not be NULL and must not already have an initializer.
assign_stmtPointer to the assignment expression statement to be merged. Must not be NULL and must be of the form variable = expression where the left-hand side is a simple variable reference.
Returns
True if the merge operation was successful, false if the merge could not be performed due to validation failures such as mismatched variables, existing initializer, or incompatible statement forms.
Precondition
decl is not NULL.
assign_stmt is not NULL.
The assignment statement must have an SgAssignOp as its expression.
The left-hand side of the assignment must be an SgVarRefExp.
The declaration must not have an existing initializer.
The variable in the assignment must match the variable in the declaration.
Postcondition
If successful, the declaration is moved to the position of the assignment statement and contains an initializer with the right-hand side of the original assignment.
If successful, the original assignment statement is removed from the AST.
Preprocessing information is preserved and appropriately relocated.
Note
During translation, the declaration may not yet be inserted into its scope, causing symbol lookup to return NULL. In such cases, the function falls back to comparing variable names instead of symbols.
The function uses SageInterface::removeStatement which does not support removing statements that are not inside a container. Users may need to handle such cases separately.
Warning
The function modifies the AST by moving and removing statements. Ensure that any iterators or references to the affected statements are updated accordingly.

◆ moveCommentsToNewStatement()

void SageInterface::moveCommentsToNewStatement ( SgStatement * sourceStatement,
const vector< int > & indexList,
SgStatement * destinationStatement,
bool destinationStatementProceedsSourceStatement )

Moves selected preprocessing comments from a source statement to a destination statement.

This function transfers preprocessing information (comments, directives) from a source statement to a destination statement based on a list of indices specifying which comments to move. The function handles the relative positioning of comments appropriately depending on whether the destination statement precedes or follows the source statement in the code.

The algorithm adjusts the relative position of each comment being moved:

  • When the destination precedes the source (or destination is SgGlobal), comments marked as "before" are changed to "after" position. For scope statements that are ancestors of the source, comments are set to "inside" position for C/C++ languages.
  • When the destination follows the source, comments marked as "after" or "end_of" are changed to "before" position. Comments are prepended to maintain their original order relative to any existing comments on the destination statement.

Special handling is provided for SgGlobal as a destination, treating it as an enclosing scope rather than a preceding statement to avoid comments appearing at the end of the file.

After moving comments to the destination, the function removes the transferred entries from the source statement by marking them as NULL and then erasing the NULL entries.

Parameters
sourceStatementPointer to the statement from which comments will be moved. Must not be NULL and must have valid attached preprocessing information.
indexListA vector of indices specifying which comments in the source statement's attached preprocessing info list should be moved to the destination.
destinationStatementPointer to the statement to which comments will be moved. Must not be NULL and must have valid file info.
destinationStatementProceedsSourceStatementBoolean flag indicating the relative position of statements. True if the destination statement appears before the source statement in the code, false otherwise.
Warning
The function modifies both the source and destination statements' attached preprocessing information in place.
For ifdef, ifndef, if directives, there is a known corner case where matching endif may not be found if the directive spans a wide range of code.
Precondition
sourceStatement must be a valid non-NULL pointer to an SgStatement.
destinationStatement must be a valid non-NULL pointer to an SgStatement with valid file info.
All indices in indexList must be valid indices into the source statement's attached preprocessing info list.
The attached preprocessing info on sourceStatement must not be NULL if indexList is non-empty.
Postcondition
The comments specified by indexList are attached to destinationStatement with appropriate relative positions.
The corresponding entries are removed from sourceStatement's preprocessing info list.
The order of moved comments is preserved relative to each other.
Note
This function is particularly useful when removing or relocating statements while preserving associated comments and preprocessor directives.
For C/C++ languages, when the destination is an ancestor scope of the source, comments are attached with "inside" position to ensure proper unparsing.
The function uses an anchor-based insertion strategy to maintain comment order when prepending to existing comments on the destination statement.

◆ moveDeclarationToAssociatedNamespace()

void SageInterface::moveDeclarationToAssociatedNamespace ( SgDeclarationStatement * declarationStatement)

Relocates a declaration statement to be explicitly represented in its associated namespace.

This function moves a declaration statement to its associated namespace scope, which is required for some backend compilers to properly process template instantiations. This is particularly necessary for the GNU g++ compiler, which does not permit name qualification to express the namespace where a template instantiation should be placed. Such name qualification would sometimes require global qualification, which is also not allowed by GNU g++ compiler versions 4.4 through 4.8.

The function identifies the previous and next statements relative to the given declaration in order to properly close off the current namespace and potentially reopen it. It handles several cases including the most common case where both previous and next statements exist, the case where only a previous statement exists (last template instantiation in global scope), and edge cases where statements may be missing.

If the declaration is associated with a namespace definition, the function prepares to move the declaration from its current parent scope to the appropriate namespace. Declarations not associated with a namespace do not require wrapping.

Parameters
declarationStatementPointer to the declaration statement that needs to be moved to its associated namespace. Must not be NULL.
Warning
This function will call ROSE_ABORT() in several corner cases that are not yet fully implemented, including when there is no previous statement or when both previous and next statements are NULL.
The implementation appears to be incomplete, with several code paths leading to ROSE_ABORT() calls marked as tests for handling corner cases.
Precondition
The declarationStatement parameter must be a valid pointer to an SgDeclarationStatement.
The declaration statement should be part of a valid AST with proper parent and scope relationships.
Postcondition
If successful, the declaration statement will be repositioned to be explicitly represented within its associated namespace in the AST.
Note
This function is specifically designed to support general unparsing of template instantiations for the GNU g++ compiler.
Some edge cases are not fully handled and will result in program termination via ROSE_ABORT().

◆ moveForStatementIncrementIntoBody()

void SageInterface::moveForStatementIncrementIntoBody ( SgForStatement * f)

Moves the increment expression of a for-loop into the loop body.

This function transforms a for-loop by relocating its increment expression from the for-statement header into the loop body as the final statement. This transformation is useful for certain loop normalizations or when preparing loops for specific optimizations that require the increment to be explicitly visible within the loop body.

The transformation process involves the following steps:

  1. Check if the increment expression is null; if so, no action is taken.
  2. Create an expression statement from the current increment expression.
  3. Update the parent pointer of the increment expression to the new statement.
  4. Add the new increment statement to the end of the loop body using addStepToLoopBody.
  5. Replace the original increment in the for-statement header with a null expression.
  6. Set the parent of the null expression to the for-statement.
Parameters
fPointer to the SgForStatement whose increment expression should be moved into the loop body. Must not be NULL.
Precondition
The parameter f must point to a valid SgForStatement node.
The for-statement must have a properly initialized loop body.
Postcondition
If the original increment was not a null expression, it is now the last statement in the loop body.
The for-statement increment slot contains a null expression.
All parent pointers are correctly updated to maintain AST consistency.
Note
If the for-statement already has a null increment expression, the function returns immediately without making any modifications.
This function uses SageBuilder to construct new AST nodes and SageInterface::addStepToLoopBody to properly insert the increment statement at the end of the loop body.
Warning
The caller must ensure that the for-statement pointer is valid and that the AST is in a consistent state before calling this function.

◆ movePreprocessingInfo()

void SageInterface::movePreprocessingInfo ( SgStatement * stmt_src,

Moves preprocessing information (comments and CPP directives) from one statement to another.

This function transfers attached preprocessing information such as comments (C-style, C++, Fortran) and C preprocessor directives (include, define, undef, ifdef, ifndef, if, else, elif, endif, pragma, line, error, warning) from a source statement to a destination statement. The function supports filtering by relative position and allows control over whether the moved items are prepended or appended to the destination statement's preprocessing info list.

The implementation iterates through all preprocessing info items attached to the source statement, filters them based on the source position parameter (if specified), and transfers matching items to the destination statement. Items are marked as transformations to support token-based unparsing. The function also handles C linkage specification markers (extern "C" start and end).

When usePrepend is true, the function maintains the original order of directives by tracking the previously inserted item and inserting subsequent items after it. This ensures that a sequence of CPP directives maintains their relative ordering after the move.

stmt_srcPointer to the source statement from which preprocessing information will be moved. Must not be NULL.
stmt_dstPointer to the destination statement to which preprocessing information will be moved. Must not be NULL and must not share the same preprocessing info list as stmt_src.
src_positionThe relative position filter for source preprocessing info. If set to PreprocessingInfo::undef, all preprocessing info is considered for moving. Otherwise, only info matching this position is moved.
dst_positionThe relative position to assign to moved preprocessing info at the destination. If set to PreprocessingInfo::undef, the original position is preserved.
usePrependIf true, preprocessing info is prepended to the destination (inserted before existing info while maintaining order). If false, info is appended after existing info.
Warning
The source and destination statements must not share the same attached preprocessing info list, as this would cause iterator invalidation during the move operation.
Precondition
stmt_src is not NULL.
stmt_dst is not NULL.
The attached preprocessing info list of stmt_src and stmt_dst must be distinct objects (not the same pointer).
Postcondition
All matching preprocessing info items are removed from stmt_src and added to stmt_dst.
Moved preprocessing info items are marked as transformations via setAsTransformation().
The destination statement has containsTransformationToSurroundingWhitespace set to true.
The isModified flag of stmt_dst is preserved if it was not already set before the call.
Note
If the source statement has no attached preprocessing info (NULL list), the function returns immediately without performing any operations.
This function is designed to work with token-based unparsing, which requires special handling of the isModified flag to avoid incorrect whitespace handling.

Moves statements from an Ada package body to a namespace definition and creates alias symbols.

This function facilitates the transfer of statements between an Ada package body and a C++ namespace definition statement. Second, it creates alias symbols in the global definition associated with the target namespace declaration. This function is particularly useful during Ada-to-C++ translation or when restructuring Ada code representations within the ROSE compiler infrastructure.

◆ moveUpInnerDanglingIfEndifDirective()

int SageInterface::moveUpInnerDanglingIfEndifDirective ( SgLocatedNode * lnode)

Moves unbalanced preprocessor directives from within a subtree to be attached after the root node.

This function identifies and relocates dangling or unbalanced preprocessor conditional directives (if, ifdef, ifndef, else, elif, endif) that exist within the subtree rooted at the given located node. The algorithm uses a stack-based approach (simulated with a vector) to match begin directives with their corresponding end directives. Directives that cannot be matched (i.e., dangling directives) are collected and moved to be attached after the root node.

The algorithm works in the following steps:

  1. Performs a pre-order traversal to collect all preprocessing info from the subtree, excluding those attached directly to the root node (depth 0).
  2. Uses a stack-based matching algorithm where begin directives (if, ifdef, ifndef) are pushed onto the stack, and end directives (endif) attempt to neutralize matching begin directives.
  3. Middle directives (else, elif) are associated with their corresponding begin directives when balanced, or treated as unbalanced keepers otherwise.
  4. All unbalanced directives (keepers) are moved to be attached after the root node with their relative position set to "after".
  5. Original locations are nullified and cleaned up.
Parameters
lnodePointer to the located node representing the root of the subtree to process. This node will receive the relocated preprocessor directives attached after it.
Returns
The number of preprocessor directives that were moved to the new location.
Precondition
lnode must not be NULL.
lnode must be a valid SgLocatedNode with properly attached preprocessing information.
Postcondition
All dangling preprocessor directives from within the subtree are attached after lnode.
The original preprocessing info entries that were moved are removed from their original containers.
The relative position of all moved directives is set to PreprocessingInfo::after.
Warning
This function modifies the preprocessing information attached to nodes within the subtree. The original attachment locations will have their moved entries nullified and then erased.
Note
The function uses an internal map (infoMap) to track depth, index, and container information for each preprocessing info object encountered during traversal.
Middle directives (else, elif) are specially handled to maintain their association with their corresponding begin directives during the move operation.
The function processes associated middle directives in reverse order when moving them to preserve correct directive ordering.

This function relocates an existing variable declaration statement from its current scope to a new target scope within the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). The function handles different target scope types with specialized logic:

For SgBasicBlock targets, the declaration is simply prepended to the block.

For SgForStatement targets, the function transforms the declaration to become part of the for loop's initialization statement. It expects a pattern where the for loop has a single initialization statement of the form i=0, and it merges the variable declaration with this initializer to produce a declaration like int i=0 in the for loop header.

The function also ensures that the associated variable symbol is properly moved from the original scope's symbol table to the target scope's symbol table, updating the initialized name's scope reference accordingly.

For SgForStatement targets, only a single initialization statement is currently supported. More complex initialization patterns will cause an assertion failure.
The function will trigger an assertion failure if an unsupported target scope type is provided.
Any scope adjustment for special cases like SgIfStmt should be performed before calling this function.
Precondition
decl is not NULL.
target_scope is not NULL.
target_scope differs from the current scope of decl.
For SgForStatement targets, the for loop must have exactly one initialization statement that is an expression statement containing an assignment operation.
Postcondition
The declaration is removed from its original scope and inserted into the target scope.
The variable symbol is relocated from the original scope's symbol table to the target scope's symbol table.
The initialized name's scope reference is updated to the target scope.
The symbol exists in the target scope's symbol table.
Note
This function uses SageInterface::removeStatement to detach the declaration and SageInterface::prependStatement for basic block insertion.
For for-loop targets, the original initialization expression statement is deep deleted after extracting its right-hand side value.
The function relies on SageInterface::fixVariableDeclaration behavior but manually handles symbol table updates since fixVariableDeclaration does not properly switch scopes for initialized names.

The algorithm first identifies the parent statement, then determines the appropriate removal strategy based on whether the parent is a basic block, a for-loop initializer, or another statement type. When this pattern is found (i.e., (&var)->member), the function transforms it into an equivalent dot expression (var.member).

The transformation is performed by creating a new SgDotExp with deep copies of the operands and replacing the original arrow expression. The function uses a reverse iterator for safer traversal during transformation and maintains a visited map to handle cases where subtrees may be shared (particularly relevant for the jovial2cpp translator which generates multiple source file ASTs that may share subtrees).

The AST must be well-formed with proper parent-child relationships.

The original arrow expressions that were transformed are no longer part of the AST.
Warning
This function modifies the AST in place. The original arrow expressions are replaced and may be deallocated.
If the root is NULL, the function will trigger an assertion failure.

◆ normalizeForLoopIncrement()

bool SageInterface::normalizeForLoopIncrement ( SgForStatement * loop)

Normalizes the increment expression of a for-loop to use the plus-assign operator.

This function transforms various forms of loop increment expressions into a canonical form using the plus-assign operator (+=). The normalization converts:

  • i++ to i += 1
  • i– to i += -1
  • i -= s to i += -s

The function first validates that the loop's test expression is a binary operation with a variable reference on the left-hand side. It then checks that the increment expression operates on the same variable as the test condition before performing the transformation. Expressions that are already in the form of SgAssignOp or SgPlusAssignOp are left unchanged and considered successfully normalized.

Parameters
loopPointer to the SgForStatement representing the for-loop to be normalized. Must not be NULL.
Returns
True if the increment expression was successfully normalized or was already in an acceptable form (assignment or plus-assign). Returns false if the loop structure does not meet the requirements for normalization, such as when the test expression is not a binary operation, the loop variable cannot be identified, or the increment expression uses an unsupported form.
Precondition
The loop parameter must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgForStatement.
The for-loop must have a test expression that is a binary operation with a variable reference on the left-hand side.
Postcondition
If the function returns true and the increment was transformed, the original increment expression is replaced with an equivalent plus-assign expression.
The loop variable in the increment expression matches the variable in the test expression's left-hand side.
Note
This function uses deep copying when creating replacement expressions to ensure proper AST node ownership.
The function handles type casting by using SkipCasting to look through cast expressions when identifying variable references.
Increment expressions of type SgAssignOp and SgPlusAssignOp are considered already normalized and are not modified.

◆ normalizeForLoopInitDeclaration()

bool SageInterface::normalizeForLoopInitDeclaration ( SgForStatement * loop)

Promotes a variable declaration from a for loop's init statement to the enclosing function scope.

This function normalizes for loop initialization statements by extracting variable declarations from the loop header and placing them at the beginning of the enclosing function body. For example, a loop of the form "for (int i=0; ...)" is transformed into "int i_x; for (i_x=0; ...)". This normalization is useful for various loop transformations and analyses that require the loop index variable to be declared outside the loop scope.

The algorithm performs the following steps:

  1. Validates that the loop has exactly one init statement that is a variable declaration
  2. Extracts the variable name, type, and initial value from the declaration
  3. Creates a new variable declaration with a potentially modified name to avoid collisions
  4. Prepends the new declaration to the enclosing function body
  5. Updates all references to the original variable within the loop to use the new symbol
  6. Replaces the original declaration in the loop header with an assignment statement
  7. Records the transformation for potential later reversal
Parameters
loopPointer to the SgForStatement node representing the for loop to be normalized. Must not be NULL.
Returns
True if the normalization was successful or if the loop was already normalized (no variable declaration in init statement). False if the loop has multiple init statements, or if the declaration uses a complex initializer that cannot be handled.
Warning
The function modifies the AST in place. The original variable declaration is removed from the loop header and a new declaration is inserted at the function scope level.
The return value is ambiguous when the init statement is not a variable declaration: it returns true indicating the loop is already normalized, but this may not reflect the actual normalization status.
Precondition
The loop parameter must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgForStatement node.
The loop must be contained within a function definition with a valid body.
Postcondition
If successful, a new variable declaration is prepended to the enclosing function body.
All variable references to the original loop index within the loop are updated to reference the new variable symbol.
The transformation is recorded in trans_records.forLoopInitNormalizationTable and trans_records.forLoopInitNormalizationRecord for potential later reversal.
Note
Only handles for loops with exactly one init statement that is a simple variable declaration with an assign initializer (e.g., int i = 0).
Complex initializers such as SgConstructorInitializer are not supported and will cause the function to return false.
If a variable with the same name already exists in the visible scope, a suffix "_nom_" followed by a counter is appended to avoid name collisions.
The original declaration and new declaration pair are stored for potential undo operations.

◆ normalizeForLoopTest()

bool SageInterface::normalizeForLoopTest ( SgForStatement * loop)

Normalizes the test expression of a for-loop to use inclusive comparison operators.

This function transforms the test condition of a for-loop to use normalized comparison operators. Specifically, it converts strict inequality operators to their inclusive equivalents by adjusting the right-hand side operand:

  • Less-than (i < x) is converted to less-than-or-equal (i <= x - 1)
  • Greater-than (i > x) is converted to greater-than-or-equal (i >= x + 1)

The normalization process requires that the test expression is a binary comparison operation with a variable reference on the left-hand side. Expressions that are already normalized (using <=, >=, or !=) are left unchanged but still return success. The function handles casting on the left-hand side operand by skipping through cast expressions to find the underlying variable reference.

Parameters
loopPointer to the SgForStatement representing the for-loop whose test expression is to be normalized. Must not be NULL.
Returns
True if the normalization was successful or if the test expression was already in a normalized form (<=, >=, or !=). Returns false if the test expression is not a binary operation, if the left-hand side is not a variable reference, if the variable symbol cannot be obtained, or if the comparison operator is not one of the recognized types.
Precondition
The loop parameter must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgForStatement.
The for-loop should have a valid test expression that is a binary comparison.
Postcondition
If successful and the original operator was < or >, the test expression is replaced with an equivalent <= or >= expression respectively, with the right-hand side adjusted by 1.
The original test expression is deleted and replaced in the AST.
Note
The function uses deepCopy to create new AST nodes for the replacement expression, ensuring proper memory management.
The replaceExpression function handles deletion of the original test expression by default.
Not-equal comparisons (!=) are currently accepted but not transformed, which may need reconsideration for certain use cases.
Warning
The function modifies the AST in place. Ensure that any references to the original test expression are updated accordingly.

Outputs the global function type symbol table to standard output.

This function prints the contents of the global function type symbol table maintained by ROSE. The global function type table is constructed during the EDG/Sage translation phase and initially contains EDG names for all instantiated templates. In a subsequent AST fixup phase, the table is rebuilt to use modified template names, which are mangled names derived from the modified template names used in Sage III.

The function retrieves the global function type table from SgNode and invokes its print_functypetable method to display the table contents. This is primarily useful for debugging and inspection of the internal function type symbol table state.

This function will trigger an assertion failure if the global function type table has not been properly initialized.

It is designed to be used in combination with cutPreprocessingInfo() to facilitate moving preprocessing information (such as comments and preprocessor directives) between nodes in the ROSE AST.

The function handles different relative positions for attaching the preprocessing information. When the position is "before", the saved items are inserted at the beginning of the destination node's preprocessing info list in reverse order to maintain the original ordering. When the position is "after", the items are appended to the end using standard copy with back_inserter. The "inside" position is partially implemented but not fully supported, and will produce a warning message to standard error.

The implementation accounts for the use of std::vector instead of std::list for the AttachedPreprocessingInfoType, which requires different insertion strategies since vectors do not support front_inserter.

Parameters
dst_nodePointer to the destination SgLocatedNode where the preprocessing information will be pasted. Must be a valid non-null pointer to a located node in the AST.
posThe relative position specifying where to attach the preprocessing information on the destination node. Valid values are PreprocessingInfo::before, PreprocessingInfo::after, and PreprocessingInfo::inside (though inside is not fully supported).
save_bufReference to the buffer containing the saved preprocessing information to be pasted. This buffer is typically populated by a prior call to cutPreprocessingInfo().
Warning
The PreprocessingInfo::inside position is not fully supported. Using this position will result in a warning message being printed to standard error, and the first item's information will be displayed for debugging purposes.
Precondition
dst_node must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgLocatedNode.
save_buf should contain preprocessing information previously saved, typically via cutPreprocessingInfo().
Postcondition
If save_buf is non-empty, the preprocessing information from save_buf is attached to dst_node at the specified relative position.
The dst_node's preprocessing info list is created if it does not exist.
Note
If save_buf is empty, the function returns immediately without performing any operations.
This function is intended to be used as a counterpart to cutPreprocessingInfo() for moving preprocessing information between AST nodes.

Prepends a statement to the beginning of an SgForInitStatement.

This function inserts a given statement at the beginning of the initialization statement list within an SgForInitStatement node. Before performing the insertion, the function updates internal data structures to handle cases where the statement being moved may be associated with macro expansions. This ensures that any macro expansion associations are properly marked as transformations when statements are relocated within the AST.

The function performs two internal map resets: one for the statement being inserted to handle its potential macro expansion associations, and one for the target for-init statement to ensure proper handling of macro expansions at the insertion location.

Parameters
stmtPointer to the SgStatement to be prepended to the for-init statement. Must not be NULL.
for_init_stmtPointer to the SgForInitStatement where the statement will be prepended. Must not be NULL.
Precondition
stmt must not be NULL.
for_init_stmt must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The statement stmt is inserted at the beginning of the initialization statement list in for_init_stmt.
Internal maps are updated to reflect the statement movement and any associated macro expansions are marked as transformations.
Note
This function calls resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement on both the statement being inserted and the target for-init statement to properly handle macro expansion tracking.
Warning
The function will trigger an assertion failure if either stmt or for_init_stmt is NULL.

◆ prependStatement() [2/2]

void SageInterface::prependStatement ( SgStatement * stmt,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Prepends a statement to the beginning of a specified scope.

This function inserts a given statement at the beginning of a scope statement. If no scope is explicitly provided, the function uses the top of the scope stack maintained by SageBuilder. Before insertion, the function performs necessary fixups on the statement to ensure it is properly configured for the target scope. Additionally, the function handles internal map updates for statements that may be associated with macro expansions, ensuring that moved statements are properly tracked and any associated macro expansion statements are marked as transformations.

The implementation performs the following steps:

  1. Validates the statement and determines the target scope
  2. Fixes the statement for the target scope using fixStatement()
  3. Resets internal maps for both the statement and scope to handle macro expansion tracking
  4. Inserts the statement into the scope at the beginning position
  5. Sets the parent relationship between the statement and scope
  6. Updates defining and non-defining links for function declarations when not in frontend construction mode
Parameters
stmtPointer to the statement to be prepended. Must not be NULL.
scopePointer to the scope statement where the statement will be prepended. If NULL, the top of the SageBuilder scope stack will be used as the target scope.
Precondition
The stmt parameter must not be NULL.
If scope is NULL, the SageBuilder scope stack must not be empty.
Postcondition
The statement is inserted at the beginning of the specified scope.
The statement's parent is set to the scope.
Internal maps are updated to reflect the statement's new location.
For function declarations, defining and non-defining links are updated unless in frontend construction mode.
Note
This function has similar behavior to SageBuilder::appendStatement() but inserts at the beginning rather than the end of the scope.
When the source position classification mode is e_sourcePositionFrontendConstruction, the expensive fixup for function declaration links is skipped since the AST is already properly constructed by the frontend.
The function handles macro expansion tracking by resetting internal maps for both the statement being inserted and the target scope.
Warning
The caller must ensure that the statement is valid and compatible with the target scope type.

void SageInterface::prependStatementList ( const std::vector< SgStatement * > & stmts,

Prepends a list of statements to the beginning of a scope in reverse order.

This function inserts multiple statements at the beginning of a specified scope statement. The statements are processed in reverse order (from last to first in the input vector) so that after all insertions are complete, the statements appear in the same order as they were provided in the input vector. Each statement is prepended individually using the prependStatement function, which handles the actual insertion into the scope's statement list.

The algorithm iterates through the vector from the end to the beginning, calling prependStatement for each element. This ensures that the first element of the input vector ends up as the first statement in the scope after all prepend operations are completed.

Parameters
stmtsA vector of pointers to SgStatement objects to be prepended to the scope. The statements will appear in the scope in the same order as they appear in this vector. The vector may be empty, in which case no modifications are made to the scope.
scopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement where the statements will be prepended. This scope will contain the new statements at its beginning after the operation completes.
Precondition
The scope pointer must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgScopeStatement.
All statement pointers in the stmts vector should be valid and non-null.
The statements in stmts should not already be attached to another scope without proper handling.
Postcondition
All statements from stmts are inserted at the beginning of scope in their original order.
The parent of each inserted statement is set to the specified scope.
Note
This function relies on prependStatement for individual statement insertion, which handles updating parent pointers and maintaining AST consistency.
If the input vector is empty, the function completes without modifying the scope.
Warning
Passing a null scope pointer may result in undefined behavior.
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the statements are compatible with the target scope type.

The function internally uses the serialize() helper function to traverse and format the AST structure into a string representation, which is then printed to the console.

The serialization is performed with an empty prefix and label, and the boolean parameter to serialize() is set to false, indicating a specific formatting mode for the output. This function is primarily intended for debugging and diagnostic purposes to inspect the structure of AST nodes.

◆ printAST2TextFile() [1/2]

void SageInterface::printAST2TextFile ( SgNode * node,
const char * filename,
bool printType )

Serializes an AST node and writes its textual representation to a file.

This function takes an AST node and serializes it into a human-readable text format, then writes the output to a specified file. The serialization process converts the tree structure into a string representation that can be used for debugging, analysis, or documentation purposes. Optionally, the function can also append type information by querying the memory pool for all SgType nodes and serializing them as well.

The implementation uses an output string stream to build the serialized representation, then writes the contents to the specified file. When type printing is enabled, the function queries the ROSE memory pool using NodeQuery::queryMemoryPool to find all type nodes (V_SgType variant) and appends their serialized forms to the output file.

Parameters
nodePointer to the SgNode representing the root of the AST subtree to be serialized. This node and all its descendants will be processed.
filenameThe name of the output file where the serialized AST text will be written. The file will be created or overwritten if it already exists.
printTypeA boolean flag indicating whether to append type information to the output file. When true, all SgType nodes from the memory pool are serialized and appended after the main AST content. Defaults to true.
Warning
The output file will be overwritten if it already exists without any warning or confirmation.
If the file cannot be opened for writing, the behavior is undefined as no error checking is performed on the file stream.
Precondition
The node parameter should point to a valid SgNode object in the AST.
The filename parameter should be a valid, non-null path string.
The ROSE memory pool should be properly initialized if printType is true.
Postcondition
A text file is created at the specified filename containing the serialized AST representation.
If printType is true, the file also contains serialized type information from the memory pool.
Note
This function is useful for debugging and understanding the structure of the AST at a particular point in the compilation process.
The serialize function is called internally to perform the actual conversion of AST nodes to text format.

Prints all attached preprocessing information (comments and directives) for a given AST node.

For each attached comment or directive, the function displays the relative position (before, after, inside, etc.), the string content, the number of lines, and the column number of the end of the string.
