◆ querySubTree()

template<typename NodeType>
std::vector< NodeType * > SageInterface::querySubTree ( SgNode * top,
VariantT variant = (VariantT)NodeType::static_variant )

Queries a subtree of the AST and returns all nodes of a specific type.

This function traverses the abstract syntax tree (AST) starting from a given root node and collects all descendant nodes that match the specified variant type. The function leverages NodeQuery::querySubTree to perform the initial query, then casts each resulting node to the requested NodeType using dynamic_cast. This provides a type-safe way to retrieve nodes of a specific type from the AST hierarchy.

The function is templated on NodeType, which should be a class derived from SgNode. By default, the variant parameter is set to the static_variant of the NodeType, allowing automatic type-based filtering without explicit variant specification.

Parameters
topPointer to the root SgNode from which the subtree query begins. This node and all its descendants will be searched for matching nodes.
variantThe VariantT enumeration value specifying which node type to query for. Defaults to NodeType::static_variant, which automatically selects the variant corresponding to the template parameter type.
Returns
A std::vector containing pointers to all nodes of type NodeType found in the subtree rooted at top. The vector will be empty if no matching nodes are found.
Precondition
top must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgNode in a properly constructed AST.
NodeType must be a type derived from SgNode with a valid static_variant member.
Postcondition
All pointers in the returned vector are valid and point to nodes of type NodeType within the queried subtree.
The original AST structure remains unchanged.
Note
The function uses dynamic_cast to ensure type safety. An assertion failure will occur if any node returned by the internal query cannot be cast to NodeType, which would indicate a mismatch between the variant and the template type.
The returned vector owns no memory; the nodes remain part of the AST and should not be deleted through these pointers unless proper AST modification procedures are followed.

◆ rebuildSymbolTable()

void SageInterface::rebuildSymbolTable ( SgScopeStatement * scope)

Rebuilds the symbol table for a given scope statement.

This function reconstructs the symbol table for a specified scope by iterating through all declarations within that scope and creating appropriate symbols for each declaration. It is primarily called from the implementation of copy member functions to ensure that copied AST nodes have properly populated symbol tables.

The function handles various scope types differently:

  • For SgForStatement: Processes variable declarations in initialization and test expressions
  • For SgFunctionDefinition and SgTemplateFunctionDefinition: Adds function parameters and label statements
  • For SgIfStmt, SgSwitchStatement, SgWhileStmt: Handles variable declarations in conditions
  • For SgJavaForEachStatement: Processes the element variable declaration
  • For basic blocks, class definitions, global scope, and namespace definitions: Processes contained statements

The function creates symbols for various declaration types including:

  • Function declarations (regular, member, template, and template instantiation)
  • Variable declarations (including template variables)
  • Class declarations (including template classes and instantiations)
  • Enum declarations and their enumerators
  • Typedef declarations (including template typedefs)
  • Template declarations
  • Namespace declarations and aliases

For declarations that may have multiple forms (defining and non-defining), only one symbol is created to avoid duplicates. Friend declarations are handled specially to avoid inserting symbols into incorrect scopes.

Parameters
scopePointer to the SgScopeStatement for which the symbol table should be rebuilt. Must not be NULL.
Warning
If the symbol table already exists and is non-empty, an assertion failure will occur.
Reaching the default case in the scope type switch statement will cause an abort, indicating an unhandled scope type.
Reaching the default case in the declaration type switch statement will cause an abort, indicating an unhandled declaration type.
Precondition
The scope parameter must not be NULL.
If a symbol table already exists for the scope, it must be empty (size of 0).
Postcondition
The scope will have a valid, non-NULL symbol table.
The symbol table will contain appropriate symbols for all declarations in the scope.
The symbol table's parent will be set to the scope.
Note
This function delegates to several helper functions including supportForVariableDeclarations, supportForVariableLists, supportForLabelStatements, and supportForBaseTypeDefiningDeclaration for handling specific declaration patterns.
For template instantiation member functions declared outside their class scope, the function attempts to add symbols to the correct scope by looking up the associated template declaration.
Certain declaration types such as SgUsingDirectiveStatement, SgPragmaDeclaration, SgTemplateInstantiationDirectiveStatement, SgUsingDeclarationStatement, SgAsmStmt, and SgStaticAssertionDeclaration do not generate symbols in the symbol table.

◆ recordNormalizations()

void SageInterface::recordNormalizations ( SgStatement * s)

Records normalization transformations for token-based unparsing support.

This function records where normalization transformations have been applied to the AST so that denormalizations can be performed as required for token-based unparsing. Token-based unparsing aims to generate minimal diffs by preserving the original source code formatting where possible. By tracking which basic blocks have been added during normalization, the system can later reverse these changes to produce output that more closely matches the original source.

The function extracts the SgBasicBlock from the provided statement and adds it to an internal collection (addedBasicBlockNodes) that tracks all basic blocks introduced through normalization processes.

Parameters
sA pointer to an SgStatement that must be an SgBasicBlock. This represents a basic block that was added during AST normalization and needs to be tracked for potential denormalization.
Warning
The function will trigger an assertion failure if the provided statement is not an SgBasicBlock (i.e., if isSgBasicBlock returns NULL).
Precondition
The parameter s must not be NULL.
The parameter s must be a valid SgBasicBlock node.
Postcondition
The basic block is appended to the addedBasicBlockNodes collection.
The size of addedBasicBlockNodes is incremented by one.
Note
This function was added in version dated 1/18/2015 to support better quality token-based unparsing.
The function modifies the global or class-level container addedBasicBlockNodes.

Recursively prints information about a node and all its ancestors in the AST.

This function traverses the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) from a given node upward to the root, printing diagnostic information about each node along the way. Diagnostic information for the node and all its ancestors has been printed to standard output.
Note
This function prints to standard output (cout) and is primarily intended for debugging purposes.
For SgLocatedNode instances, the unparseToString() method is called but its return value is not actually printed in the current implementation.
Warning
This function uses recursion and may cause stack overflow if the AST depth is extremely large.
The output format includes separator lines and may produce substantial output for nodes deep in the AST hierarchy.

◆ ReductionRecognition()

void SageInterface::ReductionRecognition ( SgForStatement * loop,
std::set< std::pair< SgInitializedName *, OmpSupport::omp_construct_enum > > & results )

Identifies reduction variables and their associated operations within a for loop.

This function performs reduction recognition analysis on a given canonical for loop to detect variables that are used in reduction patterns. Reduction variables are scalar variables that accumulate values across loop iterations using associative and commutative operations such as addition, multiplication, minimum, or maximum.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. First verifies that the input loop is a canonical for loop; if not, the function returns early.
  2. Collects all scalar variable references within the loop body, excluding the loop index variable and locally declared variables.
  3. Groups variable references by their initialized name and counts occurrences.
  4. For variables referenced once, checks if they match single-appearance reduction patterns (e.g., compound assignment operators like +=, *=).
  5. For variables referenced twice, checks for assignment-based reductions (e.g., x = x + expr) or conditional reductions (e.g., if-based min/max patterns).
  6. Successfully identified reduction variables along with their operation types are added to the results set.

The function recognizes common reduction patterns including arithmetic operations and conditional min/max constructs. Variables must be live-in to the loop (not declared within the loop body) to be considered as reduction candidates.

Parameters
loopPointer to the SgForStatement representing the for loop to analyze. Must be a valid canonical for loop for reduction recognition to proceed.
resultsReference to a set that will be populated with pairs of reduction variables and their corresponding reduction operation types. Each pair consists of an SgInitializedName pointer identifying the reduction variable and an OmpSupport::omp_construct_enum value indicating the reduction operation.
Precondition
The loop parameter must point to a valid SgForStatement node in the AST.
The results set should be initialized (may be empty or contain previous results).
Postcondition
If the loop is not canonical, results remains unchanged.
If reduction variables are found, they are inserted into the results set as pairs of variable name and operation type.
Note
This function only processes canonical for loops as determined by isCanonicalForLoop(). Non-canonical loops are silently skipped.
The function currently handles variables referenced at most twice within the loop. More complex reduction patterns with additional references are not recognized.
Future enhancements may include recognition of ternary operator reductions (e.g., maxV = array[i] > maxV ? array[i] : maxV) and function-based reductions (e.g., maxV = max(maxV, array[i])).
Warning
Variables declared within the loop body scope are excluded from reduction analysis, as they do not represent true reductions across iterations.

◆ removeAllOriginalExpressionTrees()

void SageInterface::removeAllOriginalExpressionTrees ( SgNode * top)

Removes all original expression trees from value and cast expressions within an AST subtree.

This function traverses the abstract syntax tree (AST) rooted at the specified node and sets the original expression tree pointer to NULL for all SgValueExp and SgCastExp nodes encountered. The original expression tree is an auxiliary data structure that stores the unparsed representation of expressions before any transformations. By removing these trees, the function ensures that subsequent unparsing operations will use the current expression values rather than cached original representations.

The traversal is performed using a preorder depth-first search strategy via the AstSimpleProcessing visitor pattern. For each node visited, the function checks if it is either a value expression (SgValueExp) or a cast expression (SgCastExp), and if so, clears its original expression tree reference.

Parameters
topPointer to the root node of the AST subtree to process. This node and all its descendants will be visited during the traversal. May be NULL, in which case no traversal occurs.
Warning
This operation is destructive and cannot be undone. Once the original expression trees are removed, the original source representations are lost.
Precondition
The AST rooted at top should be well-formed and properly constructed.
Postcondition
All SgValueExp and SgCastExp nodes within the subtree rooted at top will have their originalExpressionTree pointers set to NULL.
Note
This function is useful when modifying expression values programmatically and needing the unparsed output to reflect the new values rather than the original source code representation.
The function uses a local visitor class that inherits from AstSimpleProcessing to perform the traversal efficiently.

◆ removeConsecutiveLabels()

void SageInterface::removeConsecutiveLabels ( SgNode * top)

Removes consecutive label statements by redirecting goto statements to the last label in a sequence.

This function traverses all goto statements within the subtree rooted at the specified node and optimizes consecutive label statements. When multiple label statements appear consecutively in a basic block, this function updates each goto statement to point to the last label in the sequence rather than an intermediate one. This optimization simplifies the control flow graph by eliminating unnecessary intermediate labels that serve no purpose.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Query all goto statements in the subtree rooted at the given node.
  2. For each goto statement, retrieve its target label statement.
  3. If the label's parent is a basic block, find the label's position in the block's statement list.
  4. Scan forward through consecutive label statements following the target label.
  5. Update the goto statement to point to the last label in the consecutive sequence.
Parameters
topThe root node of the subtree to process. All goto statements within this subtree will be examined and potentially updated. Must be a valid AST node.
Precondition
The parameter top must point to a valid SgNode within a properly constructed AST.
All goto statements within the subtree must have valid label targets.
Postcondition
All goto statements that previously pointed to a label followed by consecutive labels will now point to the last label in that consecutive sequence.
The AST structure remains valid and consistent.
Note
This function only processes goto statements whose target labels have a SgBasicBlock as their parent. Labels with other parent types are skipped.
The function does not remove the intermediate label statements from the AST; it only redirects the goto statements.
Warning
This function modifies the AST in place by changing goto statement targets. Ensure that any dependent analyses or transformations are aware of these changes.

◆ removeConst()

SgType * SageInterface::removeConst ( SgType * t)

Removes a top-level const qualifier from a type, if present.

This function strips the top-level const qualifier from a given ROSE SgType. It handles typedef types by recursively processing the underlying base type until the actual type is reached. For modifier types (SgModifierType), the function creates a deep copy of the type and clears the const flag from its const-volatile modifier, preserving the original type unchanged. If the type does not have a const qualifier or is neither a typedef nor a modifier type, the original type pointer is returned unmodified.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. If the type is a typedef type, recursively call removeConst on the base type.
  2. If the type is a modifier type, create a deep copy, unset the const modifier, and return the modified copy.
  3. Otherwise, return the original type unchanged.
Parameters
tPointer to the SgType from which to remove the const qualifier. May be a typedef type, modifier type, or any other SgType derivative.
Returns
A pointer to an SgType with the top-level const qualifier removed. Returns a new deep-copied type if modification was necessary, or the original type pointer if no const qualifier was present.
Precondition
The parameter t must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgType object.
Postcondition
If the input type had a top-level const qualifier, the returned type will have that qualifier removed. The original type object remains unmodified when a deep copy is created.
Note
This function only removes top-level const qualifiers. Nested const qualifiers (e.g., in pointer-to-const types) are not affected.
When a modifier type is processed, a deep copy is created to avoid modifying the original AST node. The caller may need to manage the memory of the newly created type node.
Warning
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify that the deep copy operation succeeds. If the deep copy fails, the assertion will trigger a program abort in debug builds.

◆ removeJumpsToNextStatement()

void SageInterface::removeJumpsToNextStatement ( SgNode * top)

Removes redundant goto statements that jump to the immediately following label.

This function traverses the AST rooted at the specified node and identifies goto statements within basic blocks that jump to a label statement immediately following them. Such goto statements are redundant because control flow would naturally fall through to the next statement anyway. The function removes these unnecessary jumps to simplify the code structure.

The algorithm works by performing a post-order traversal of the AST. For each basic block encountered, it iterates through the statements looking for goto statements. When a goto is found, it checks if the next statement is a label statement and if that label matches the goto's target. If so, the goto statement is erased from the basic block. The process repeats until no more changes are made within each basic block, ensuring all redundant gotos are removed even if multiple consecutive ones exist.

This function is conditionally compiled and is not available when USE_ROSE is defined.

Parameters
topThe root node of the AST subtree to process. The traversal will visit all nodes under this root, examining basic blocks for redundant goto statements.
Precondition
The parameter top must be a valid pointer to an SgNode within a properly constructed AST.
The AST must be in a consistent state with valid parent-child relationships.
Postcondition
All goto statements that jump to their immediately following label statement within the same basic block will be removed from the AST.
The AST structure remains valid after the transformation.
Note
This function uses an internal visitor class RemoveJumpsToNextStatementVisitor that inherits from AstSimpleProcessing to perform the traversal.
The function modifies the AST in place by erasing statements from basic blocks.
Only goto statements within SgBasicBlock nodes are considered for removal.
This optimization is a form of dead code elimination that simplifies control flow.
Warning
Modifying the AST during traversal requires careful handling. This implementation breaks out of the inner loop after each modification and restarts the scan to avoid iterator invalidation issues.

◆ removeLabeledGotos()

void SageInterface::removeLabeledGotos ( SgNode * top)

Removes redundant label statements that immediately precede goto statements.

This function identifies and eliminates unnecessary label statements in the AST that appear directly before goto statements within basic blocks. When a label statement immediately precedes a goto statement, the label is considered redundant because control flow can be redirected to the goto's target label instead.

The algorithm works in two passes:

  1. First pass: Traverses all goto statements in the subtree and builds a mapping of labels that should be replaced. For each goto statement that is preceded by a label statement within the same basic block, the preceding label is mapped to the goto's target label.
  2. Second pass: Updates all goto statements to point to their final target labels by following the replacement chain until a label with no replacement is found. This handles cases where multiple labels form a chain of redirections.
Parameters
topThe root node of the AST subtree to process. All goto statements within this subtree will be examined and potentially modified.
Precondition
The parameter top must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgNode.
The AST rooted at top must be well-formed with proper parent-child relationships.
Postcondition
All goto statements in the subtree have been updated to bypass any intermediate label statements that were immediately preceding other gotos.
The label replacement mapping ensures that goto targets are resolved to their final destinations, eliminating chains of label redirections.
Note
This function only processes goto statements whose immediate parent is an SgBasicBlock. Goto statements in other contexts are skipped.
The function does not remove the actual label statements from the AST; it only updates goto targets. Separate dead code elimination may be needed to remove the now-unreferenced labels.
The replacement chain resolution in the second pass prevents infinite loops by following the mapping until a fixed point is reached.
Warning
This transformation may affect debugging information and source position mappings in the transformed code.

◆ removeStatement()

void SageInterface::removeStatement ( SgStatement * targetStmt,
bool autoRelocatePreprocessingInfo = true )

Removes a statement from the AST with optional relocation of preprocessing information.

This function removes the specified statement from its parent in the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). When a statement is removed, any attached comments and/or C preprocessor directives (such as ifdef, endif, include) need to be handled appropriately. By default, these preprocessing information items are relocated to a surrounding statement from the same file to preserve their presence in the output.

The algorithm for relocating preprocessing information works as follows:

  1. First, any inner dangling if/endif directives are moved up in the AST.
  2. All attached preprocessing information is collected into a capture list.
  3. A surrounding statement from the same file is identified using findSurroundingStatementFromSameFile().
  4. If a valid surrounding statement is found, the comments and directives are moved to that statement.
  5. If no surrounding statement is found, SgGlobal may be used as the target.

The function also resets internal data structures that may have references to the removed statement, such as macro expansion mappings.

Special handling is applied for SgBasicBlock nodes, where comment relocation is skipped.

Parameters
targetStmtPointer to the statement to be removed from the AST. Must not be null.
autoRelocatePreprocessingInfoFlag indicating whether to automatically relocate attached preprocessing information (comments and CPP directives) to a surrounding statement. Defaults to true. Set to false when the statement is being moved elsewhere and its preprocessing information should travel with it.
Warning
This function is not supported on Microsoft Windows platforms and will abort if called in that environment.
Side effects for symbol tables are not fully considered in this implementation as noted in the TODO comment.
This function is disabled when ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is defined.
Precondition
targetStmt must not be null.
targetStmt must be a removable statement as determined by LowLevelRewrite::isRemovableStatement().
targetStmt must have a valid parent that is an SgStatement for removal to proceed.
Postcondition
The target statement is removed from its parent statement.
If autoRelocatePreprocessingInfo is true and the statement had attached preprocessing information, that information has been moved to a surrounding statement.
Internal maps referencing the target statement have been reset.
Note
SgGlobal cannot be removed from SgFile even though SgFile is the parent of SgGlobal, because SgFile is not a statement.
This functionality is tested by the translator at tests/nonsmoke/functional/roseTests/astInterfaceTests/removeStatementCommentRelocation.C
When relinking AST statements by removing and reattaching elsewhere, set autoRelocatePreprocessingInfo to false so preprocessing information travels with the statement.

◆ removeUnusedLabels()

void SageInterface::removeUnusedLabels ( SgNode * top,
bool keepChild )

Removes all unused labels from a section of code.

This function identifies and removes label statements that are not referenced by any goto statements within the specified code section. It first calls findUnusedLabels to obtain a set of all unused label statements, then iterates through this set to remove each unused label. The function provides two modes of operation: one that preserves the child statement of the label by replacing the label statement with its child, and another that simply removes the entire label statement including any associated child statements.

Parameters
topPointer to the root node of the AST subtree to analyze for unused labels. This node defines the scope within which labels are checked for usage.
keepChildBoolean flag controlling how unused labels are removed. When set to true, the child statement of the label is preserved by replacing the label statement with its child statement. When set to false (the default), the entire label statement is removed using myRemoveStatement. Default value is false.
Precondition
The top parameter must point to a valid SgNode within a properly constructed AST.
The AST must be in a consistent state before calling this function.
Postcondition
All unused label statements within the specified subtree are removed from the AST.
If keepChild is true, child statements of removed labels remain in the AST at the position where the label was located.
If keepChild is false, both the label and its associated statements are removed from the AST.
Note
This function modifies the AST in place. Any pointers to removed label statements will become invalid after this function executes.
The function relies on findUnusedLabels to determine which labels are unused, so the accuracy of removal depends on that function's analysis.
Warning
Removing labels that are actually used by goto statements elsewhere in the program (outside the analyzed subtree) may result in invalid code. Ensure the top parameter encompasses all relevant code that might reference the labels.

◆ replaceDefiningFunctionDeclarationWithFunctionPrototype()

SgFunctionDeclaration * SageInterface::replaceDefiningFunctionDeclarationWithFunctionPrototype ( SgFunctionDeclaration * functionDeclaration)

Replaces a defining function declaration with its corresponding function prototype.

This function takes a defining function declaration (a function with a body) and replaces it in the AST with a non-defining function declaration (a function prototype without a body). The replacement preserves important attributes from the original declaration including declaration modifiers, function modifiers, special function modifiers, linkage specifications, and extern brace settings. The physical file ID is also preserved to ensure proper unparsing.

The function handles the transfer of attached preprocessing information (comments and CPP directives) from the original defining declaration to the new prototype. Template instantiation function declarations are treated specially and are not replaced, as they are not directly from source code.

The implementation uses buildFunctionPrototype to create the new non-defining declaration, then copies relevant modifiers and attributes before calling replaceStatement to perform the actual AST replacement.

Parameters
functionDeclarationPointer to the defining function declaration to be replaced. Must be a valid non-null pointer to an SgFunctionDeclaration that represents a defining declaration (has a function body).
Returns
Pointer to the newly created non-defining function declaration (prototype) that replaced the original defining declaration. Returns NULL if the input is a template instantiation function declaration, as these are not replaced.
Precondition
functionDeclaration must not be NULL.
functionDeclaration should be a defining function declaration with a body.
Postcondition
If successful and not a template instantiation, the original defining declaration is replaced in the AST by the returned prototype.
The returned prototype has the same modifiers and attributes as the original declaration.
Preprocessing information is moved from the original declaration to the new prototype.
The parent pointer of the new prototype is properly set (not NULL).
If the original declaration was static, the returned prototype is also static.
Warning
The original functionDeclaration may have its parent pointer invalidated after this operation. Care should be taken when using the original declaration afterward.
The attached preprocessing info lists of the original and new declarations must be distinct to avoid iterator invalidation issues.
Note
Template instantiation function declarations (SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl) are not processed by this function and will result in a NULL return value.
The movePreprocessingInfo flag is set to true by default when calling replaceStatement, ensuring comments and CPP directives are transferred to the new prototype.

◆ replaceExpression()

void SageInterface::replaceExpression ( SgExpression * oldExp,
SgExpression * newExp,
bool keepOldExp )

Replaces an expression in the AST with a new expression.

This function substitutes an existing expression node in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree with a new expression node. The function handles a wide variety of parent node types including statements, operators, and language-specific constructs for C++, Fortran, MATLAB, Jovial, and Ada. The replacement process involves updating the parent node to point to the new expression and properly setting the parent pointer of the new expression. If the old expression was an lvalue, the new expression is also marked as an lvalue. For variable reference expressions, parentheses are automatically added for safety.

The function supports replacement within the following parent node types:

  • Expression statements (SgExprStatement)
  • For statements (SgForStatement, SgMatlabForStatement, SgJovialForThenStatement, SgFortranDo)
  • Range expressions (SgRangeExp)
  • Return statements (SgReturnStmt)
  • Binary and unary operators (SgBinaryOp, SgUnaryOp)
  • Conditional expressions (SgConditionalExp)
  • Expression lists (SgExprListExp)
  • Initialized names (SgInitializedName)
  • Case option statements (SgCaseOptionStmt)
  • Process control statements (SgProcessControlStatement)
  • Various Ada-specific constructs (SgAdaExitStmt, SgAdaModularType, SgAdaDelayStmt, etc.)
  • Generic expression parents via replace_expression method
Parameters
oldExpPointer to the expression node to be replaced. Must not be NULL.
newExpPointer to the new expression node that will replace oldExp. Must not be NULL.
keepOldExpBoolean flag indicating whether to preserve the old expression in memory. If false (default), the old expression is deeply deleted to avoid dangling nodes in the memory pool. If true, the old expression is kept but its parent pointer is set to NULL.
Warning
If the parent node type is not handled by this function, an error message is printed to stderr and the program aborts via ROSE_ABORT().
For compiler-generated code where the parent is a SgValueExp, the function returns early without performing any replacement since such code will not appear in the final AST.
Precondition
oldExp must not be NULL.
newExp must not be NULL.
oldExp must have a valid non-NULL parent node.
When replacing an initializer in SgInitializedName, newExp must be of type SgInitializer.
Postcondition
The new expression is properly linked into the AST with correct parent pointer.
If keepOldExp is false, the old expression is deleted from memory.
If keepOldExp is true, the old expression has its parent pointer set to NULL.
If the old expression was an lvalue, the new expression is also marked as an lvalue.
Note
If oldExp and newExp are the same pointer, the function returns immediately without making any changes.
When newExp is a SgVarRefExp, it is automatically enclosed in parentheses for safety by setting the need_paren flag to true.
This function handles language-specific constructs for multiple languages supported by ROSE including C++, Fortran, MATLAB, Jovial, and Ada.

◆ replaceExpressionWithStatement()

void SageInterface::replaceExpressionWithStatement ( SgExpression * from,
StatementGenerator * to )

Replaces an expression within a statement with a generated statement.

This function performs a complex transformation that replaces a specified expression with a statement generated by the provided StatementGenerator. The function handles various enclosing statement contexts including for loops, while loops, do-while loops, if statements, switch statements, return statements, variable declarations, and expression statements.

The transformation strategy varies depending on the context of the expression:

For variable declarations: Delegates directly to replaceSubexpressionWithStatement.

For for-loop increment expressions: The increment is moved into the loop body with a label, and continue statements are converted to goto statements targeting that label. The original increment position is replaced with a null expression.

For for-loop test expressions: The test is pushed into the loop body as a temporary boolean variable assignment, with a conditional break if the test fails. The original test is replaced with true.

For while-loop conditions: Similar to for-loop tests, the condition is pushed into the body with a temporary variable and conditional break.

For do-while conditions: A wrapper block is created with a boolean temporary variable initialized to true. The condition evaluation is moved to the end of the loop body, and continue statements are converted to goto statements.

For if-statement conditions: A wrapper block is created with a temporary boolean variable that captures the condition result before the if statement executes.

For switch-statement selectors: A wrapper block is created with a temporary variable of the selector's type to hold the evaluated selector value.

This function was modified to handle changes in Sage III where the test expression for SgForStmt can be either an SgExpression or SgStatement.

Parameters
fromThe expression to be replaced. Must be a valid expression contained within a supported statement type (expression statement, for statement, return statement, or variable declaration).
toThe statement generator that produces the replacement statement. This generator is invoked during the replaceSubexpressionWithStatement call.
Warning
This function uses internal variable names prefixed with "rose__temp" which must not conflict with user code variable names.
The function modifies the AST structure significantly, including potentially wrapping statements in new basic blocks and converting control flow statements.
This function is disabled when ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is defined.
Precondition
The from parameter must be a valid, non-null SgExpression pointer.
The to parameter must be a valid, non-null StatementGenerator pointer.
The expression must be contained within an SgExprStatement, SgForStatement, SgReturnStmt, or SgVariableDeclaration.
The enclosing statement must have a valid parent in the AST.
Postcondition
The original expression has been replaced according to the transformation rules.
The AST remains valid with proper parent-child relationships maintained.
New temporary variables may have been introduced into the scope.
Control flow may have been restructured with new basic blocks and labels.
Note
The temporary variable names used (rose__temp1, rose__temp2, rose__temp3) do not need to be unique across the program but must not appear in user code.
This function relies on several helper functions including getStatementOfExpression, getRootOfExpression, pushTestIntoBody, addStepToLoopBody, and replaceSubexpressionWithStatement.
The function contains a bugfix from MS dated 7/3/2018 related to variable symbol creation during buildVariableDeclaration calls.

◆ replaceMacroCallsWithExpandedStrings()

void SageInterface::replaceMacroCallsWithExpandedStrings ( SgPragmaDeclaration * target)

Replaces macro calls within a pragma declaration with their expanded string representations.

This function processes a pragma declaration to find any attached preprocessing information that represents macro calls. When macro calls are found, the function expands them using the Wave preprocessor library and replaces the original macro call text in the pragma with the expanded string content. This is implemented as part of Wave support in ROSE.

The algorithm iterates through all attached preprocessing information on the target pragma declaration. For each macro call found, it extracts the expanded token sequence from the Wave preprocessor, converts it to a string, and performs string replacement on the pragma text. The replacement is performed repeatedly until no more occurrences of the macro call are found in the pragma text. After replacement, the old pragma object is deleted and a new pragma with the updated text is created and set.

This function is conditionally compiled and is only available when USE_ROSE is not defined and when ROSE_SKIP_COMPILATION_OF_WAVE is not defined, as it depends on Wave preprocessor functionality.

Parameters
targetPointer to the SgPragmaDeclaration node whose macro calls should be expanded. Must not be NULL when USE_ROSE is not defined.
Warning
This implementation uses string matching and replacing, which is acknowledged as a dirty fix. The ideal solution would be having preprocessed pragma text generated directly by the compiler. String matching and replacing is inherently unsafe and may produce incorrect results in edge cases.
The original pragma object is deleted and replaced with a new one. Any external references to the old pragma object will become invalid.
Precondition
target must not be NULL.
The function requires Wave preprocessor support to be compiled and available.
Postcondition
If macro calls were present in the pragma, they are replaced with their expanded forms.
The original pragma object is deleted and a new pragma object is created with the modified text.
Note
This function is part of the Wave preprocessor support in ROSE.
The function returns early without modification if no preprocessing information is attached to the target pragma declaration.
This function is excluded from compilation when USE_ROSE is defined via ifndef USE_ROSE.
The Wave-dependent code section is excluded when ROSE_SKIP_COMPILATION_OF_WAVE is defined via ifndef ROSE_SKIP_COMPILATION_OF_WAVE.

◆ replaceStatement()

void SageInterface::replaceStatement ( SgStatement * oldStmt,
SgStatement * newStmt,
bool movePreprocessingInfoValue = false )

Replaces an existing statement in the AST with a new statement.

This function substitutes an old statement node in the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) with a new statement node. The replacement is performed by locating the parent of the old statement and invoking the parent's replace_statement method to perform the actual substitution. After replacement, the function synchronizes the physical file ID information from the old statement to the new statement to maintain source location consistency. The new statement's parent pointer is also updated to point to the old statement's parent.

When the movePreprocessingInfoValue parameter is set to true, the function handles the transfer of preprocessing information (such as ifdef, endif, and other preprocessor directives) from the old statement to the new statement. This includes moving up any inner dangling directives to prevent them from being lost during the replacement operation.

Parameters
oldStmtPointer to the statement that will be replaced. Must not be NULL and must have a valid parent statement in the AST.
newStmtPointer to the new statement that will replace the old statement. Must not be NULL.
movePreprocessingInfoValueBoolean flag indicating whether preprocessing information should be transferred from the old statement to the new statement. Defaults to false.
Precondition
oldStmt must not be NULL.
newStmt must not be NULL.
oldStmt must have a valid parent that is an SgStatement.
oldStmt and newStmt should be different nodes for any meaningful replacement.
Postcondition
The old statement is replaced by the new statement in the AST.
The new statement's physical file ID matches the old statement's physical file ID.
The new statement's parent pointer is set to the old statement's parent.
If movePreprocessingInfoValue is true, preprocessing information is transferred from the old statement to the new statement.
Note
If oldStmt and newStmt are the same pointer, the function returns immediately without performing any operation.
The function does not delete or deallocate the old statement after replacement. The caller is responsible for managing the memory of the replaced statement.
Some translators such as the outliner may have their own handling for preprocessing information transfer.
Warning
The old statement's parent must be a valid SgStatement; otherwise, an assertion failure will occur.

◆ replaceSubexpressionWithStatement()

void SageInterface::replaceSubexpressionWithStatement ( SgExpression * from,
StatementGenerator * to )

Replaces a subexpression within a statement with a generated statement.

This function transforms an expression embedded within a statement by replacing it with a statement generated by the provided StatementGenerator. The function handles several cases depending on the context of the expression:

  1. If the expression is the entire expression statement, it directly replaces the statement with the generated one.
  2. If the expression is the right-hand side of an assignment operation at the top level of an expression statement, it generates a statement using the left-hand side operand as context.
  3. For other cases, the function uses a multi-step transformation:
    • Splits the expression using splitExpression to extract it into an initializer
    • Converts the initializer into an assignment statement
    • Replaces the resulting assignment statement with the generated statement

This function is only active when ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is not defined.

Parameters
fromThe expression to be replaced. This expression must be part of a valid statement in the AST. The caller should not be currently traversing from this expression or the statement containing it.
toA pointer to a StatementGenerator object that will produce the replacement statement. The generate method is called with either NULL or the left-hand side of an assignment depending on the context.
Warning
The caller must ensure they are not currently traversing the expression or its containing statement, as this operation modifies the AST structure.
This function modifies the AST in place, which may invalidate iterators or pointers to affected nodes.
Precondition
The parameter from must be a valid non-null expression that is part of a statement.
The parameter to must be a valid non-null StatementGenerator capable of producing replacement statements.
Postcondition
The expression from has been replaced by a statement generated by to, and the parent relationships in the AST have been updated accordingly.
Note
This function has no effect when ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is defined.
The function uses helper functions getStatementOfExpression, getRootOfExpression, splitExpression, convertInitializerIntoAssignment, and replaceAssignmentStmtWithStatement to perform the transformation.

Replaces all references to a variable with references to another variable within a given scope.

This function traverses the abstract syntax tree (AST) within the specified scope and replaces all variable reference expressions (SgVarRefExp) that refer to the old variable symbol with references to the new variable symbol. This is essentially a variable substitution operation that updates all uses of variable a to instead reference variable b throughout the given scope.

The implementation uses NodeQuery::querySubTree to collect all SgVarRefExp nodes within the scope's subtree, then iterates through each reference and updates those that match the old symbol to point to the new symbol.

new_symPointer to the variable symbol that will replace references to old_sym. Must not be NULL and must be different from old_sym.

Precondition
old_sym is not NULL.
new_sym is not NULL.
old_sym and new_sym are different symbols (old_sym != new_sym).
scope is not NULL.
Postcondition
All SgVarRefExp nodes within the scope that previously referenced old_sym now reference new_sym.

This function modifies the AST in place by updating symbol pointers in variable reference expressions.
The function does not update variable declarations, only variable references.

◆ replaceWithPattern()

SgNode * SageInterface::replaceWithPattern ( SgNode * anchor,
SgNode * new_pattern )

Replaces an anchor node with a pattern, substituting all variant expressions in the pattern with copies of the anchor.

This function performs a pattern-based replacement operation in the ROSE AST. It takes an anchor expression node and a pattern expression node, then replaces all SgVariantExpression nodes found within the pattern with deep copies of the anchor expression. After all variant expressions have been substituted, the original anchor expression is replaced by the modified pattern expression in the AST.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Validates that both anchor and new_pattern are valid SgExpression nodes.
  2. Queries the pattern subtree to find all SgExpression nodes.
  3. For each SgVariantExpression found in the pattern, creates a deep copy of the anchor expression and replaces the variant expression with this copy.
  4. Finally, replaces the original anchor expression with the fully substituted pattern expression.

This is useful for applying transformation patterns where placeholder expressions (SgVariantExpression) need to be filled in with actual expression values from the source code.

Parameters
anchorThe anchor node to be replaced. Must be a valid SgExpression node. This node will be replaced by the pattern and its copies will substitute all variant expressions within the pattern.
new_patternThe pattern node containing the replacement structure. Must be a valid SgExpression node. All SgVariantExpression nodes within this pattern will be replaced with copies of the anchor expression.
Returns
Returns the new_pattern node after all substitutions have been performed and the anchor has been replaced.
Precondition
The anchor parameter must be a valid SgExpression node (not NULL).
The new_pattern parameter must be a valid SgExpression node (not NULL).
The anchor node must be properly connected to an AST for the final replacement to succeed.
Postcondition
All SgVariantExpression nodes within the pattern have been replaced with deep copies of the anchor expression.
The original anchor expression has been replaced by the pattern expression in the AST.
The returned pattern node is now integrated into the AST at the former location of the anchor.
Note
The function uses deepCopy to create copies of the anchor expression, ensuring that each substitution gets an independent copy rather than sharing the same node.
The final replaceExpression call is made with the keepOldExp parameter set to false, meaning the original anchor expression may be deleted.
Warning
The function will trigger an assertion failure if either anchor or new_pattern cannot be cast to SgExpression.

This function traverses the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) starting from the specified node and reports all SgLocatedNode instances that have been marked as modified (via the isModified flag). It is primarily intended as a debugging utility for token-based unparsing, helping developers track which nodes have been modified during transformations.

The function first attempts to identify the source file associated with the given node, either directly if the node is an SgSourceFile, or indirectly through an SgGlobal scope. It then collects all modified located nodes using collectModifiedLocatedNodes and prints detailed information about each one, including the filename and node class name.

Note
This function produces formatted console output with visual separators for easy identification in log files. The output includes header and footer separator lines made of hash characters.
The function contains commented-out diagnostic code that can be enabled for additional debugging, including an assertion that can halt execution for testing.

This function is intended for debugging purposes only and may produce significant output when many nodes are modified. It should not be used in production code where performance is critical.

The function first attempts to determine the source file context by checking if the input node is an SgSourceFile or SgGlobal scope. It then collects all modified statements using collectModifiedStatements and iterates through them, printing the filename, memory address, and class name of each modified statement. ◆ reset_name_collision_map()

void SageInterface::reset_name_collision_map ( )

Resets all internal name collision tracking maps to their empty state.

This function clears the internal data structures used for tracking name collisions during AST transformations and code generation. It resets three separate maps: the name collision map which tracks duplicate names, the name-to-node map which associates string names with AST nodes, and the node-to-name map which provides the reverse mapping from AST nodes back to their assigned names. This function is typically called when starting a new transformation context or when the previous name collision state is no longer relevant.

Note
This function operates on static or global internal maps within the SageInterface namespace. Calling this function will affect all subsequent name collision detection operations.
Warning
Calling this function while name collision tracking is actively being used may result in incorrect name generation or unexpected name collisions in generated code.
Precondition
The internal maps may contain data from previous operations.
Postcondition
All three internal maps (local_name_collision_map, local_name_to_node_map, and local_node_to_name_map) are empty.

◆ resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement()

void SageInterface::resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement ( SgStatement * sourceStatement)

Resets internal data structure mappings when a statement is modified or removed.

This function updates internal data structures that hold references to statements when those statements are modified. The primary use case is handling macro expansion data structures that maintain references to statements associated with macro expansions.

When a statement associated with a macro expansion is removed or modified, the macro expansion tracking information must be updated to force all related statements to be marked as transformed. This ensures that the AST will be unparsed correctly instead of outputting tokens representing the original macro call, which could result in incorrect or partial representations of the transformed code mixed with the original macro invocation.

The algorithm performs the following steps:

  1. Retrieves the enclosing source file for the given statement
  2. Looks up the statement in the source file's macro expansion map
  3. If found and not already processed, marks all statements in the associated macro expansion as transformed and requiring output in code generation
  4. Marks the macro expansion itself as having been processed
Parameters
sourceStatementPointer to the statement that is being modified or removed. This statement may be associated with a macro expansion that needs to be updated. If the statement has not yet been added to the AST, the function will safely handle the case where no enclosing source file can be found.
Precondition
The sourceStatement pointer should be valid and point to a legitimate SgStatement object.
Postcondition
If the statement was associated with a macro expansion, all statements in that macro expansion will be marked as transformations and set to output in code generation.
The associated macro expansion will be marked as transformed to prevent redundant processing.
Note
If the statement has not yet been added to the AST, the function will return early without performing any updates since no enclosing source file will be found.
Statements that do not have valid Sg_File_Info objects are skipped when marking transformations, as they may be newly created statements not yet fully initialized.
Other data structures such as representativeWhitespaceStatementMap and redundantlyMappedTokensToStatementMultimap may also need updating in related contexts but are not modified by this function.
Warning
Care must be taken when statements are deleted, as the associated statement vector in the macro expansion may contain references to deleted statements. The function relies on the macro expansion being marked as transformed to avoid issues with memory pool reuse.

◆ resetModifiedLocatedNodes()

void SageInterface::resetModifiedLocatedNodes ( const std::set< SgLocatedNode * > & modifiedNodeSet)

Resets the modification flag for a set of located nodes in the IR.

This function iterates through a previously constructed set of SgLocatedNode pointers and marks each node as modified by setting its isModified flag to true. This is useful for restoring the modification state of IR (Intermediate Representation) nodes after certain transformations or analyses have been performed, allowing the system to track which nodes have been changed.

The function uses a simple iteration algorithm that traverses the entire set and calls set_isModified(true) on each node encountered.

Parameters
modifiedNodeSetA constant reference to a set containing pointers to SgLocatedNode objects that should be marked as modified. The set may be empty, in which case no nodes are modified.
Precondition
All pointers in modifiedNodeSet must be valid, non-null pointers to existing SgLocatedNode objects in the AST.
The SgLocatedNode objects referenced in the set must not have been deleted.
Postcondition
All nodes in the modifiedNodeSet have their isModified flag set to true.
Note
This function does not modify the input set itself; it only modifies the state of the nodes pointed to by the elements in the set.
Debug output statements are present but disabled via preprocessor conditionals.
Warning
Passing invalid or dangling pointers in the set will result in undefined behavior.

◆ resetScopeNumbers()

void SageInterface::resetScopeNumbers ( SgFunctionDefinition * functionDefinition)

Resets and assigns unique scope numbers to all scope statements within a function definition.

This function performs a preorder traversal of the abstract syntax tree (AST) rooted at the given function definition to uniquely label all scope statements (SgScopeStatement nodes). Each scope encountered during the traversal is assigned a sequential integer identifier starting from 1, and these mappings are stored in the function definition's scope number list.

The implementation uses a nested traversal class (ScopeNumberingTraversal) that extends AstSimpleProcessing to visit each node in preorder. When a SgScopeStatement is encountered, it increments a counter and inserts the scope-to-number mapping into the function definition's internal scope map. The traversal automatically detects and stores the root function definition when it encounters the first SgFunctionDefinition node.

The scope number list must be empty before calling this function, as it does not clear existing entries but rather expects to populate an empty map.

Parameters
functionDefinitionPointer to the SgFunctionDefinition node whose scope statements are to be numbered. This serves as the root of the AST traversal. Must not be NULL.
Warning
This function asserts that the scope number list is empty before processing. Calling this function on a function definition that already has scope numbers assigned will trigger an assertion failure.
Precondition
functionDefinition must not be NULL.
The scope number list of functionDefinition must be empty (i.e., get_scope_number_list().empty() == true).
Postcondition
All SgScopeStatement nodes within the function definition will have unique integer identifiers assigned and stored in the function definition's scope number list.
The scope numbers are assigned in preorder traversal order, starting from 1.
Note
The scope numbering includes the function definition itself if it is considered a scope statement, as well as all nested scopes such as basic blocks, for loops, while loops, if statements, and other scope-creating constructs.
This function is typically used for analysis or transformation passes that require unique identification of scopes within a function.

Saves the AST rooted at the given node to a PDF file with a default filename.

This function provides a convenient overload for saving an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) representation to a PDF file using a default filename. It internally delegates to the two-parameter version of saveToPDF, passing "temp.pdf.json" as the default output filename. The function generates an intermediate JSON representation that can be converted to PDF format for visualization purposes.

Parameters

Precondition
The node parameter should point to a valid SgNode within a properly constructed AST.
Postcondition
A file named "temp.pdf.json" is created or overwritten in the current working directory containing the JSON representation of the AST.
Note
This is a convenience wrapper function. For specifying a custom output filename, use the two-parameter overload saveToPDF(SgNode*, const std::string&).
The output file uses a .json extension, suggesting the actual output is a JSON intermediate format rather than a direct PDF file.
Warning
The default filename "temp.pdf.json" will overwrite any existing file with the same name without warning.

void SageInterface::saveToPDF ( SgNode * node,
std::string filename )

Saves the AST of the enclosing file to a PDF file.

This function generates a PDF representation of the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) for the file that contains the given node. It first locates the enclosing file node from the provided SgNode, then uses the AstJSONGeneration utility to generate the PDF output. The entire file's AST structure is captured in the resulting PDF document, which can be useful for visualization and debugging purposes.

◆ scopeHasStatementsFromSameFile()

bool SageInterface::scopeHasStatementsFromSameFile ( SgScopeStatement * scope)

Determines whether a scope contains statements originating from the same file as the scope itself.

This function supports token-based unparsing when working with header files by detecting whether a scope contains statements that must be unparsed because they originate from the same physical file as the scope. The function examines each statement within the scope and compares its physical file ID against the scope's physical file ID.

When the scope has statements from the same file, and if there is a transformation contained in any of those statements, the scope must be unparsed one statement at a time during token-based unparsing. If the scope has no statements from the same file, then the existence of any statement containing a transformation does not cause the statements to be unparsed individually.

The function handles two cases based on the scope's content:

  • If the scope contains only declarations, it iterates through the declaration statement list.
  • Otherwise, it iterates through the general statement list.

The iteration terminates early once a statement from the same file is found.

Parameters
scopePointer to the SgScopeStatement to be examined. Must not be NULL.
Returns
True if there is at least one statement in the scope that originates from the same physical file as the scope itself. False if the scope is empty or contains only statements associated with other files (such as header files).
Precondition
The scope parameter must not be NULL.
The scope and its contained statements must have valid file information with physical file IDs.
Postcondition
The scope and its contents remain unchanged.
Note
This function is part of the infrastructure supporting token-based unparsing in ROSE.
Debug printf statements are present in the implementation for development purposes.
The function uses physical file IDs rather than logical file IDs to determine file origin.
Warning
The function will trigger an assertion failure if the scope parameter is NULL.

◆ serialize_list()

template<typename T>
void SageInterface::serialize_list ( T & plist,
std::string T_name,
std::string & prefix,
bool hasRemaining,
std::ostringstream & out,
std::string & edgeLabel )

Empty function or ill-formed function detected.

Serializes a list-like container into a tree-formatted text representation.

This function generates a human-readable, tree-structured text representation of a list container and its elements. It recursively serializes each non-null element in the list by calling a serialize function on each child. The output uses ASCII art characters to represent the tree structure with proper indentation and branch connectors.

The algorithm first scans the list backwards to find the last non-null element, which is used to determine proper tree branch formatting (whether to show continuing branches or terminal branches). Each non-null element is then serialized recursively with appropriate prefix strings to maintain visual tree alignment.

Parameters
plistReference to the list-like container to be serialized. The container must support size() method and index-based access via operator[]. Elements must be pointer-like types that can be evaluated in boolean context to check for null.
T_nameA string representing the human-readable type name of the container, used for display purposes in the output.
prefixReference to the current indentation prefix string used for tree structure formatting.
hasRemainingBoolean flag indicating whether there are remaining sibling nodes at the current level, affecting the branch connector style.
outReference to the output string stream where the serialized representation is written.
edgeLabelReference to a string label to be displayed on the edge connecting this node to its parent in the tree visualization.
Precondition
The container plist must be a valid, initialized container supporting size() and operator[] access.
The out stream must be in a valid state for writing.
A compatible serialize() function must be available for the element type contained in plist.
Postcondition
The serialized tree representation of plist and all its non-null children has been appended to the out stream.
The original plist container remains unchanged.
Note
The function uses vertical bar and underscore characters to create ASCII tree branch visuals: "|---" for nodes with remaining siblings and "|___" for terminal nodes.
Null elements in the list are skipped and not serialized.
The memory address of the list is included in the output for debugging purposes.
This function depends on an external serialize() function being available to handle the recursive serialization of child elements.
Warning
The recursive nature of this function may cause stack overflow for deeply nested data structures.
The T_name parameter should accurately reflect the type of plist for meaningful output, as the function does not validate this correspondence.

◆ set_name()

int SageInterface::set_name ( SgInitializedName * initializedNameNode,
SgName new_name )

Renames an initialized name node by updating its symbol table entry and name.

This function performs a complete renaming operation for a given SgInitializedName node in the ROSE AST. The renaming process involves several steps:

  1. Locating the appropriate scope and symbol table containing the symbol
  2. Finding the symbol associated with the current name based on the parent declaration type
  3. Removing the old symbol table entry
  4. Inserting a new entry with the updated name while preserving the symbol object
  5. Updating the name stored in the SgInitializedName node itself
  6. Marking the enclosing statement and all references as modified for proper unparsing

The function handles different declaration types including variable declarations, function parameter lists, class declarations, function declarations, and enum declarations. It also traverses the memory pool to find all SgVarRefExp nodes that reference the renamed symbol and marks them as transformations for correct header file unparsing.

Parameters
initializedNameNodePointer to the SgInitializedName node whose name is to be changed. Must not be NULL.
new_nameThe new name to assign to the initialized name node.
Returns
Returns 1 on successful renaming operation. Returns 0 if no matching symbol is found in the symbol table, if the parent statement cannot be transformed due to header file constraints, or if the symbol table insertion fails.
Warning
The return value semantics appear to be reversed from typical conventions where 0 indicates success and non-zero indicates error.
If the parent declaration is part of a header file included multiple times with different include syntax, the transformation will be rejected and the function will return 0.
Precondition
initializedNameNode must not be NULL.
initializedNameNode must have a valid scope with an initialized symbol table.
initializedNameNode must have a valid parent declaration.
Postcondition
On success, the name in initializedNameNode is updated to new_name.
On success, the symbol table entry is updated with the new name.
On success, the enclosing statement is marked as modified and as a transformation.
On success, all SgVarRefExp nodes referencing the symbol are marked as transformations.
Note
This function supports enum values within SgEnumDeclaration as of version 2/4/2021.
The function reuses the existing symbol object rather than creating a new one, which allows for efficient detection of references during the memory pool traversal.
Debug output can be enabled by setting DEBUG_SET_NAME to 1 via the define directive.

◆ setBaseTypeDefiningDeclaration()

void SageInterface::setBaseTypeDefiningDeclaration ( SgVariableDeclaration * var_decl,
SgDeclarationStatement * base_decl )

Sets the base type defining declaration for a variable declaration.

This function associates a base type defining declaration (such as a struct or class definition) with a variable declaration. It handles the case where the base declaration may have been previously inserted into a scope by removing it from that scope first. The function then establishes the parent-child relationship between the variable declaration and the base declaration, and updates internal mangled names for any anonymous declarations.

The algorithm performs the following steps:

  1. If the base declaration has a parent and that parent is its scope, check if it exists in the scope's statement list and remove it if found.
  2. Set the base declaration's parent to the variable declaration.
  3. Associate the base declaration with the variable declaration via set_baseTypeDefiningDeclaration.
  4. Traverse the memory pool to reset empty names for anonymous declarations.
Parameters
var_declPointer to the variable declaration that will contain the base type defining declaration. Must not be null.
base_declPointer to the declaration statement that defines the base type (e.g., a struct or class definition). Must not be null.
Warning
There is a known issue (gitlab-issue-349) that may arise when base_decl has a comment attached and it is the first statement in a scope. Removing base_decl in this case may cause comments to be moved unexpectedly. Consider moving comments to var_decl first to avoid potential problems.
Precondition
var_decl must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgVariableDeclaration.
base_decl must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgDeclarationStatement.
Postcondition
base_decl's parent is set to var_decl.
var_decl's base type defining declaration is set to base_decl.
If base_decl was previously in a scope's statement list, it has been removed.
Empty names in the AST memory pool have been reset via ResetEmptyNames traversal.
Note
This function uses ResetEmptyNames traversal instead of resetNamesInAST() because the latter would trigger an assertion failure related to mangleNameMap.size() == 0.

This function modifies the storage modifier of a given declaration statement to mark it as extern. It accesses the declaration modifier of the statement, then retrieves the storage modifier, and finally sets the extern flag on it. The extern storage class specifier indicates that the declared entity has external linkage and is defined elsewhere.

This function modifies the AST node in place. The change affects how the declaration is represented and unparsed in the generated source code.

SgDeclarationModifier
SgStorageModifier

◆ setFortranNumericLabel()

Sets a Fortran numeric label on a statement.

This function assigns a numeric label to a Fortran statement within the ROSE abstract syntax tree. Fortran numeric labels are integer values (1-99999) that can be used for statement identification, typically for GOTO targets, FORMAT statements, or DO loop constructs. The function creates a new SgLabelSymbol and SgLabelRefExp as needed, associating them with the specified statement.

The function first determines the appropriate label scope (defaulting to the enclosing function definition if not provided). It then looks up whether a label symbol with the given numeric value already exists in that scope. If not found, a new SgLabelSymbol is created and inserted into the scope's symbol table. If a duplicate label is detected, the function reports an error and aborts. Finally, a SgLabelRefExp is created and attached to the statement according to the specified label type (start or end label).

label_scopeThe scope in which the label symbol should be defined. If NULL, defaults to the enclosing function definition of the statement.

The function will abort with an assertion failure if a duplicate label value is detected within the same scope.
The function will abort if an unsupported label_type is provided.
Precondition
stmt must not be NULL.
label_value must be in the range [1, 99999].
If label_scope is NULL, stmt must be contained within a function definition.
The label_value must not already exist as a label in the target scope.
Postcondition
A new SgLabelSymbol is created and inserted into the label scope's symbol table.
A SgLabelRefExp is created and attached to the statement's numeric_label or end_numeric_label field depending on label_type.
The SgLabelRefExp's parent is set to the statement.
Note
This function is specific to Fortran code and should not be used for C or C++ statements.
The SgLabelRefExp objects are created transparently as needed.

◆ setLhsOperand()

void SageInterface::setLhsOperand ( SgExpression * target,

Sets the left-hand side operand of a binary or variadic argument expression.

This function assigns a new left-hand side (LHS) operand to a target expression node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree. The function handles three specific expression types: SgVarArgCopyOp, SgVarArgStartOp, and SgBinaryOp. After setting the LHS operand, the function updates the parent pointer of the LHS expression to maintain proper AST structure. If both LHS and RHS operands are present after the assignment, the function calls markLhsValues to properly mark lvalue properties on the target expression.

The function uses dynamic type checking via isSg* functions to determine the actual type of the target expression and calls the appropriate set_lhs_operand method for that type. If the target expression is not one of the supported types, the function reports an error and aborts execution.

targetThe target expression node whose LHS operand is to be set. Must be a valid pointer to an SgExpression that is either an SgVarArgCopyOp, SgVarArgStartOp, or SgBinaryOp.
lhsThe expression to be set as the left-hand side operand of the target. Must be a valid pointer to an SgExpression and must not be the same object as target.
Warning
If the target expression is not of a supported type (SgVarArgCopyOp, SgVarArgStartOp, or SgBinaryOp), the function will output an error message and call ROSE_ABORT to terminate execution.
Precondition
target must not be NULL.
lhs must not be NULL.
target and lhs must be different objects (target != lhs).
Postcondition
The LHS operand of target is set to lhs.
The parent pointer of lhs is set to target.
If target has both LHS and RHS operands after the assignment, markLhsValues is called to update lvalue markings.
Note
The markLhsValues function contains an assertion that requires the RHS operand to be non-NULL, which is why lvalue marking is only performed when both operands are available.

Sets the body statement of a loop construct.

This function assigns a new body statement to a given loop statement node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). After setting the condition, the function also updates the parent pointer of the condition statement to maintain proper AST structure.

If loopStmt is not one of the supported loop types (while, for, or do-while), the function will trigger an assertion failure.
