◆ setLoopLowerBound()

void SageInterface::setLoopLowerBound ( SgNode * loop,
SgExpression * lb )

Sets the lower bound expression of a loop header.

This function modifies the lower bound of a loop construct by replacing the existing lower bound expression with a new one. It supports both C/C++ for loops (SgForStatement) and Fortran DO loops (SgFortranDo).

For C/C++ for loops, the function handles two initialization statement forms:

  1. Assignment expression statements (e.g., i=0): The function locates the SgAssignOp node and replaces its right-hand side operand with the new lower bound expression.
  2. Variable declaration statements (e.g., int i=0): The function locates the SgAssignInitializer node and replaces its operand with the new lower bound expression.

For Fortran DO loops, the function retrieves the initialization expression, which is expected to be an assignment operation, and replaces its right-hand side operand with the new lower bound.

The function uses NodeQuery::querySubTree to locate the appropriate AST nodes within the loop initialization statement. It assumes the loop is in canonical form with exactly one initialization statement.

Parameters
loopPointer to the loop node whose lower bound is to be modified. Must be either an SgForStatement or SgFortranDo node.
lbPointer to the new lower bound expression to set. This expression will be inserted into the AST and its parent pointer will be updated.
Warning
The function does not deallocate or handle the original lower bound expression that is being replaced. This may lead to memory leaks if the original expression is not managed elsewhere.
If the loop type is neither SgForStatement nor SgFortranDo, the function will output an error message and trigger an assertion failure.
Precondition
loop must not be NULL.
lb must not be NULL.
The loop must be in canonical form with exactly one initialization statement.
For SgForStatement, the initialization must contain either an SgAssignOp or an SgAssignInitializer.
For SgFortranDo, the initialization must be an SgAssignOp.
Postcondition
The loop's lower bound expression is replaced with lb.
The parent pointer of lb is set to the appropriate parent node in the AST.
If the original right-hand side was an lvalue, the new expression's lvalue flag is set accordingly (for assignment expression case only).
Note
This function only handles loops in canonical form. Non-canonical loops with multiple initialization statements are not supported.
The original lower bound expression is orphaned but not deleted, which may require manual cleanup by the caller.

◆ setLoopStride()

void SageInterface::setLoopStride ( SgNode * loop,
SgExpression * stride )

Sets the stride (step) of a loop's incremental expression.

This function modifies the stride of a loop's increment expression, supporting various common forms of loop increment syntax. It handles both C/C++ for loops (SgForStatement) and Fortran DO loops (SgFortranDo).

For Fortran DO loops, the function directly sets the increment expression.

For C/C++ for loops, the function recognizes and transforms multiple increment expression patterns:

  • Case 1: i++ is transformed to i += stride
  • Case 1.5: i– is transformed to i += stride
  • Case 2: i += X has its right-hand side replaced with stride
  • Case 2.5: i -= X is transformed to i += stride
  • Case 3: i = i + X or i = X + i has the non-loop-variable operand replaced with stride
  • Case 3.5: i = i - X is transformed to use i += stride

The function uses AST subtree queries to identify the specific form of the increment expression and applies the appropriate transformation.

Parameters
loopPointer to the loop node whose stride is to be modified. Must be either an SgForStatement (C/C++ for loop) or an SgFortranDo (Fortran DO loop).
stridePointer to the expression representing the new stride value to be set for the loop increment.
Warning
The function assumes canonical loop forms. Non-canonical increment expressions such as i *= X are not handled and may produce unexpected results.
The original increment expression memory is not explicitly deleted for Fortran DO loops, which may lead to memory leaks.
For cases involving subtraction (i -= X or i = i - X), the function converts them to addition with the provided stride, which may change the loop semantics if the stride sign is not adjusted accordingly.
Precondition
loop must not be NULL.
stride must not be NULL.
loop must be either an SgForStatement or an SgFortranDo node.
For C/C++ for loops, the increment expression should follow one of the recognized canonical forms.
Postcondition
The loop's increment expression is modified to use the specified stride.
The stride expression's parent pointer is set appropriately in the AST.
Note
For increment expressions with multiple operators of the same type in the subtree, only the first one found is considered.
The function will trigger an assertion failure if the loop type is neither SgForStatement nor SgFortranDo.

◆ setLoopUpperBound()

void SageInterface::setLoopUpperBound ( SgNode * loop,
SgExpression * ub )

Sets the upper bound expression of a loop header.

This function modifies the upper bound of a loop construct, supporting both C/C++ for-loops (SgForStatement) and Fortran DO-loops (SgFortranDo). For a typical C/C++ for-loop of the form "for (i=lb; i op ub; ...)", this function replaces the upper bound expression in the loop condition. The function handles the condition expression regardless of the specific comparison operator type used in the loop test.

For C/C++ for-statements, the function extracts the binary operation from the test expression and replaces its right-hand side operand with the new upper bound. For Fortran DO-statements, it directly sets the bound using the appropriate setter method.

Parameters
loopA pointer to the loop node whose upper bound is to be modified. Must be either an SgForStatement or an SgFortranDo node.
ubA pointer to the expression that will serve as the new upper bound. This expression will have its parent pointer updated to reflect its new position in the AST.
Warning
The function will trigger an assertion failure and terminate if the loop parameter is neither an SgForStatement nor an SgFortranDo.
For SgForStatement, the function assumes the test expression is an SgExprStatement containing a binary operation. If this assumption is violated, an assertion failure will occur.
The original upper bound expression for Fortran DO-loops is not deleted, which may lead to memory leaks.
Precondition
loop must not be NULL.
ub must not be NULL.
For SgForStatement, the test expression must be a binary operation wrapped in an SgExprStatement.
Postcondition
The loop's upper bound is set to the provided expression ub.
The parent pointer of ub is updated to point to its new parent node in the AST.
Note
This function only supports SgForStatement and SgFortranDo loop types. Other loop constructs such as while-loops are not supported.
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the new upper bound expression is semantically valid for the loop context.

◆ setOneSourcePositionForTransformation()

void SageInterface::setOneSourcePositionForTransformation ( SgNode * node)

Sets the source position for a transformation on a given AST node.

This function is a deprecated wrapper that sets the source position information for a node that has been created or modified as part of a source-to-source transformation. It internally delegates to the setSourcePosition() function to perform the actual source position assignment.

This function was previously part of an older API and has been superseded by setSourcePositionAsTransformation(). The function exists for backward compatibility purposes. When compiled with ROSE_DEBUG_NEW_EDG_ROSE_CONNECTION defined, a deprecation warning message is printed to standard output.

Parameters
nodePointer to the SgNode for which the source position should be set. This node typically represents an AST element that was created or modified during a transformation pass.
Warning
This function is deprecated. Use setSourcePositionAsTransformation() instead for new code.
Precondition
The node parameter should be a valid pointer to an existing SgNode object.
Postcondition
The source position of the specified node is set appropriately for transformation-generated code.
Note
When the ROSE_DEBUG_NEW_EDG_ROSE_CONNECTION preprocessor macro is defined, this function outputs a deprecation warning message to assist developers in identifying usage of the old API.

◆ setOperand()

void SageInterface::setOperand ( SgExpression * target,
SgExpression * operand )

Sets the operand of a target expression node in the ROSE AST.

This function assigns a given operand expression to a target expression node within the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). The function handles various types of expression nodes that can contain operands, including unary operators, sizeof operations, typeid operations, variable argument operations, and initializers. The implementation uses a switch statement to dispatch to the appropriate setter method based on the variant type of the target expression. After setting the operand, the function updates the parent pointer of the operand to maintain AST consistency and marks left-hand side values as needed.

The supported target expression types include:

  • SgActualArgumentExpression
  • SgAsmOp
  • SgSizeOfOp
  • SgTypeIdOp
  • SgVarArgOp
  • SgVarArgStartOneOperandOp
  • SgAssignInitializer
  • Any SgUnaryOp derived class
Parameters
targetPointer to the target expression node whose operand will be set. Must not be NULL and must not be the same as the operand parameter.
operandPointer to the expression node to be set as the operand of the target. Must not be NULL and must not be the same as the target parameter.
Warning
This function may overwrite existing operands without warning. Any previously set operand will be replaced, and the caller is responsible for managing the memory of the old operand if necessary.
If the target expression type is not handled by this function, the program will abort with an error message.
Precondition
target is not NULL.
operand is not NULL.
target and operand are not the same object (target != operand).
target is one of the supported expression types or derives from SgUnaryOp.
Postcondition
The operand is set as the child of the target expression.
The parent pointer of operand is set to target.
Left-hand side values are marked appropriately via markLhsValues.
Note
This function modifies both the target and operand nodes to maintain proper parent-child relationships in the AST.
For unsupported target expression types that are not SgUnaryOp derivatives, the function will output an error message to stderr and call ROSE_ABORT().

◆ setParameterList()

template<class actualFunction>
void SageInterface::setParameterList ( actualFunction * func,
SgFunctionParameterList * paralist )

Sets the parameter list for a function declaration node in the ROSE AST.

This templated function assigns a given SgFunctionParameterList to a function declaration node. It is designed to work with both SgFunctionDeclaration and SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration types, as well as their associated member function derived classes. The function handles memory management by deleting any existing parameter list if it differs from the new one being assigned. It also establishes proper parent-child relationships in the AST and configures the declaration pointer for each initialized name in the parameter list.

For Ada language support, the function verifies that each parameter has an associated variable declaration, as Ada stores variable declarations in the function parameter scope. For other languages, the function sets the declaration pointer in each SgInitializedName IR node to support the AST Copy mechanism.

Parameters
funcPointer to the function declaration node that will receive the parameter list. This can be an SgFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, or their derived member function classes. Must not be NULL.
paralistPointer to the SgFunctionParameterList to be assigned to the function. Must not be NULL. Should ideally be an exclusive parameter list for this function declaration to avoid symbol table corruption.
Warning
Sharing parameter lists between multiple function declarations can corrupt symbol tables. Users should use deepCopy() to obtain an exclusive parameter list for each function declaration.
The SgFunctionDeclaration constructor automatically generates an SgFunctionParameterList, so care must be taken when setting a new parameter list to avoid memory leaks.
Precondition
func must not be NULL.
paralist must not be NULL.
For Ada language, each argument in the parameter list must have an associated SgVariableDeclaration accessible via get_declptr().
Postcondition
The function's parameter list is set to paralist.
The parent of paralist is set to func.
For non-Ada languages, each SgInitializedName in the parameter list has its declaration pointer set to func.
Any previously existing parameter list (if different from paralist) is deleted.
Note
This function does not create symbols for arguments of non-defining function declarations.
The implementation considers differences between C++ and Fortran language handling, though specific Fortran handling details may require further consideration.

If the declaration already has an associated pragma, the old pragma is deleted to prevent memory leaks before the new pragma is assigned. The function also establishes the proper parent-child relationship by setting the pragma's parent pointer to the declaration node.

◆ setRhsOperand()

void SageInterface::setRhsOperand ( SgExpression * target,
SgExpression * rhs )

Sets the right-hand side operand of a target expression node.

This function assigns a new right-hand side (RHS) operand to a given target expression in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). The function handles several specific expression types including SgVarArgCopyOp, SgVarArgStartOp, and general SgBinaryOp nodes. After setting the RHS operand, the function updates the parent pointer of the RHS expression to maintain proper AST structure. If both left-hand side and right-hand side operands are present after the assignment, the function also marks the left-hand side values appropriately using markLhsValues.

The function uses dynamic type checking via isSg* functions to determine the specific type of the target expression and calls the appropriate set_rhs_operand method for that type. If the target expression type is not one of the handled cases, the function outputs an error message and aborts execution.

Parameters
targetPointer to the target expression node whose RHS operand will be set. Must be a valid non-null pointer to an SgExpression that is either an SgVarArgCopyOp, SgVarArgStartOp, or SgBinaryOp. Must not be the same as the rhs parameter.
rhsPointer to the expression node to be set as the right-hand side operand. Must be a valid non-null pointer to an SgExpression. Must not be the same as the target parameter.
Warning
If the target expression type is not SgVarArgCopyOp, SgVarArgStartOp, or SgBinaryOp, the function will print an error message and call ROSE_ABORT to terminate execution.
Precondition
target is not null.
rhs is not null.
target and rhs are different objects (target != rhs).
target must be of type SgVarArgCopyOp, SgVarArgStartOp, or SgBinaryOp.
Postcondition
The RHS operand of target is set to rhs.
The parent pointer of rhs is set to target.
If both LHS and RHS operands exist, the LHS values are marked via markLhsValues.
Note
This function modifies both the target expression and the rhs expression by updating their internal pointers.
The function only marks lvalues when both operands are available, ensuring proper semantic analysis of assignment-like expressions.

◆ setSourcePosition()

void SageInterface::setSourcePosition ( SgNode * node)

Sets the source position information for a given AST node based on the current classification mode.

This function configures the source position information for an AST node according to the currently active SourcePositionClassification mode. The function retrieves the current classification mode and applies the appropriate source position handling strategy based on that mode. Different modes support different use cases such as default positioning, transformation marking, compiler-generated code classification, null pointer assignment, and frontend construction positioning.

The function handles the following classification modes:

  • e_sourcePositionError: Triggers an error and aborts execution.
  • e_sourcePositionDefault: Sets default source position for SgLocatedNode instances.
  • e_sourcePositionTransformation: Marks the node as a transformation.
  • e_sourcePositionCompilerGenerated: Not yet implemented, aborts execution.
  • e_sourcePositionNullPointers: Sets source position pointers to NULL.
  • e_sourcePositionFrontendConstruction: Sets default source position for frontend AST construction, supporting SgLocatedNode, SgPragma, SgType, and SgFunctionParameterTypeList nodes.
  • e_sourcePosition_last: Triggers an error and aborts execution.

During AST construction from the EDG frontend, the SourcePositionClassification will typically be e_sourcePositionFrontendConstruction. The source position information assigned during this phase is later reset using information from EDG.

Parameters
nodePointer to the SgNode for which source position information should be set. The node type determines which source position handling is applicable. For certain modes, the node must be an SgLocatedNode or specific derived types.
Warning
The e_sourcePositionCompilerGenerated mode is not implemented and will cause program termination if used.
Using e_sourcePositionError or e_sourcePosition_last modes will cause program termination via ROSE_ABORT.
In e_sourcePositionDefault mode, passing a non-SgLocatedNode will cause program termination.
In e_sourcePositionFrontendConstruction mode, passing unsupported node types (not SgLocatedNode, SgPragma, SgType, or SgFunctionParameterTypeList) will cause program termination.
Precondition
The node parameter must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgNode.
The source position classification mode must be properly initialized via the corresponding setter function before calling this function.
Postcondition
The node's source position information is configured according to the current classification mode, or the program has terminated due to an unsupported mode or node type combination.
Note
The setSourcePositionToDefault function is called frequently during AST construction, which may have performance implications.
For improved efficiency in frontend processing, the e_sourcePositionNullPointers mode is preferred to avoid building and rebuilding source position information unnecessarily.

◆ setSourcePositionAsTransformation()

void SageInterface::setSourcePositionAsTransformation ( SgNode * node)

Marks an IR node's source position information as being part of a transformation.

This function sets the source position information for a given AST node to indicate that it was generated as part of a transformation rather than originating from source code. The function handles different types of nodes appropriately: SgLocatedNode types receive both start and end of construct markers, SgExpression types additionally receive an operator position marker, and SgPragma nodes receive special handling for their source position. SgGlobal nodes are treated specially by not setting an end of construct marker since they should have NULL endOfConstruct.

The function uses Sg_File_Info::generateDefaultFileInfoForTransformationNode() to create the appropriate file information objects that mark the node as transformation-generated. Each created Sg_File_Info object has its parent pointer set to the corresponding node to maintain proper AST structure.

Parameters
nodePointer to the SgNode whose source position should be marked as a transformation. Must not be NULL. The node is dynamically cast to determine its specific type and appropriate source position handling.
Precondition
node must not be NULL.
The node should be a valid AST node that may require source position information.
Postcondition
If node is an SgLocatedNode, its startOfConstruct is set to transformation file info.
If node is an SgLocatedNode but not SgGlobal, its endOfConstruct is also set.
If node is an SgExpression, its operatorPosition is additionally set.
If node is an SgPragma with NULL startOfConstruct, its startOfConstruct is set.
All created Sg_File_Info objects have their parent pointers correctly set.
Note
This function was introduced to support specification of IR nodes being part of a transformation (as noted from 5/1/2012).
SgGlobal nodes are handled specially and do not receive an endOfConstruct marker.
SgPragma nodes are handled as a special case of non-located nodes that still require file info.
Warning
This function unconditionally overwrites existing source position information for SgLocatedNode types, which may not be the desired behavior if the node already has valid source position data.

◆ setSourcePositionAtRootAndAllChildren()

void SageInterface::setSourcePositionAtRootAndAllChildren ( SgNode * root)

Sets source position information for a node and all its descendants in the AST.

This function traverses the entire subtree rooted at the specified node and sets the source position information for each node encountered. It uses a query-based approach to collect all nodes in the subtree and then iterates through them, applying the setSourcePosition function to each node individually.

The implementation first queries the subtree using NodeQuery::querySubTree to obtain a container of all SgNode descendants (including the root itself). It then iterates through this collection and calls setSourcePosition on each node to establish proper source position attributes.

Parameters
rootPointer to the root SgNode from which the subtree traversal begins. All nodes in the subtree rooted at this node will have their source position information set.
Warning
This is a relatively expensive operation as it queries and processes all nodes in the subtree. Performance may be a concern for large AST subtrees.
Precondition
The root parameter should point to a valid SgNode in the AST.
Postcondition
All nodes in the subtree rooted at root will have their source position information set via the setSourcePosition function.
Note
This function is useful for ensuring consistent source position information across newly created or transformed AST subtrees where source location attributes need to be initialized or updated.
See also
setSourcePosition
NodeQuery::querySubTree

◆ setSourcePositionForTransformation()

void SageInterface::setSourcePositionForTransformation ( SgNode * root)

Sets the source position for a transformed AST subtree.

This function marks the source position information for a given AST node and all of its descendants as being part of a transformation. This is used to distinguish between original source code and code that has been generated or modified by ROSE transformations.

The implementation delegates to setSourcePositionAtRootAndAllChildren() to recursively process the entire subtree rooted at the given node. This function serves as a wrapper that provides a semantically meaningful name for the operation of marking transformation-generated code.

Note that this function name is considered deprecated in favor of the more descriptive setSourcePositionAtRootAndAllChildrenAsTransformation(), though both may be used. The function can be called during frontend processing, such as when OmpSupport::lower_omp() is invoked.

An alternative implementation exists (currently disabled via preprocessor conditionals) that uses NodeQuery::querySubTree() to collect all descendant nodes and then applies setOneSourcePositionForTransformation() to each node individually.

Parameters
rootPointer to the root SgNode of the subtree for which source position information should be marked as transformation-generated. This node and all of its descendants will be processed.
Warning
This function name is deprecated. Consider using setSourcePositionAtRootAndAllChildrenAsTransformation() instead for clearer semantics.
Precondition
The root parameter should point to a valid SgNode in the AST.
Postcondition
The source position information for root and all of its descendant nodes will be marked as transformation-generated.
Note
This function may be called during frontend processing by components such as OmpSupport::lower_omp(), not only during user-defined transformations.

◆ setSourcePositionPointersToNull()

void SageInterface::setSourcePositionPointersToNull ( SgNode * node)

Sets source position pointers to NULL for a given AST node.

This function sets the source position information pointers (Sg_File_Info objects) to NULL for various types of ROSE AST nodes. It handles different node types including SgLocatedNode, SgExpression, SgPragma, and SgGlobal, each of which may have different source position attributes that need to be nullified.

For SgLocatedNode instances, the function sets both startOfConstruct and endOfConstruct to NULL, except for SgGlobal nodes which should only have their startOfConstruct set to NULL (as SgGlobal nodes are expected to have NULL endOfConstruct by design). For SgExpression nodes, an additional operatorPosition pointer is also set to NULL. For SgPragma nodes that are not SgLocatedNode instances, only the startOfConstruct is set to NULL.

The function prints warning messages to stdout when it detects that existing Sg_File_Info objects are being overwritten, indicating potential memory leaks since the existing objects are not deleted before setting the pointers to NULL.

Parameters
nodePointer to the SgNode whose source position pointers should be set to NULL. Must not be NULL.
Warning
This function may cause memory leaks. When source position pointers are not already NULL, the existing Sg_File_Info objects are not deleted before setting the pointers to NULL. Warning messages are printed to stdout when this occurs.
For SgGlobal nodes, only startOfConstruct is set to NULL; endOfConstruct is intentionally left unchanged as it is expected to already be NULL.
Precondition
node must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If node is an SgLocatedNode, its startOfConstruct pointer will be NULL.
If node is an SgLocatedNode but not an SgGlobal, its endOfConstruct pointer will be NULL.
If node is an SgExpression, its operatorPosition pointer will be NULL.
If node is an SgPragma (not an SgLocatedNode), its startOfConstruct pointer will be NULL.
Note
This function uses ROSE dynamic type checking functions (isSgLocatedNode, isSgExpression, isSgPragma, isSgGlobal) to determine the node type.
Consider using setSourcePositionToNULL as a more descriptive name for this function, though such a rename would require additional logic changes to properly handle memory management of existing Sg_File_Info objects.

Determines whether a preprocessing info directive should be skipped during C++ declaration translation.

This function examines the type of a given preprocessing information directive and determines if it should be excluded from translation to C++ declarations. Certain directive types such as comments (C-style, C++-style, and Fortran-style), blank preprocessor lines, and C linkage specification markers are considered non-translatable and should be skipped during the translation process.

◆ splitExpression()

SgAssignInitializer * SageInterface::splitExpression ( SgExpression * from,
string newName = "" )

Splits an expression by extracting it into a temporary variable declaration.

This function extracts a given expression from its current location in the AST and replaces it with a reference to a newly created temporary variable. The original expression becomes the initializer of the new variable declaration, which is inserted before the statement containing the expression.

The function handles complex cases involving short-circuit evaluation operators (logical AND, logical OR) and conditional expressions. When the expression to be split has ancestors that are short-circuit operators or conditional expressions, the function first transforms those ancestors using replaceExpressionWithStatement before proceeding with the split. This ensures correct evaluation semantics are preserved.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Locate the statement containing the expression
  2. Ensure the statement has a proper basic block parent if needed
  3. Identify any ancestor expressions that require special handling (AND, OR, conditional)
  4. Transform ancestors from outermost to innermost using appropriate generators
  5. Create a new variable declaration with a generated or user-specified name
  6. Replace the original expression with a variable reference
  7. Set the original expression as the initializer of the new variable
  8. Insert the variable declaration before the original statement
Parameters
fromThe expression to be split and extracted into a temporary variable. Must not be NULL.
newNameOptional name for the temporary variable. If empty, a unique name will be generated using the pattern "rose_temp__N" where N is an incrementing counter.
Returns
The SgAssignInitializer node containing the original expression as the initializer of the newly created variable declaration. Returns NULL if ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is defined.
Warning
This function modifies the AST in place. The original expression is removed from its original location and reattached as an initializer.
The function assumes the expression's type is copy constructible. While the explicit check is currently disabled due to issues with template class specializations, non-copy-constructible types may cause compilation errors in the generated code.
Precondition
The parameter from must not be NULL.
The expression must be contained within a valid statement.
The statement must have a valid scope statement as an ancestor.
Postcondition
A new variable declaration is inserted before the statement containing the original expression.
The original expression is replaced with a variable reference in the AST.
The original expression becomes the initializer of the new variable.
Note
This function was merged from replaceExpressionWithStatement.C.
When ancestors requiring special handling exist, the function recursively calls itself after transforming those ancestors.
The function uses SageInterface::gensym_counter for generating unique variable names.
Special handling is provided for expressions within for-loop initialization statements (SgForInitStatement).

◆ splitExpressionIntoBasicBlock()

void SageInterface::splitExpressionIntoBasicBlock ( SgExpression * expr)

Splits an expression into a basic block structure for loop tests and similar constructs.

This function generalizes the normal splitExpression functionality to accommodate loop tests and other control flow constructs that require expression decomposition. It creates a nested StatementGenerator structure that wraps the given expression into a basic block containing an assignment statement. The function then delegates to replaceExpressionWithStatement to perform the actual transformation.

The implementation defines a local SplitStatementGenerator class that inherits from StatementGenerator. This generator captures the original expression and, when invoked, produces a basic block containing an assignment statement that assigns the original expression to the provided answer variable. This pattern allows for controlled expression evaluation within a block scope.

Parameters
exprPointer to the SgExpression node that should be split into a basic block. This expression will be wrapped in an assignment statement within a newly created basic block structure.
Warning
The input expression pointer should be valid and part of an existing AST. Passing a null or invalid pointer may result in undefined behavior.
Precondition
The expr parameter must point to a valid SgExpression node that is part of a well-formed SAGE III abstract syntax tree.
The expression must be in a context where it can be legally replaced with a statement or basic block.
Postcondition
The original expression has been replaced in the AST with a basic block containing an assignment statement that evaluates the expression.
The AST remains in a consistent and valid state after the transformation.
Note
This function uses SageBuilder utilities internally to construct the new AST nodes (buildBasicBlock and buildAssignStatement).
This is particularly useful for transforming complex expressions in loop conditions or other contexts where expressions need to be evaluated in a controlled block scope.

The scope parameter must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgScopeStatement.
The AST containing the scope must be well-formed and properly constructed.

All top-level variable declarations with initializers in the scope have been split into separate declaration and assignment statements (when topLevelOnly is true).

◆ splitVariableDeclaration() [2/2]

SgExprStatement * SageInterface::splitVariableDeclaration ( SgVariableDeclaration * decl)

Splits a variable declaration with an initializer into a separate declaration and assignment statement.

This function takes a variable declaration that contains an initializer and separates it into two parts: the declaration without initialization and a subsequent assignment statement. This transformation is useful for code normalization, simplifying analysis, or preparing code for certain transformations that require declarations and assignments to be separate statements.

The function handles various types of initializers including assign initializers and aggregate initializers. When an assign initializer is present, the operand is extracted; otherwise, the initializer itself is used as the right-hand side of the generated assignment. The right-hand side expression is deep copied to ensure independence from the original initializer. After creating the assignment statement, the original declaration's initializer pointer is set to NULL, effectively removing the initialization from the declaration. The newly created assignment statement is automatically inserted immediately after the original declaration in the AST.

Parameters
declPointer to the variable declaration to be split. Must not be NULL. The declaration should contain at least one initialized name, and the function operates on the first initialized name in the declaration.
Returns
Pointer to the newly created assignment statement if the declaration had an initializer, or NULL if the declaration had no initializer to split off.
Precondition
decl must not be NULL.
decl must be a valid SgVariableDeclaration node in the AST.
decl should contain at least one initialized name accessible via getFirstInitializedName.
Postcondition
If the declaration had an initializer, the initializer pointer of the first initialized name is set to NULL.
If an assignment statement was created, it is inserted into the AST immediately after the original declaration.
The original initializer object is not cleaned up and may need manual deallocation.
Note
The function only processes the first initialized name in the declaration. Declarations with multiple variables may not be fully handled.
The original initializer object is not deleted; there is a TODO in the implementation to clean up the initializer, which may lead to memory leaks if not addressed externally.
The right-hand side expression is deep copied, so modifications to the returned assignment statement will not affect the original initializer.
Warning
The original initializer is orphaned but not deallocated, which may cause memory leaks.

◆ statementCanBeTransformed()

bool SageInterface::statementCanBeTransformed ( SgStatement * stmt)

Determines whether a given statement can be safely transformed.

This function checks if a statement can be transformed while maintaining compatibility with token-based unparsing and header file unparsing options. It examines the source file context of the statement and consults the EDG-ROSE translation include file map to determine if transformations are supported.

The function performs the following steps:

  1. Retrieves the enclosing source file for the given statement.
  2. If the source file uses token-based unparsing and header file unparsing, it looks up the statement's source filename in the EDG include file map.
  3. If found in the map, it checks whether the include file supports token-based unparsing for transformations.
  4. Returns false if the include file cannot support token-based unparsing, otherwise returns true.

For statements not found in the include file map (typically the original input source file rather than a header file), the function defaults to returning true, allowing transformations.

Parameters
stmtPointer to the SgStatement object to be checked for transformation eligibility. Must not be NULL and must be associated with a valid source file.
Returns
True if the statement can be transformed, false if transformations cannot be supported due to token-based unparsing limitations with header file unparsing.
Precondition
The statement must be part of a valid AST with an enclosing source file.
The stmt parameter must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The AST and statement remain unchanged; this is a query operation only.
Note
This function uses EDG_ROSE_Translation::edg_include_file_map which is constructed during EDG/ROSE translation to track include file information.
If the source file does not have both unparse_tokens and unparseHeaderFiles options enabled, the function returns true without additional checks.
Warning
The function will trigger a ROSE_ASSERT failure if the enclosing source file cannot be found for the given statement.

◆ suggestNextNumericLabel()

int SageInterface::suggestNextNumericLabel ( SgFunctionDefinition * func_def)

Suggests the next usable non-conflicting numeric label value for a Fortran function definition scope.

This function analyzes the symbol table of a given Fortran function definition to determine the next available numeric label value that does not conflict with existing labels. The algorithm iterates through all symbols in the function's symbol table, identifies label symbols, and finds the maximum numeric label value currently in use. The suggested next label is computed by adding 10 to the maximum found value, ensuring a gap between consecutive labels. If no labels exist, the function returns a default starting value of 10.

The function enforces Fortran 77 label constraints, where numeric labels must be at most 5 digits (maximum value of 99999).

Parameters
func_defPointer to the SgFunctionDefinition representing the Fortran function scope for which the next numeric label is to be suggested. Must not be NULL.
Returns
The suggested next numeric label value, which is guaranteed to be non-conflicting with existing labels in the function scope. Returns a value that is 10 greater than the current maximum label value, or 10 if no labels exist.
Warning
The function will trigger an assertion failure if the computed result exceeds 99999, which is the maximum allowed label value for Fortran 77.
Precondition
The func_def parameter must not be NULL.
The current source language must be Fortran (verified via SageInterface::is_Fortran_language()).
The function definition must have a valid symbol table.
Postcondition
The returned value is greater than or equal to 10.
The returned value does not conflict with any existing numeric label in the function scope.
The returned value is less than or equal to 99999.
Note
This function is specific to Fortran language constructs and should only be called when processing Fortran source code.
The label increment of 10 provides spacing for potential manual insertion of intermediate labels if needed.

◆ templateArgumentEquivalence()

bool SageInterface::templateArgumentEquivalence ( SgTemplateArgument * arg1,
SgTemplateArgument * arg2 )

Determines whether two template arguments are semantically equivalent.

This function compares two SgTemplateArgument objects to determine if they represent equivalent template arguments. The comparison is performed based on the argument type (type argument, non-type argument, or template template argument) and uses appropriate equivalence checks for each category.

For type arguments, the function first checks pointer equality, then falls back to semantic type equivalence using isEquivalentType() when pointers differ. For non-type arguments, the function compares the underlying expressions, supporting specific value types such as SgLongIntVal and SgUnsignedLongVal. For template template arguments, the function compares the template declarations directly. Pack expansion arguments are considered equivalent if both arguments are of the same pack expansion type.

The function includes extensive debug output controlled by the DEBUG_TEMPLATE_ARG_EQUIVALENCE preprocessor macro.

Parameters
arg1Pointer to the first template argument to compare. Must not be NULL.
arg2Pointer to the second template argument to compare. Must not be NULL.
Returns
True if the two template arguments are considered equivalent, false otherwise.
Precondition
arg1 must be a valid non-NULL pointer to an SgTemplateArgument object.
arg2 must be a valid non-NULL pointer to an SgTemplateArgument object.
For type arguments, both arg1->get_type() and arg2->get_type() must be non-NULL.
Postcondition
The input arguments remain unchanged.
Warning
The function will abort (ROSE_ABORT) if template template arguments have different template declarations, as this comparison is not yet implemented.
The function will abort if arguments of undefined type are compared.
For non-type arguments, only SgLongIntVal and SgUnsignedLongVal expression types are currently supported. Other expression types will cause an abort.
Comparing arguments with unhandled argument types will result in program abort.
Note
This function supports pointer equality as a fast path for all argument types.
Type equivalence for type arguments uses the isEquivalentType() function when direct pointer comparison fails.
Support for SgUnsignedLongVal was added to handle processing of nlohmann/json.hpp.

◆ templateArgumentListEquivalence()

bool SageInterface::templateArgumentListEquivalence ( const SgTemplateArgumentPtrList & list1,
const SgTemplateArgumentPtrList & list2 )

Determines whether two template argument lists are equivalent.

This function compares two lists of template arguments to determine if they are semantically equivalent. The comparison is performed in multiple stages for efficiency. First, it checks if the lists have the same size. If sizes differ, the lists cannot be equivalent. Second, it performs a quick STL equality check to see if the lists are identical. Finally, if the quick check fails, it iterates through each corresponding pair of template arguments and uses the templateArgumentEquivalence function to compare them individually. The lists are considered equivalent only if all corresponding template arguments are equivalent.

Debug output can be enabled by defining the DEBUG_TEMPLATE_ARG_LIST_EQUIVALENCE preprocessor macro, which will print diagnostic information about the comparison process to standard output.

Parameters
list1The first template argument list to compare. This is a constant reference to an SgTemplateArgumentPtrList containing pointers to template argument nodes.
list2The second template argument list to compare. This is a constant reference to an SgTemplateArgumentPtrList containing pointers to template argument nodes.
Returns
True if both template argument lists are equivalent, meaning they have the same size and all corresponding template arguments are equivalent according to templateArgumentEquivalence. Returns false otherwise.
Precondition
Both list1 and list2 must contain valid pointers to SgTemplateArgument objects, or be empty lists.
Postcondition
The input lists remain unchanged after the comparison.
Note
This function relies on templateArgumentEquivalence to perform the element-wise comparison of individual template arguments.
The STL equality operator check provides a fast path for cases where the lists contain identical pointer values.

◆ templateDefinitionIsInClass()

bool SageInterface::templateDefinitionIsInClass ( SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl * memberFunctionDeclaration)

Determines if a template member function definition is located inside its class definition.

This function checks whether the template declaration associated with a given member function instantiation is defined within the class body or outside of it. The determination is made by examining the parent scope of the template declaration. If the parent scope is a class definition (SgClassDefinition), then the template definition is considered to be inside the class.

The implementation retrieves the template declaration from the member function instantiation and checks if its parent node is an SgClassDefinition. This approach provides a straightforward way to distinguish between in-class template definitions and out-of-class template definitions.

Parameters
memberFunctionDeclarationPointer to the template instantiation member function declaration to be analyzed. This represents an instantiated member function from a class template.
Returns
True if the template definition associated with the member function is defined inside the class definition, false if it is defined outside the class or if the template declaration or its parent is NULL.
Precondition
The memberFunctionDeclaration parameter should be a valid pointer to an SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl node in the AST.
Postcondition
The AST remains unchanged after this function call.
Note
This function only examines the immediate parent scope of the template declaration. It does not perform deep traversal of the AST hierarchy.
The function contains commented-out alternative implementation code that uses a different approach involving class template instantiation checking, which may be useful for reference or future modifications.

◆ translateScopeToUseCppDeclarations()

void SageInterface::translateScopeToUseCppDeclarations ( SgScopeStatement * scope)

Translates C preprocessor directives attached to statements within a scope into explicit C++ declaration IR nodes.

This function processes all statements within a given scope and converts attached C preprocessor directives (such as include, define, ifdef, etc.) from preprocessing information annotations into explicit IR nodes in the AST. The function handles two categories of scopes differently: scopes that contain only declarations (such as global scope, namespace definitions, and class definitions) and scopes that can contain non-declaration statements (such as SgBasicBlock).

The algorithm works in multiple phases:

  1. First, it iterates through all statements or declarations in the scope and calls translateStatementToUseCppDeclarations for each one to identify directives that need to be converted.
  2. The resulting directives are stored in a map to avoid iterator invalidation during the insertion phase.
  3. In the second phase, the function iterates over the collected directive map and inserts each directive IR node into the scope before its associated statement.
  4. Finally, it removes the original preprocessing info entries that were converted to IR nodes, while preserving comments and other directive types that should not be translated.
Parameters
scopePointer to the scope statement whose contained statements should be processed for C preprocessor directive translation. Must not be NULL.
Warning
This function modifies the AST by inserting new IR nodes and removing attached preprocessing information. The original preprocessing info for translated directives will be deleted.
Debug printf statements are present throughout this function and will produce console output during execution.
Precondition
The scope parameter must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgScopeStatement.
The AST containing the scope must be in a consistent state.
Postcondition
All translatable C preprocessor directives attached to statements within the scope will be converted to explicit IR nodes inserted before their respective statements.
The original preprocessing info entries for translated directives will be removed from their associated statements.
Comments and non-translatable directives will remain as attached preprocessing information.
Note
The function uses skipTranslateToUseCppDeclaration to determine which preprocessing info entries should not be converted to IR nodes.
A map is used to collect directives before insertion to prevent iterator invalidation when modifying the statement lists.

Translates preprocessor directives attached to a statement into C preprocessor directive IR nodes.

This function extracts preprocessor directives that are attached to a given statement and converts them into SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement IR nodes. The function iterates through all attached preprocessing information associated with the statement and creates corresponding directive objects for each eligible directive. Some directive types are intentionally skipped as they would require additional IR node types to be added to the system. The function uses the skipTranslateToUseCppDeclaration helper function to determine which directives should be excluded from translation.

Parameters
statementThe statement from which attached preprocessor directives will be extracted and translated. This statement should have preprocessing information attached to it. If the statement has no attached preprocessing info, an empty vector is returned.
Returns
A vector containing pointers to newly created SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement objects, one for each eligible preprocessor directive that was attached to the input statement. Returns an empty vector if the statement has no attached preprocessing information or if all attached directives are skipped.
Note
The second parameter of type SgScopeStatement* is currently unused in the implementation.
Debug output is printed to stdout showing the size of the directive list after each iteration through the attached preprocessing information.
Certain types of preprocessor directives are intentionally not processed into IR nodes. These would require new IR node types to be added and can be implemented later if needed.
Precondition
The statement parameter should be a valid pointer to an SgStatement object.
Postcondition
The returned vector contains newly allocated SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement objects that the caller is responsible for managing.

◆ translateToUseCppDeclarations()

void SageInterface::translateToUseCppDeclarations ( SgNode * n)

Translates an AST subtree to use C++ style declarations.

This function performs a postorder traversal of the given AST subtree to translate declarations to use C++ style syntax. The implementation defines an internal traversal class (CppTranslationTraversal) that inherits from AstSimpleProcessing. During the traversal, each node is visited and checked to determine if it is a scope statement. Currently, only global scope (SgGlobal) nodes are processed by calling translateScopeToUseCppDeclarations on them. All other scope types are skipped with a diagnostic message.

The traversal is performed in postorder, which is appropriate since the function transforms the AST at each scope level. Processing children before parents ensures that nested transformations are completed before the parent scope is modified.

Parameters
nPointer to the root SgNode of the AST subtree to be traversed and translated. This node and all its descendants will be visited during the traversal.
Warning
Currently, this function only processes global scope nodes. All other scope types (such as function scopes, class scopes, etc.) are explicitly skipped and will not be translated.
Note
The function outputs diagnostic printf messages during execution to trace the traversal progress and indicate which nodes are being processed or skipped.
The implementation includes a commented-out preorder traversal option, but postorder traversal is used to ensure proper handling of AST transformations.
Precondition
The parameter n must be a valid pointer to an SgNode within a properly constructed ROSE AST.
Postcondition
All global scope nodes within the subtree rooted at n will have been processed by translateScopeToUseCppDeclarations to convert their declarations to C++ style.

◆ UnderlyingType()

SgType * SageInterface::UnderlyingType ( SgType * type)

Retrieves the underlying type of an enumeration type.

This function is intended to return the underlying integral type of an enumeration type, which is a feature introduced in C++11. The underlying type of an enum determines the storage and value range of the enumeration. In C++11 and later, enumerations can have explicitly specified underlying types (e.g., enum class Color : unsigned int).

Currently, this function is not yet implemented (NYI) and will trigger an assertion failure if called. The function exists as a placeholder for future implementation of C++11 enum underlying type support.

Parameters
typeA pointer to an SgType object representing an enumeration type. The type must be a valid enum type as verified by IsEnum().
Returns
A pointer to the SgType representing the underlying type of the enumeration. Currently always returns NULL due to incomplete implementation.
Warning
This function is not yet implemented. Calling this function will result in an assertion failure at runtime.
This function always returns NULL in its current state and should not be used in production code.
Precondition
The parameter type must not be NULL.
The parameter type must represent an enumeration type (IsEnum(type) must return true).
Postcondition
In the current implementation, an assertion failure occurs before any meaningful result can be returned.
Note
This is a C++11 feature that requires full implementation to support strongly-typed enumerations and their underlying types.
The ROSE_ASSERT macro is used to enforce preconditions and to indicate that this feature is not yet implemented.

◆ unnormalizeForLoopInitDeclaration()

bool SageInterface::unnormalizeForLoopInitDeclaration ( SgForStatement * loop)

Reverses the normalization of a for-loop initialization declaration.

This function undoes a previous normalization transformation applied to a for-loop's initialization statement. During normalization, a variable declaration in the loop initialization (e.g., "for(int i=0; ...)") is typically moved outside the loop and replaced with an assignment expression. This function restores the original declaration back into the loop's initialization statement.

The algorithm performs the following steps:

  1. Checks if the loop was previously normalized using the transformation records table
  2. Retrieves the original and normalized declarations from the transformation records
  3. Removes the normalized declaration and the assignment expression statement
  4. Restores the original declaration to the loop's initialization statement list
  5. Updates all variable references within the loop to use the original symbol
  6. Clears the normalization record for this loop
Parameters
loopPointer to the SgForStatement representing the for-loop to be unnormalized. Must not be NULL.
Returns
True if the unnormalization was successfully performed, false if the loop was not previously normalized and no action was taken.
Precondition
The loop parameter must not be NULL.
If the loop was previously normalized, the transformation records must contain valid entries for both the original and normalized declarations.
The loop's initialization statement list must contain exactly one statement if the loop was previously normalized.
Postcondition
If successful, the loop's initialization statement contains the original variable declaration.
All variable references within the loop that referred to the normalized symbol now refer to the original symbol.
The transformation record for this loop is cleared (marked as not normalized).
The normalized declaration and assignment statement are removed from the AST.
Note
This function relies on the global trans_records structure to track normalization state and store the original and normalized declarations.
Only loops with a single initialization statement are handled.
Warning
This function assumes the loop was normalized using the corresponding normalization function and that the transformation records are intact. Calling this on a loop with corrupted or missing records may cause assertion failures.

◆ updateDefiningNondefiningLinks()

void SageInterface::updateDefiningNondefiningLinks ( SgFunctionDeclaration * func,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Updates the linking between defining and non-defining function declarations within a scope.

This function maintains the consistency of links between defining and non-defining declarations of the same function within a given scope. In C++, a function may have multiple declarations (forward declarations) and one definition. This function ensures that all declarations of the same function are properly linked together by updating the definingDeclaration and firstNondefiningDeclaration pointers.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. Collects all statements from the given scope, handling both declaration-only scopes and general scopes differently.
  2. Identifies all function declarations in the scope that match the given function using the isSameFunction comparison.
  3. If the input function is itself a defining declaration, sets the definingDeclaration link for all matching declarations to point to it.
  4. If the input function is a non-defining declaration, updates the firstNondefiningDeclaration links appropriately, either propagating from the first non-defining declaration or inheriting from an existing declaration in the list.

Note that this function has been identified as a performance bottleneck, particularly due to the isSameFunction calls, which can consume significant execution time when processing large files.

Parameters
funcPointer to the function declaration whose links need to be updated. Must not be NULL. This can be either a defining or non-defining declaration.
scopePointer to the scope statement containing the function declarations to search. Must not be NULL. The scope is searched for all declarations of the same function.
Warning
This function has been identified as expensive in terms of performance, taking approximately 22.5 percent of total processing time in some test cases. The isSameFunction comparison is the primary contributor to this overhead.
A warning message is printed if the function symbol for the firstNondefiningDeclaration cannot be found in its associated scope, which may indicate an inconsistent AST state.
Precondition
func must not be NULL.
scope must not be NULL.
func->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration()->get_scope() must not be NULL.
The list of matching function declarations (sameFuncList) must not be empty when processing non-defining declarations.
Postcondition
All function declarations in scope that match func will have their definingDeclaration pointer updated if func is a defining declaration.
The firstNondefiningDeclaration links will be properly set for non-defining declarations, but only if they were previously NULL.
Note
The function only sets firstNondefiningDeclaration if it is not already set, to avoid overwriting existing valid links.
The function avoids setting a declaration to be its own firstNondefiningDeclaration.
Scope handling differs based on whether the scope contains only declarations or includes other statement types.

◆ whereAmI()

void SageInterface::whereAmI ( SgNode * node)

Prints diagnostic information about the location of a node in the AST hierarchy.

This function provides diagnostic support for debugging by traversing up the AST from a given node and printing information about each ancestor node. It is useful for detecting where in the AST hierarchy a failure or issue occurs. The function walks up the parent chain starting from the given node, printing the class name and file information for each parent node encountered until it reaches the file list level.

The function enforces that certain high-level IR nodes (SgFile, SgFileList, SgProject) are not accepted as input, as the highest acceptable node level is SgGlobal (global scope). For each parent node visited, the function displays the node pointer, class name, and detailed file information using the display method of the file info object.

Parameters
nodePointer to the SgNode from which to begin the upward traversal. Must not be NULL. Must not be an SgFile, SgFileList, or SgProject node.
Warning
This function produces console output via printf. It should only be called when diagnostic output is actually needed for debugging purposes.
The function will trigger an assertion failure if the input node is NULL or if it is an SgFile, SgFileList, or SgProject node.
Precondition
node must not be NULL.
node must not be of type SgFile, SgFileList, or SgProject.
Each parent node in the traversal chain must have valid file information (get_file_info() must not return NULL).
Postcondition
Diagnostic information about the node's ancestry has been printed to stdout.
Note
This function was added as part of refactoring diagnostic support in February 2012.
The traversal stops when it reaches the SgFileList level, preventing traversal past the SgFile level of the AST.

◆ wrapAllTemplateInstantiationsInAssociatedNamespaces()

void SageInterface::wrapAllTemplateInstantiationsInAssociatedNamespaces ( SgProject * root)

Wraps all template instantiations by moving them to their associated namespaces.

This function traverses the entire AST rooted at the given SgProject and identifies all template instantiation nodes. It collects these instantiations into a vector first to avoid iterator invalidation issues that would occur if transformations were performed during traversal. After collection, each template instantiation declaration is moved to its associated namespace using the moveDeclarationToAssociatedNamespace function.

The function uses RoseAst for AST traversal and the isTemplateInstantiationNode helper to identify template instantiation nodes. Only nodes that can be cast to SgDeclarationStatement are processed for the namespace wrapping transformation.

This function is primarily called from the tests/nonsmoke/functional/testTemplates translator for testing purposes.

Parameters
rootPointer to the SgProject representing the root of the AST to be processed. This should be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SgProject.
Warning
This feature is only available when building with autotools. When building with CMake (USE_CMAKE defined), the function will output an error message and abort execution via ROSE_ABORT().
The function performs AST transformations which modify the structure of the syntax tree. Ensure that no other operations are concurrently accessing or modifying the AST.
Precondition
The root parameter must point to a valid SgProject that has been properly constructed and initialized.
The AST must be in a consistent state before calling this function.
Postcondition
All template instantiation declarations found in the AST will have been moved to their associated namespaces.
The AST structure will be modified to reflect the namespace wrapping of template instantiations.
Note
The function collects all template instantiations into a vector before performing any transformations to prevent iterator invalidation errors that would occur if the AST were modified during traversal.
Not all template instantiation nodes are necessarily SgDeclarationStatement instances; non-declaration nodes are silently skipped.

This function provides a convenient overload for wrapping a function declaration by automatically generating the wrapper function name from the original function's name.
